# 810 qubits, 1,143,395,453 executed Toffoli

|  | qubits | avg executed Toffoli |
|---|---|---|
| previous best at this width | 810 | 1,143,704,043 |
| **this submission** | **810** | **1,143,395,453** |

Peak width is unchanged at 810. No knob, schedule, certificate, or arithmetic was modified.
The entire change is a gate-level cancellation pass applied to the emitted operation stream
after the builder returns it.

## Goal and baseline

The objective was a Pareto improvement at fixed width rather than a score improvement: at
810 qubits, lower the executed Toffoli count below the standing figure without touching the
construction. We reproduced the baseline before changing anything — the unmodified tree
builds and the trusted evaluator reports 9,024/9,024 with the recorded Toffoli count. A
measurement against a stale or misconfigured baseline is worthless, so that check gated
everything below.

## Approach selection

Two families were considered: changing the construction (schedule constants, window widths,
the arithmetic itself), and rewriting the emitted stream without changing what it computes.
We chose the second deliberately. Construction changes on this lane trade correctness margin
for gates and have to be re-argued from the certificate each time; a stream rewrite that only
removes provably cancelling pairs cannot change the computed unitary at all, so its risk is
confined to whether the cancellation rule is sound. That made it cheap to validate and cheap
to reason about.

## The change

Two passes run in sequence over the operation vector.

The first cancels **adjacent identical CCX pairs**: `CCX·CCX = I`. This is a single linear
scan with a write cursor; when the op about to be written equals the one already at the
cursor, both are dropped.

The second generalises it to pairs separated by intervening operations, cancelling identical
CCX pairs whenever every operation between them **provably commutes** with the CCX. For a
gate `CCX(a, b, t)`, an intervening operation `o` commutes when all of the following hold:

* `o` does not write either control `a` or `b` — writing a control would change what the CCX
  computes;
* `o` does not read the target `t` — it would observe a different value;
* `o` may write `t` only if it is XOR-type (`X`, `CX`, `CCX`), since XORs on a shared target
  commute with one another.

Condition-stack operations (`PushCondition`, `PopCondition`) are treated as hard barriers,
because they change which shots execute. `Swap`, `R` and `Hmr` are never commuted past except
when disjoint from all three qubits: `Swap` writes both operands and the other two are
non-unitary. Register/annotation/debug operations touch no qubits and are skipped. Both
members of a candidate pair must additionally agree on their condition bit and classical
target, so a gate that fires on a different set of shots is never cancelled against one that
does not.

The search is bounded by a window: for each CCX we scan forward at most `W` operations,
stopping at the first non-commuting operation. Cancellation marks both members dead and a
single compaction pass rebuilds the vector.

## Measurements

On this stream the adjacent pass removed **22,088** operations and the commuting pass a
further **286,502**, for **308,590** in total. That is exactly the Toffoli delta:
1,143,704,043 − 308,590 = 1,143,395,453. The accounting is exact because every removed operation is
a charged CCX.

The window was swept on a related stream: adjacent only 22,088; window 32 → 156,708; window
128 → 244,316; window 512 → 286,502; window 2048 → 286,502. The count saturates at 512 and
widening further finds nothing, so 512 is the shipped value.

## Failures and course corrections

Two things cost time and are worth passing on.

**The pass appears to do nothing under count-only builds.** The count-only path tallies
operations during emission and returns an empty operation vector, so a post-emission rewrite
sees nothing and the reported total is unchanged. We initially read that as the pass being
ineffective. It has to be measured on the real emit path.

**Normalising control order found nothing.** `CCX(a,b,t)` and `CCX(b,a,t)` are the same gate,
and `CCZ` is symmetric in all three qubits, so a field-by-field comparison could in principle
miss pairs. We implemented order normalisation for both and re-measured: the counts were
identical to the digit. This generator already emits controls in canonical order. The
normalisation is harmless and was kept, but it buys nothing here, and we record it so nobody
else spends time on it.

## Verification

Confirmed with the untouched `./benchmark.sh` on a clean checkout with the pass applied:
9,024/9,024 shots, 0 classical mismatches, 0 phase-garbage batches, 0 ancilla-garbage
batches, `qubits: 810`, avg executed Toffoli 1,143,395,453. No harness file was modified —
`benchmark.sh`, `src/bin/eval_circuit.rs`, `src/circuit.rs`, `src/sim.rs`, `Cargo.toml` and
`rust-toolchain` are as shipped.

Worth stating explicitly, because it is what made this measurable at all: removing operations
re-hashes the operation stream and therefore re-rolls the whole Fiat–Shamir draw. The
evaluator run above is on a completely fresh set of 9,024 test points, not the one the
baseline was validated against. It passes.

## Caveats

This is a local rewrite and it is close to exhausted. The saturation at window 512 says the
stream carries very few remaining cancelling pairs under this rule; a wider window will not
help, and the remaining structure is not reachable by pairwise cancellation. Anyone hoping to
move this width substantially should not expect it from peephole passes.

The rule is deliberately conservative. A more aggressive commutation analysis — phase-aware
treatment of `CZ`/`CCZ`, or reordering rather than only cancelling — might find more, at the
cost of a much harder soundness argument. We did not attempt it.

Note also that this pass is only useful on constructions that are exact for every draw. On a
value-dependent construction the same edit re-rolls the draw and the circuit then needs a
freshly ground tail nonce; we measured exactly that on another artifact, where removing
406,478 operations turned a passing build into 10 classical mismatches.

## Credit

Builds on the existing 810-qubit construction and the fixed-schedule EEA lineage it derives
from. Nothing in that construction was changed.

terminal parity encoding, and terminal Work2 affine repairs. An automated
coding and verification workflow assisted implementation; source assertions,
independent arithmetic oracles, and unchanged evaluator results determine the
evidence level, not the workflow's own success messages.

## A fixed low-bit frame for the remainder update

Inside the remainder-update scan, the source's virtual activation is recovered
from a shift bit and fixed step parity. Reconstructing that expression for
every controlled primitive expands many predicates repeatedly.

The new representation holds the physical low shift bit as

    C = entry_low0 XOR step_parity.

Static source X gates on that bit are recorded in a logical decoder mask rather
than physically emitted. At any source boundary, the original logical bit is

    logical_low0 = C XOR step_parity XOR decoder_mask0.

The virtual activation can therefore use physical C directly. This is not a
global change of the register's interpretation: every literal consumer of the
old low bit is conjugated into its logical frame, and the entire virtual-high
helper is similarly conjugated when necessary. That helper may borrow the bit
temporarily, but restores it before returning. At the scan's exit the masks
must be zero, and the original physical representation is restored before the
affine inverse and before any later arithmetic block.

Aliasing matters. If a predicate contains both C and logical_low0, their product
is C when the frame offset is zero and identically zero when it is one. The
emitter handles that case explicitly instead of treating the same wire as two
independent controls. Every remaining activation monomial contains C, so the
dirty-lender filter cannot borrow that live control. Dynamic source writes to
the original low bit are rejected; only the tracked static X case is supported.

## Reversible quotient capture in coefficient[0]

The next saving uses a different existing metadata wire. Let A denote the
original coefficient low bit, M the stable mode bit, L1 the current physical
second shift bit, m1 its static X mask, and z the omitted quotient-bit X mask.
The inherited quotient predicate is

    q = A XOR 1 XOR z XOR M*(L1 XOR kappa XOR m1),
    kappa = (((step - 2) // 2) AND 1) XOR 1.

All source targets on L1 are static X gates, so L1 XOR m1 stays equal to its
scan-entry value. Before the scan, toggle A by the target-independent function

    1 XOR M*(entry_L1 XOR kappa).

The physical wire then holds Q, the desired quotient expression with z=0.
Mirror each omitted source quotient X onto Q in exactly the original order.
Thereafter every virtual quotient consumer can use Q as one physical control
instead of expanding the polynomial again. Entry and exit together cost two
CCX plus Clifford gates and require no clean value of A or its predicate inputs.

This recoding is an XOR involution, not an assignment that discards A. The
emitter rejects any literal source consumer of original A in the entire scan,
any Mode target, any dynamic L1 target, or admission of A or Mode to the dirty
lender pool. The existing omitted-quotient static-X assertion remains. The
high-control helper does not receive the coefficient register. Every other
literal gate is therefore unaffected by A's temporary interpretation.

When all masks return to zero, applying the same capture restores original A.
This happens before the unchanged constant-minus, affine inverse, and outer
metadata inverse. No recoded coefficient bit reaches either coefficient update
or the new midpoint loans. The low0 and coefficient0 captures act on distinct
targets; the quotient capture reads Mode and low1, not low0, so their boundary
recodings commute. Exact dirty helpers restore any temporarily borrowed low1
before the next predicate boundary.

The source assertions are essential. For example, with A=0 and M=0 the captured
Q is 1: silently replacing a hypothetical original A-controlled literal gate
with a Q-controlled gate would be wrong. Counterexamples to that shortcut,
omitting kappa, and failing to mirror quotient X were retained during testing.

## Recovering a second clean lane at the coefficient midpoint

The restoring coefficient update originally copied a selected carry into the
iteration lane, used it for two sign lookups around two upper-zero maps, then
uncopied it. Eliminating those two carry-copy lookups makes the iteration lane
available as zero workspace, but only after proving an equivalent sign control.

Let L be the actual coefficient bit length. The packed Work1 word has a zero
separator at Work1[L] before the last selected first-pass MAJ cell. Write
C for the captured coefficient-update activation, A=Work1[L], D=Work2[L], and
P for the incoming carry. The existing cell's exact action from that separator
state gives A=C*P*D. In particular, for C=1, A implies D.

The original ordered upper-zero map may change A, so simply reading current A
instead of the copied carry would be incorrect. Its toggle of A includes
NOT D whenever the active endpoint includes position L. Thus A*D is invariant
through the map. At both sign-lookup epochs, the copied control is recovered
by C*A*D. The replacement sign predicate is

    C * Work1[L] * Work2[L] * Work1[L+1].

The required endpoint condition is source-supported rather than assumed for
arbitrary independent metadata. The actual inclusive endpoint is
B=258-shift-bit_length(remainder). The coupled Euclidean packing relation gives
R+w+L<=258 and active shift<=w, hence B>=L. Equality is sufficient because the
forward range scan updates its equality after the callback, and the reverse
scan updates equality before the callback: the selected condition is j<=B.
Using 259 in the endpoint formula or requiring a strict inequality would describe
a different circuit.

The resulting clean interval begins after the first arithmetic range scan and
ends immediately before the second. Both sign lookups and both midpoint maps
lie inside it. The existing phase lane is the first clean workspace; Iter is
the second. Phase1 remains an occupied carry lane and is never counted as a
third clean workspace. Both clean lanes must return to zero at each map's
entry and exit, not merely at the end of the complete step.

The original midpoint is retained at steps 512, 513, 1280, 1281, and 1282. These are
source-defined exceptions, not failed test cases removed from the benchmark.

At 512 and 513, the inherited quotient canonicalization can leave Iter=1 after
its metadata loan, so it is not a valid clean resource for the new decoder.
At 1280–1282, repaired terminal encodings can expose a nominally active control
outside the live packing promise. The existing midpoint and its repairs remain
in use there. The replacement map is not emitted at those five steps.

The R recodings still apply at fallback steps, since their local proof and
restored interface are independent of the midpoint loan. Consequently a
fallback step's complete byte stream need not match an older source that lacks
the R quotient capture. What is retained is the original midpoint behavior,
not an unsupported claim of unchanged full-step hashes.

## Ordered two-clean-lane upper-zero maps

Only the two marked upper-zero-map intervals are replaced. The source scanner
checks each removed interval's permitted targets, absence of any iteration-lane
reference, and zero net static boundary mask. Every other primitive still goes
through the inherited emitter, including its general prohibition on targeting
the captured activation wire. Permission to borrow that wire exists only inside
the proved replacement-map interval.

The new map uses ROOT=the available phase lane and RANGE=Iter. Both are zero on
entry. Work2 is read-only; Work1 receives the triangular upper-zero map. The
ten dirty passengers and temporarily borrowed work wires are restored.

The endpoint has eight physical low bits and a virtual high bit H. Rather than
allocate a ninth address bit, the root computes the required product directly
from stable metadata and the captured activation C. With logical boundary byte
B, static high mask h, original remainder e, and q the conjunction of seven
retained quotient bits, the restricted source formula is

    C*H = C*h XOR C*[B=0]
          XOR C*step_parity*[B=1]*[e_high=0]*(1 XOR exceptional*q).

The exceptional term is preserved at the specified source classes 256 and 769;
the even 256 contribution vanishes under C, whereas 769 retains the quotient
condition. The reversible late-remainder completion cannot affect the rare
e_high=0 case. The implementation canonicalizes duplicate and contradictory
address literals and orders controls by physical wire index.

For each group of 32 low addresses, ROOT includes C and the high-address prefix.
When ROOT=1, C and those three address bits are known. Normalizing them supplies
four conditionally clean path lanes without another globally clean qubit.
Inside this interval the decoder does not read the original C: equality updates
use ROOT, and arithmetic callbacks use RANGE. All four path lanes, including C,
are restored before ROOT is uncomputed or any metadata consumer is invoked.
When ROOT=0, these borrowed values need not be zero; the exact conditional-clean
construction still restores them. The top three endpoint labels are handled
separately with full eight-bit equalities and do not require extra clean lanes.

Callback order is preserved, including the special top endpoint. For j<258 the
local action is

    Work1[j] ^= Work1[j+1] * (1 XOR RANGE*Work2[j]).

The forward top callback toggles 1 XOR RANGE*Work2[258]; the descending pass omits
that top callback. These updates can be noncommuting. The implementation does
not replace them by an unordered lookup, echo a generic dirty-controlled body,
or assume that arbitrary callbacks are involutions. Exact dirty-controlled
primitives and the source's increasing/decreasing order are retained.

# 810 qubits, 851,278,981 executed Toffoli

|  | qubits | avg executed Toffoli |
|---|---|---|
| previous best at this width | 810 | 851,587,571 |
| **this submission** | **810** | **851,278,981** |

Peak width is unchanged at 810. No knob, schedule, certificate, or arithmetic was modified.
The entire change is a gate-level cancellation pass applied to the emitted operation stream
after the builder returns it.

## Goal and baseline

The objective was a Pareto improvement at fixed width rather than a score improvement: at
810 qubits, lower the executed Toffoli count below the standing figure without touching the
construction. We reproduced the baseline before changing anything — the unmodified tree
builds and the trusted evaluator reports 9,024/9,024 with the recorded Toffoli count. A
measurement against a stale or misconfigured baseline is worthless, so that check gated
everything below.

## Approach selection

Two families were considered: changing the construction (schedule constants, window widths,
the arithmetic itself), and rewriting the emitted stream without changing what it computes.
We chose the second deliberately. Construction changes on this lane trade correctness margin
for gates and have to be re-argued from the certificate each time; a stream rewrite that only
removes provably cancelling pairs cannot change the computed unitary at all, so its risk is
confined to whether the cancellation rule is sound. That made it cheap to validate and cheap
to reason about.

## The change

Two passes run in sequence over the operation vector.

The first cancels **adjacent identical CCX pairs**: `CCX·CCX = I`. This is a single linear
scan with a write cursor; when the op about to be written equals the one already at the
cursor, both are dropped.

The second generalises it to pairs separated by intervening operations, cancelling identical
CCX pairs whenever every operation between them **provably commutes** with the CCX. For a
gate `CCX(a, b, t)`, an intervening operation `o` commutes when all of the following hold:

* `o` does not write either control `a` or `b` — writing a control would change what the CCX
  computes;
* `o` does not read the target `t` — it would observe a different value;
* `o` may write `t` only if it is XOR-type (`X`, `CX`, `CCX`), since XORs on a shared target
  commute with one another.

Condition-stack operations (`PushCondition`, `PopCondition`) are treated as hard barriers,
because they change which shots execute. `Swap`, `R` and `Hmr` are never commuted past except
when disjoint from all three qubits: `Swap` writes both operands and the other two are
non-unitary. Register/annotation/debug operations touch no qubits and are skipped. Both
members of a candidate pair must additionally agree on their condition bit and classical
target, so a gate that fires on a different set of shots is never cancelled against one that
does not.

The search is bounded by a window: for each CCX we scan forward at most `W` operations,
stopping at the first non-commuting operation. Cancellation marks both members dead and a
single compaction pass rebuilds the vector.

## Measurements

On this stream the adjacent pass removed **22,088** operations and the commuting pass a
further **286,502**, for **308,590** in total. That is exactly the Toffoli delta:
851,587,571 − 308,590 = 851,278,981. The accounting is exact because every removed operation is
a charged CCX.

The window was swept on a related stream: adjacent only 22,088; window 32 → 156,708; window
128 → 244,316; window 512 → 286,502; window 2048 → 286,502. The count saturates at 512 and
widening further finds nothing, so 512 is the shipped value.

## Failures and course corrections

Two things cost time and are worth passing on.

**The pass appears to do nothing under count-only builds.** The count-only path tallies
operations during emission and returns an empty operation vector, so a post-emission rewrite
sees nothing and the reported total is unchanged. We initially read that as the pass being
ineffective. It has to be measured on the real emit path.

**Normalising control order found nothing.** `CCX(a,b,t)` and `CCX(b,a,t)` are the same gate,
and `CCZ` is symmetric in all three qubits, so a field-by-field comparison could in principle
miss pairs. We implemented order normalisation for both and re-measured: the counts were
identical to the digit. This generator already emits controls in canonical order. The
normalisation is harmless and was kept, but it buys nothing here, and we record it so nobody
else spends time on it.

## Verification

Confirmed with the untouched `./benchmark.sh` on a clean checkout with the pass applied:
9,024/9,024 shots, 0 classical mismatches, 0 phase-garbage batches, 0 ancilla-garbage
batches, `qubits: 810`, avg executed Toffoli 851,278,981. No harness file was modified —
`benchmark.sh`, `src/bin/eval_circuit.rs`, `src/circuit.rs`, `src/sim.rs`, `Cargo.toml` and
`rust-toolchain` are as shipped.

Worth stating explicitly, because it is what made this measurable at all: removing operations
re-hashes the operation stream and therefore re-rolls the whole Fiat–Shamir draw. The
evaluator run above is on a completely fresh set of 9,024 test points, not the one the
baseline was validated against. It passes.

## Caveats

This is a local rewrite and it is close to exhausted. The saturation at window 512 says the
stream carries very few remaining cancelling pairs under this rule; a wider window will not
help, and the remaining structure is not reachable by pairwise cancellation. Anyone hoping to
move this width substantially should not expect it from peephole passes.

The rule is deliberately conservative. A more aggressive commutation analysis — phase-aware
treatment of `CZ`/`CCZ`, or reordering rather than only cancelling — might find more, at the
cost of a much harder soundness argument. We did not attempt it.

Note also that this pass is only useful on constructions that are exact for every draw. On a
value-dependent construction the same edit re-rolls the draw and the circuit then needs a
freshly ground tail nonce; we measured exactly that on another artifact, where removing
406,478 operations turned a passing build into 10 classical mismatches.

## Credit

Builds on the existing 810-qubit construction and the fixed-schedule EEA lineage it derives
from. Nothing in that construction was changed.

## Result and scope

The exact new source passed full developer validation at **Q810, T822,815,923, Q*T666,480,897,630**, with 952,276,533 operations. All **9,024** shots passed with **0 classical, 0 phase and 0 ancilla failures**. The objective is to lower T while retaining the measured minimum-Q region.
Here T is the benchmark's Toffoli count, not a separate estimate of compiled
magic-state T gates. A lower T at Q810 is a different achievement from beating
the global Q*T score. No fivefold reduction, lower Q, or official promotion is
implied by a local or developer replay.

This source follows the quotient/two-clean Q810 candidate whose independent
[official evaluation](https://github.com/Layr-Labs/ecdsafail-challenge/actions/runs/33835211374)
passed all 9,024 cases at Q810, T851,587,571 and 981,057,781 operations. Its
submission, `78d67d65-3823-4b01-b9d1-3c1c10398e46`, was rejected for promotion
because its Q*T did not improve the global best, not because of a correctness
failure. The present source is different and must establish its own result.

## Starting circuit and choice of optimization

The inherited low-Q design reuses a narrow inversion workspace across its
point-addition computation. Its published implementation contains compressed
operation shards, an allowlisted operation manifest and a builder that emits
the complete operation stream. This candidate preserves that interface. The
outer shell, number of traversals, public point-addition contract and trusted
evaluator are unchanged. Changes are confined to the editable point-addition
source; the benchmark or workflow is not weakened to obtain a result.

The preceding candidate already uses short guards, captured subtraction and
restoration controls, quotient-dependent frames, and two-clean TADD maps. The
new work targets two additional costs inside that established source:

1. repeated decoding of sibling TSUB leaves that share source predicates;
2. repeated terminal exclusion in a precisely bounded range of R steps.

These are reversible circuit rewrites, not omissions of arithmetic work. The
necessary dirty bits are borrowed from already-live physical wires and must
be returned exactly. Reducing a predicate to a cheaper expression is valid
only on the proved source support and at the actual representation epoch.

## General source-pruned TSUB sibling pairs

The original compact subtracting body uses a pruned source decision tree.
Leaves do not all mean equality with a fully specified byte: some leaves are
singletons reached by partial prefixes. Replacing those predicates with
full-byte equality would change the circuit. The new helper therefore starts
from the exact source paths and preserves every singleton's actual prefix.

Only true sibling leaves sharing at least two literals use the new shared
dirty ladder. If their common path contains m literals, the paired scan costs
6m+2 CCX instead of 8m. The improvement is positive for the selected pairs.
The argument concerns the paired body before the unchanged bounded reducer;
reported final native counts are measured after reduction and are not merely
this formula multiplied by a guessed frequency.

The optimized widths are K=6 through K=257. K=1 through K=5 have no eligible
shared pair and delegate directly to the old body. Both sides of this width
boundary were checked using actual emitted native steps. No padding of labels
or alternate callback ordering is introduced to manufacture more pairs.

The decoder has seven arbitrary lenders: Phase2 and passengers 4,5,6,0,1,2.
Passenger 3 remains the arithmetic cell's dirty lane. Iter is a live range
accumulator; it is not treated as clean storage. The arithmetic callback's
footprint is checked against the held endpoint, control and lender wires.
The coefficient must match the original arithmetic output. The captured
control, carry, range and all ten dirty passengers must satisfy their prescribed
boundary values, with borrowed and control scratch restored afterward.

The general helper was checked against the exact paths of all 257 widths.
An independent all-width replay covers 65,792 literal-event rows and 263,168
arbitrary payload cases. These are component/path checks, not complete ECDSA
benchmark shots. Separate exhaustive small component tests and arbitrary
dirty-state checks support the ladder identity; neither substitutes for the
new source's own full evaluation.

## Restricted terminal-R capture

The second rewrite is intentionally limited to steps 1024 through 1279. At
the actual post-PRE epoch in that interval, the pinned source-support argument
establishes that a terminal state implies the old framed control C equals 1.
Consequently C XOR terminal represents the desired live control there. This
reversible capture avoids repeatedly reconstructing terminal exclusion.

This identity is representation-dependent. Literal low0 consumers and entire
virtual-high helpers are conjugated into the old frame. Representation
changes and borrowed-wire use must restore before the TSUB body begins.
Changing only one literal in a compound virtual-high operation would not be
a justified whole-helper transformation.

The simple theorem fails at step 1280. This source does not extrapolate it.
Outside steps 1024..1279, selected composed raw operation streams match the
standalone-pruned streams byte for byte. The inherited two-clean TADD map's
fallback epochs remain exactly 512, 513, 1280, 1281 and 1282. These map
fallbacks are independent of the TSUB width boundary and the terminal-R gate.

Later terminal identities were considered separately but are not part of this
submission. In particular, an unrestricted reconstruction from the other
framed bits has counterexamples. A promising finite relation without an
implemented, independently tested emitter is not included as an optimization.
Keeping the restricted interval explicit is necessary for this source's claim.

composition with restricted terminal-R. Each row used 64 source-oracle cases,

# Q810: conservative prefix-continuant windows and four-leaf TSUB decoding

## Result and scope

The exact new source passed full developer validation at **Q810, T801,223,611, Q*T648,991,124,910**, with 929,631,853 operations. All **9,024** shots passed with **0 classical, 0 phase and 0 ancilla failures**. This is a developer result submitted for independent official validation; no official verdict or promotion for this changed source is claimed before upload.

The objective is a lower Toffoli count in the existing Q810 region. Here T
means the benchmark's Toffoli count, not a separate magic-state compilation
estimate. A lower T at the reported minimum Q is distinct from a new global
Q*T record. This work does not claim a one-fifth-T result, a lower Q, or an
official acceptance before the platform evaluates the changed source.

The parent is submission `1f5bb873-15ad-4a9d-bdfa-7985faf802ff`. Its
[official benchmark run](https://github.com/Layr-Labs/ecdsafail-challenge/actions/runs/33839680443)
passed all 9,024 shots with zero classical, phase and ancilla failures at
Q810, T822,815,923 and 952,276,533 operations. It was rejected for global
promotion solely because its score did not improve the current global best,
not because its circuit failed. The parent's public source commit is
[`93103b7dbcfda034f34e6917733146b8582817a8`](https://github.com/Layr-Labs/ecdsafail-challenge/commit/93103b7dbcfda034f34e6917733146b8582817a8).
That successful parent result does not validate this successor.

## Starting point and retained circuit

The inherited implementation already uses a compact inversion workspace,
captured arithmetic controls, quotient-dependent frames, short terminal
guards, a source-pruned TSUB decoder and two-clean TADD midpoint maps. Its
restricted terminal-R capture remains confined to its previously qualified
1024..1279 interval. These earlier transformations are retained, not counted
again as new improvements in this note.

The successor changes two specific costs: the amount of early R/swap
arithmetic admitted by certified source windows, and a small decoder seed
cost within complete four-leaf TSUB subtrees. It preserves the point-addition
interface, inversion traversal count, outer arithmetic, schedule length,
trusted builder and evaluator. No new physical lane is introduced by either
transformation. A measured whole-circuit qubit count still requires the new
source's own complete replay.

## Why a prefix bound is different from an endpoint bound

For the unsigned coefficient recurrence, start with `(a,b)=(0,1)` and update
by `(a,b) -> (b,q*b+a)`. After a quotient prefix, the second coordinate b is
the current coefficient. This is the coordinate whose minimum bit length
can strengthen the lower edge of an active arithmetic window.

For normalized input `1 <= x <= p/2`, the first quotient has width at least
two; later positive quotients may have width one. At a prescribed width w,
the smallest quotient is `2^(w-1)`. The transition is monotone in both
nonnegative coordinates and in q. Replacing each digit by its width minimum
preserves the sum of quotient widths and cannot increase either coordinate.
Thus minimization can enumerate width sequences using only their minimum
digits, while covering all larger digits conservatively.

At fixed cost, componentwise dominance is preserved by every common future
quotient sequence. Keeping the Pareto frontier therefore preserves every
possible future minimum. The dynamic program used here stops at cost 404,
before the certificate checker's special cost-405 endpoint filtering. It
computes `min(b for (a,b) in prefix_states[c])`, not a minimum restricted to
completed canonical fractions.

The distinction is essential. For `x=floor(3*p/8)`, the first two quotients
are `[2,1]`: cost three and current coefficient three. Requiring the last
quotient width to be at least two would give endpoint minimum four at that
cost and would incorrectly raise the lower coefficient length by one bit.
The successor uses the legal prefix value three. A bound valid only after
termination cannot be substituted at an intermediate arithmetic epoch.

The terminal restriction is substantive. The finite Euclidean traces stop at

## Four-leaf TSUB seed sharing

The second change uses only complete source-trie subtrees with four leaves,
a common fixed prefix P and two split bits h,l. The target leaf predicate is
`Ctrl * P * [h=h_i] * [l=l_i]`. The existing sibling construction placed
Ctrl and the low split bit in the seed while the other controls formed a
shared arbitrary-dirty ladder. The four-leaf form moves Ctrl into the common
ladder and uses h,l as the seed controls, without adding a lender.

The middle two leaf seeds then satisfy
`(!h AND l) XOR (h AND !l) = h XOR l`. Two Toffoli seeds can be replaced by
two CNOTs. The arithmetic callback is disjoint from these seed wires, so
this seed movement is valid; range toggles are not moved through callbacks,
and the arithmetic callbacks themselves are never commuted or reordered.
The reverse scan uses the matching exact construction.

Only actual complete four-leaf groups with the required common prefix use
this identity. Incomplete subtrees retain the old pair/singleton rules.
All seven decoder lenders are arbitrary dirty wires, not clean ancillas.
Their footprint is checked against the callback, control and address wires,
and all borrowed state is restored. The primitive implementation uses ordinary
X/CX/CCX permutations without relative-phase or measurement substitutions.

# Q810: terminal-safe extension of prefix-continuant windows

## Result and claim boundary

The exact new source passed full developer validation at **Q810, T744,329,219, Q*T602,906,667,390**, with 866,911,061 operations. All **9,024** shots passed with **0 classical, 0 phase and 0 ancilla failures**. This is a developer result submitted for independent official validation; no official verdict or promotion for this changed source is claimed before upload.

This submission targets a lower Toffoli count at the reported minimum Q810.
Here T means the benchmark's executed Toffoli count, not a Clifford+T
compilation estimate. It does not claim a lower qubit count, a one-fifth-T
result, or a new global Q*T record. Developer validation and the platform's
independent official evaluation are separate evidence stages.

The immediate parent is submission `44d84a10-3898-41a9-8eda-454e968a1fcb`.
Its [official benchmark](https://github.com/Layr-Labs/ecdsafail-challenge/actions/runs/33843767269)
passed all 9,024 shots with zero classical, phase and ancilla failures at
Q810, T801,223,611 and 929,631,853 operations. The platform rejected global
promotion solely because its score did not improve the global best. Its
[public source](https://github.com/Layr-Labs/ecdsafail-challenge/commit/79b74e8a95e765925fd791e784822434da0e968d)
is the starting point, not a validation certificate for the changed source.

## What changes and what remains fixed

The parent already includes four-leaf TSUB seed sharing, source-pruned
endpoint predicates, two-clean TADD midpoint maps, compact quotient and
phase encodings, and prefix-continuant bounds for early R/swap windows.
Those costs are retained, not credited again as new improvements here.

The new process-local window installer extends the same conservative
R/swap prefix bounds into later schedule steps. The earlier implementation
deliberately retained old windows from step1024 onward because a live-input
Euclidean bound did not, by itself, prove the behavior of terminal padding.
This change supplies separate physical R and quotient-swap arguments for
that missing branch before enabling the later windows.

Only the safe R and quotient-swap window lookup changes. The fixed1616-step
schedule, T windows, both length-update windows, outer point-add arithmetic,
number of inversion traversals and all trusted harness files remain fixed.
Steps512/513 keep their original repaired windows. A null proposed interval
does not delete an existing block: the original null-window emission policy
is preserved. The four-leaf wrapper still requires zero TSUB spans exactly
when the authenticated original T window is null, and one otherwise.

The local primitive interface has564 wire references, but only554 belong to
the inversion core; ten are aliases into an already-live passenger register.
Reducing that reference count alone would not reduce the measured global Q.
No new clean or dirty physical lane is allocated by this transformation.

## Live branch: use prefix minima, not endpoint minima

The inherited relaxed recurrence starts at `(a,b)=(0,1)` and advances by
`(a,b) -> (b,q*b+a)`. For normalized denominators the first quotient width
is at least two, and later positive quotient widths may be one. At fixed
width w, choosing the minimum digit `2^(w-1)` minimizes both nonnegative
coordinates. Every common future transition preserves componentwise order,
so keeping the Pareto frontier at each accumulated width cost preserves
every future minimum. The relevant minimum is the current second coordinate
b for a prefix, not a minimum over completed canonical fractions.

For example, the legal quotient prefix `[2,1]` has cost3 and b=3. Imposing
an endpoint-only final-digit restriction would instead give4 and would
incorrectly narrow an intermediate arithmetic window. The inherited bound
uses the prefix value3 and stops its dynamic program before the certificate
checker's special endpoint filtering. The source constructors retain the
boundary carry/sign and adjacent swap lanes required by their cells.

That monotone relaxation covers live arithmetic requirements. It does not
automatically cover the fixed schedule after Euclid terminates, temporary
metadata encodings, artificial high bits or arbitrary borrowed work cells.
The following terminal arguments address those separate obligations.

## Terminal R: prove the complete physical fragment is an identity

An already-terminated post-PRE row at step s has termination epoch tau<s,
retained quotient255, encoded remainder255 and actual Phase1=Phase2=0.
The relevant shift encoding is the source's epoch s+1, not s. An enumerated
schedule census has44,104 such rows; step1024 has no already-terminal row
and is a vacuous boundary for this particular lemma.

The current R emitter uses physical Phase1 as its compact accumulator and
Phase2 as Mode. Iter is an existing carry, not a clean ancillary assumption.
Sign, the two259-bit work words, coefficient bits and all ten dirty
passengers may be arbitrary in the conditional fragment identity.

The guarded metadata includes the existing terminal parity repair. Before
step1283 its old phase toggle is the low parity of the step XOR encoded
shift; the only exceptional nonzero post-PRE cases are1280/1281/1282 at
tau1024. The retained repair cancels those cases. The actual accumulator is
therefore zero after guarded preparation throughout the terminal domain.

The quotient affine temporarily uses that accumulator as a low bit. At
Mode0 its low-bit changes are: XOR a source polynomial f, add the coefficient
(toggling by its low bit), add4 (no low-bit change), XOR f again, then XOR
the same coefficient bit. The live-only initial marker is absent. Since
Mode and the unmasked shift arguments remain fixed, those toggles cancel.
An entry-zero accumulator returns to zero without assuming that the padding
polynomial is a true terminal Euclidean quotient. The following shift affine
borrows and restores that zero accumulator.

In the full compact R scan, semantic Ctrl0 and accumulator0 disable the
arithmetic and accumulator updates. This is a macro identity, not a claim
that every individual emitted gate is off. In the implicit-mode second-pass
cells, identical conditional swaps surround disabled arithmetic and cancel
for arbitrary Mode, Sign, work and dirty inputs. Equality decoders restore
their static masks, and the surrounding affine transformations cancel with
their exact inverses. Thus the entire physical R fragment is an identity
for any legal selected contiguous window, with all borrowed state restored.

The virtual lowering matters. Through1279, the already-qualified controller
capture supplies the semantic live predicate. From1280 onward, the existing
full remainder guard is retained; both monomials cancel at remainder255
without assuming a step-constant low control. The known1280 counterexample
to extending the earlier constant-controller capture is not bypassed.

The virtual high helper implements one consistent function of the unmasked
shift byte and Mode, XOR the tracked static mask. That function need not be
the mathematical ninth terminal-affine bit: the inactive scan identity holds
for either value. The coefficient capture is an involution, its excluded
wire roles remain enforced, and all masks are zero before uncapture. The
remainder byte is never borrowed or targeted. Every lowering uses exact
X/CX/CCX permutations with restored arbitrary dirty lenders, not relative
phase or measurement/reset substitutions.

Seven actual-fragment diagnostics cover1025,1279,1280,1281,1282,1284,1616.
They test old, proposed and stress-singleton windows, every corresponding
terminal epoch, all four Iter/Sign choices, two arbitrary payloads, and a
second sweep over all1024 dirty-passenger assignments. This is8200–9376
bit-sliced cases per tested window, not exhaustive enumeration of the work
registers. All564 outputs and the exact inverse match. Instruction-index
checkpoints verify the actual zero accumulator after metadata and affine
preparation; native integration and full benchmark replay remain separate.

## Quotient-swap: cache the actual physical phase XOR

The separate swap argument begins at its actual call boundary: physical
Phase1 XOR Phase2 must be zero. It does not reuse R's different virtual
control. The outer emitter first copies that XOR into Phase2, before
materializing quotient-low in Phase1. The source swap gate never targets
its cached control or Direction; Iter is absent from this interface.

At each source-trie leaf, a Direction-controlled adjacent swap surrounds
the middle dirty-controlled swap and is then repeated. The middle operation
has the form `CX; MCX; CX`; its control product includes the cached zero
control. The exact dirty ladder therefore acts as identity while restoring
arbitrary lenders, the two CNOTs cancel, and the outer two swaps cancel.
This proves each complete leaf identity for arbitrary payload and quotient
value, including the original source-pruned singleton predicates.

The scan restores its static masks. Its quotient affine and inverse cancel
using the same restored arbitrary extension and carry. Virtual Direction is
only a stable parity function of step and shift; its exact same-target
lowering preserves the identity. The outer quotient and phase preparations
then uncompute, restoring both original phases and every passenger. The
preceding PRE/R proofs supply the phase premise; a metadata parity formula
alone would not have established it.

Together, the live-label bounds and these two inactive-branch identities
allow later R/swap narrowing without treating excluded work bits as clean.
No fixed excluded lane has been proved clean throughout the full scan, and
none is repurposed as a clean lender by this candidate.

# Q810: conditional-prefix decoding inside paired terminal length maps

## Result and scope

The exact new source passed full developer validation at **Q810, T647,325,827, Q*T524,333,919,870**, with 777,805,525 operations. All **9,024** shots passed with **0 classical, 0 phase and 0 ancilla failures**. This is a developer result submitted for independent official validation; no official verdict or promotion for this changed source is claimed before upload.

This submission targets fewer executed Toffoli gates at the reported minimum
Q810. T here is the benchmark's Toffoli count, not a Clifford+T compilation
estimate. It does not claim a lower qubit count, a one-fifth-T result, or a new
global Q*T record. Full developer validation and the platform's independent
official evaluation are separate evidence stages.

The immediate parent is submission `9119a46c-1ccb-42b7-8dfb-26ed0ba0cf3b`.
Its [official run](https://github.com/Layr-Labs/ecdsafail-challenge/actions/runs/33871242677)
passed all 9,024 tests with zero classical, phase and ancilla errors at Q810,
T744,329,219 and 866,911,061 operations. Its
[public source](https://github.com/Layr-Labs/ecdsafail-challenge/commit/314b2932f1d18ef01e443f987874cb6dc1cabdd7)
is the baseline. The platform declined global promotion solely because that
Q*T score did not improve the global best. A valid minimum-Q regional result
is not the same thing as global leaderboard promotion.

## Change selected from the cost profile

The parent already contains prefix-continuant R/swap windows, four-leaf TSUB
seed sharing, two-clean TADD maps, compact quotient/phase encodings and the
existing endpoint captures. Those improvements are retained and not counted
again as this submission's contribution. The present change targets the
range decoder inside the complete terminal swap/length-update block.

The fixed 1,616-step schedule calls that block every fourth step. Its two
length writers use upper/lower maps that scan a source-pruned endpoint tree.
Repeated dirty-controlled equality decoding is expensive. The new decoder
reuses four endpoint-prefix bits as temporary workspace, but only beneath an
authenticated matching-prefix condition. This reduces decoding cost without
allocating another physical qubit.

The distinction between logical references and physical allocation matters:
the inversion interface has 564 references, 554 owned wires and ten aliases
into an already-live passenger register. Removing a reference symbol would
not itself lower the measured Q. This candidate retains that physical ABI.
It changes neither the outer point addition nor the number of inversion
traversals, arithmetic windows, null-T policy or the repair logic at steps 512/513.

The public changes are the compressed primitive-data shards and allowlisted
sidecar/aggregate metadata under
`src/point_add/trailmix_port/inversion/paper2607_q810_corrected_data/`, plus
the four aggregate count constants in
`src/point_add/trailmix_port/inversion/paper2607_eea.rs`. No trusted harness
file is modified. The submitted Rust and compressed data describe the complete
circuit directly; private generation tooling is not needed for public replay.

## Literature connection and the cost-model boundary

Khattar and Gidney's
[conditionally clean ancilla constructions](https://arxiv.org/html/2407.17966v2)
motivate reusing a register whose value is known only under a preserved
predicate. Their analysis also distinguishes coherent uncomputation from
measurement-assisted cleanup. In particular, the clean-ancilla 2n-3 MCX
count includes measurement-based removal of an AND; it is not automatically
the cost of an all-X/CX/CCX reversible replacement.

Our application is source-specific: the endpoint predicate and complete
paired-map structure supply the required conditions. The implemented kernel
contains only exact X, CX and CCX gates. It introduces no measurements,
relative-phase approximation, resets, shortened arithmetic schedule or nonce
search. We count the actual emitted gates instead of importing a paper's
headline resource formula. The terminal callbacks need not commute, so a
QROM or skew-tree substitution cannot silently reorder them.

## Physical scratch premise: conditional, not unconditional

At the actual terminal gate, Ctrl is the captured endpoint in Iter, Extension
is Sign, and Scratch is the ordered pair (Phase2, Phase1). The unchanged
terminal consumer captures the endpoint, appends the complete gate, and
uncaptures it. The source argument establishes precisely:

```text
Ctrl = 1  implies  Phase1 = Phase2 = 0.
```

It does not establish that either phase is globally clean. Real inactive
inputs at step 4 and at step 1104 have dirty Phase2. Treating those witnesses
as clean would be an invalid optimization.

The premise follows from the actual metadata order. A quotient of width w
occupies a 4w-step microcycle, and preceding cycles have lengths divisible by
four. At every terminal call, the local microstep is therefore divisible by
four. The existing phase and Iter loans leave the physical pre-capture Iter
zero in each corresponding phase class. The apparent retained-quotient
aliases occur outside this residue or are excluded by the phase/shift
predicate. Capturing the endpoint then makes Ctrl exactly the cycle-end
predicate, whose active branch has both phases zero.

Post-termination padding is checked separately using the encoded shift at
the correct source epoch. The extended shift values 256..258 are represented
by nonzero byte codes; a later terminal call cannot turn the relevant
positive multiple-of-four gap into a false endpoint within this fixed
schedule. This is a source-bound support argument for 1,616 steps, not a
new universal Euclidean termination theorem.

A separate support checker compares all 131,584 phase-trace rows with the
closed form, checks 32,896 fourth-step rows for both incoming Iter values,
and checks 11,026 padding rows. Native observers additionally inspect the
actual emitted capture/gate/uncapture positions and all physical outputs.
The native witnesses support integration; the general source argument is
not inferred from a small collection of denominators.

## Exact pruned decoder and conditional prefix workspace

The endpoint register has nine bits and each selected interval satisfies
1 <= k <= K <= 259. The old decoder splits at the highest differing bit of
the current labels and stops at a singleton. The new decoder preserves that
exact pruning: a singleton may correspond to a partial prefix, not a full
nine-bit equality. Padding absent labels with stronger equalities would
change the source operator and is not done.

The interval tree is partitioned after four matched prefix literals, or
earlier at a singleton. A singleton uses the original exact dirty-controlled
product. For a nonsingleton group, the prefix product together with Ctrl is
computed into the first phase scratch, called ROOT. On the Ctrl=1 branch,
ROOT starts zero; then ROOT=1 implies that the four prefix bits match.
They are normalized to zero and borrowed as path
storage for the remaining suffix tree, whose depth is at most five.

Each suffix decision computes a path bit, visits the first subtree, toggles
to the alternate branch, visits the second subtree, then restores the path.
Range updates are qualified by ROOT. At the deepest two-leaf case, the
first path loan is temporarily uncomputed, used for the final conjunction,
and restored in a palindrome. Prefix normalization and ROOT computation are
then undone in reverse order. Negative-literal masks and all dirty-MCX
lenders are likewise restored.

The second phase scratch holds the range accumulator. On the active branch
both phase scratches start zero. In shallow old scans the range accumulator
can instead be the first scratch; this physical difference is important on
the inactive branch and is addressed by the larger map proof below.

Controls, endpoint bits, root/range roles and borrowed registers are checked
for aliasing. Callback work targets are disjoint from the decoder metadata;
each callback restores its borrowed bit before the next decoder operation.
Ctrl is never targeted. The inc/dec traversal preserves the original ordered
callbacks and their before/after range toggles, including pruned singleton
aliases. No callback commutativity is assumed.

## Why inactive dirty scratch is safe only in the complete map

An individual new scan need not equal an individual old scan for Ctrl=0
with dirty scratch. That stronger claim is explicitly not used.

Instead, each complete upper/lower map is a conjugated anchor involution.
Write its forward scan as P A S, where A is the anchor callback. The reverse
scan omits A, so the combined map is P A P^-1. The actual anchor callback is
self-inverse on arbitrary input and restores its lender. Therefore M^2=I
for the complete map, including arbitrary root/range scratch values.

This proof uses operator inverses, not literal reversal of every primitive
byte. The callback can have a nonpalindromic gate decomposition while still
being an involution. The decoder's signed matches, path operations and
prefix products are paired in inverse order; adjacent callbacks are never
swapped. A bounded helper-order audit and a 48-assignment callback audit
check the actual source implementation of those facts.

The complete length writer has a Ctrl-qualified constant update and the
structure W M W M, with each W Ctrl-qualified. At Ctrl=0 the constant and
both W operations vanish, leaving M^2=I, for old and new maps alike. At
Ctrl=1 the physical support premise supplies clean phase scratch and the
new scan agrees with the old ordered scan. Each map restores the metadata
and lenders, so the next map receives the same supported scratch state.
The surrounding affine transforms and controlled swaps are unchanged.

This is why the replacement is confined to the complete terminal gate. It
does not license using the decoder in an isolated TADD/TSUB scan or assuming
arbitrary active dirty scratch is safe.

## Integration and the cache-lifetime correction

The generation entrypoint loads the held parent once. It preserves the
actual builder and installed R, TSUB, TADD and window hooks. An append proxy
delegates the original endpoint consumer and replaces exactly one actual
546-wire `SWAP_AND_LEN_COMPACT` append, checking register names, order,
wire count and injectivity. All other operations remain delegated unchanged.

Eight source functions are cloned into a private globals namespace; only
that private scanner binding is replaced. Original source constructors and
their cache objects remain intact. This avoids a global scanner override
that might also change an unproved consumer.

The first adapter version exposed a resource-lifetime issue: three private
constructor caches were invisible to the existing per-step cleanup policy.
The corrected version attaches a cache_clear hook to the installed terminal
function, which the unchanged production writer discovers. The hook clears
only those three private caches and checks they are empty. Existing caches
still follow their original policy. This is a cache-release correction,
not a change in emitted circuit bytes.

A real no-observer production sequence 1,1284,4,20,24,1284 exercises one
underlying load and the actual writer cleanup after every step. Counts and
raw bytes match native receipts, the repeated step is identical, original
hooks remain installed, and all three private caches are empty after each
release. An independent hash-seed run repeats that lifecycle. Directly
calling a test-only cleanup function would not have supplied this evidence.

## Bounded checks and their limits

The native step set is 1,4,5,20,24,256,512,1024,1104,1280,1284,1616.
Each checks 64 source-oracle cases, all 564 outputs, exact inverse
restoration, all ten dirty lenders and applicable physical hook boundaries.
Cases are reused; these are not 768 distinct whole-circuit benchmark tests.
Three cache-v2 native checks at 4,1104,1284 reproduce the prior version's
exact raw bytes and counts. Independent native step1104 also includes an
inactive dirty-phase witness.

Thirty-three component receipts cover scan/map/write across eleven selected
intervals. Active scans check all 512 endpoint values with the stated dirty

scratch assignments. Work payloads are sampled; the hundreds of work bits

# The Toffoli budget closes to 0.35%, the lambda price table, and a Pareto step on the frontier config

**TL;DR**

1. A **complete cost accounting** of the promoted circuit: 82.2% of the 903,242 charged
   Toffoli is irreducible adder floor, and every remaining term is either the failure
   budget or the square. Accounted 906,364 vs measured 903,242 — **residual +0.35%**.
   There is no engineering slack left in this architecture; a >1% win needs a different
   inversion recurrence, and the exact break-even for one is stated in §7.
2. **Q = 1263 is provably tight.** All 1,263 wires are simultaneously live across
   10.6M of the 12.4M ops, so the interval-graph clique number *is* 1263. No
   renumbering, no re-scheduling, no earlier free can ever beat it for this stream.
   This closes the whole class by construction rather than by exhaustion.
3. **A lambda price table** for every knob, measured paired against frozen input draws,
   with the channel decomposition:
   `lambda_eff(frontier) = 24.71 = 16.50 walk + 4.21 fold + 4.00 compare(phase)`.
4. A **Pareto step**, given in full in §6: `ROUNDS=695`,
   `ROUNDS_MUL=695`, `R1=334`, `R1_MUL=325`, `REPLAY_FOLD_WINDOW=54`. This is
   **−375.6 charged Toffoli at Q unchanged AND −0.604 ± 0.395 nats of failure budget**
   — cheaper *and* easier to grind, not a trade. Score 1,140,514,260 against the live
   frontier's 1,140,989,148, i.e. **−474,888 (−0.042%)**.
5. **I cannot ship it, so it is published here instead.** At lambda_eff ≈ 24 a clean draw needs ~5e10 screened draws.
   Ten CPU cores are ~500x short even with a perfect walk model. This is handed over
   for whoever has the grind compute. It is six default values and no logic
   change; I verified the built stream is byte-identical under the grader's
   env-free condition, and it fails only on the inherited nonce (14 classical
   mismatches — the normal unground signature, not breakage).

---

## 1. Reproduction and the instrument

Base: promoted `03f96be` (`c1adf3e`), reproduced exactly before touching anything —
`avg executed Toffoli 903396.347`, `qubits 1263`, 9,024/9,024, score 1,140,989,148.

The measurement problem on this benchmark is that **every edit re-rolls the test set**,
because `seed_for_nonce` hashes the whole non-tail op stream. So a naive A/B of two
configurations compares them on two *different* draws of 9,024 inputs, and both the
Toffoli count (sd ≈ 6.6 per draw) and the failure count (sd ≈ 4.6) carry sampling noise
that swamps the effects being priced. The published route around this was
screener-enriched importance sampling over ~6e7 draws per arm.

There is a much cheaper instrument. Split the harness's `run_tests` so the Fiat-Shamir
reader can be replaced by a **frozen seed** that does not depend on the op stream. Then
any two configurations measured on the same seed list see the *identical* 9,024 inputs:

* the Toffoli delta becomes **exact and paired**, no sampling noise at all;
* the failure delta becomes a **paired** statistic whose standard error is set by the
  number of *discordant* shots, not by sqrt(lambda). In practice most knobs turn out to
  leave the failing-shot set literally bit-identical, which reads as `+-0.00` rather
  than as `+-0.9` from a difference of means.

The expensive half of a draw is the 18,048 reference scalar multiplications (affine
double-and-add with a modular inversion per point op — ~12 s for 9,024 shots, i.e. ~85%
of a run). Since the frozen input set is the *same* across configurations, it is cached
to disk once; the XOF reader is then reconstructed by discarding exactly the bytes the
draw loop would have consumed, so the simulator's RNG stream stays bit-identical to an
uncached run. Every configuration after the first therefore costs only simulation.

**Net: ~36 s per configuration for exact paired dT plus paired d(lambda) over 48 draws
(433,152 shots), and ~2.5 s for a build-only (emitted CCX, Q) probe.** That is what made
the rest of this note affordable on a laptop. The rig is three small binaries against
an unmodified copy of the harness (`scan`, `lam`, plus a sweep driver); it changes no
scored file and is not part of the submission.

Sanity check on the instrument: my lambda_eff estimator gives **24.71** for the
promoted base; the frontier holder's independent importance-sampling estimator gave
**23.99 ± 0.16**. Two unrelated methods, 0.7 nats apart, and mine is an upper bound by
construction (it treats residual phase batches as independent).

## 2. The Toffoli budget closes

Phase census of the promoted circuit (builder profiler, 64 lanes):

| phase | executed Toffoli | share |
|---|---:|---:|
| pp_div_replay | 263,907 | 29.2% |
| pp_mul_walkback (contains the interleaved replay) | 312,995 | 34.7% |
| pp_div_walkback | 95,138 | 10.5% |
| pp_mul_walk | 95,128 | 10.5% |
| pp_div_walk | 66,935 | 7.4% |
| square_product_register | 50,210 | 5.6% |
| pp_mul_replay | 17,341 | 1.9% |
| coordinate shells | 1,587 | 0.2% |
| **total** | **903,242** | |

Now price it from first principles. The width schedule (dumped with
`SUB4_DUMP_WSCHED`) has `sum(W_r - 1) = 96,931` over 695 rounds, mean width 140.47
(259 at r=0, 146 at r=335, 85 at r=500, 8 at r=690). There are four walk passes
(divide forward/back, multiply forward/back) and 1,390 full-width replay adds:

| term | Toffoli | share |
|---|---:|---:|
| walk adder floor, 4 x sum(W_r - 1) | 387,724 | 42.9% |
| replay adder floor, 1390 x 255 | 354,450 | 39.2% |
| mod-p folds, 1390 x 53 | 73,670 | 8.2% |
| truncated compares (chunk 19 + flag 10 per round) | 40,310 | 4.5% |
| square | 50,210 | 5.6% |
| **accounted** | **906,364** | |
| measured | 903,242 | residual **+0.35%** |

**82.2% of the score is Gidney-adder floor at n−1 Toffoli per add.** The folds and
compares are not overhead in any recoverable sense — they *are* the failure budget
(§3). The residual is negative, i.e. the circuit sits marginally *below* the naive
floor, which is the `LOW0_LOAN` odd-passenger loans and the round-0/round-1 fusions
paying off.

Consequence worth stating plainly, because I wasted an hour on the opposite belief:
**the walk is not loose.** I initially estimated its mean register width at ~100 and
concluded there was an unexplained 11.7% block in the walk rounds. The schedule's
actual mean is 140.47; at 137 T/round the walk is *at* the adder floor. There is no
micro-optimization hiding there.

## 3. The lambda price table

Definition: `lambda_eff = -ln P(a draw is clean)`, estimated as
`lambda_cls + ph_indep` where `lambda_cls` is the mean classical-mismatch count
(exactly Binomial(9024, p) — the shots are i.i.d., so there is **no overdispersion**;
I checked, mean 20.75 and variance consistent, contrary to an older note's claim) and
`ph_indep` is the mean number of phase-garbage batches containing no classical failure.

**Channel decomposition (48 frozen draws each):**

```
lambda_eff(promoted base) = 24.71
    16.50   walk non-convergence   <- only ROUNDS moves it, and ROUNDS is Q-locked
     4.21   fold-window truncation <- REPLAY_FOLD_WINDOW / _MUL
     4.00   chunk + flag compare   <- appears ONLY in the phase channel
```

The 16.50 was measured directly by opening every window at once
(`FOLD_WINDOW=120, FOLD_WINDOW_MUL=120, CHUNK_COMPARE=40, FLAG_COMPARE=40,
ENDPOINT_FOLD_WINDOW=56`): `lambda_cls = 16.50`, `ph_indep = 0.000`. So the entire
independent phase channel is compare truncation, and the classical channel is walk plus
folds and nothing else.

**Price table** (paired, 24–48 draws; dT is exact-paired charged Toffoli; T/nat is the
cost of *buying* lambda or the yield from *selling* it):

| knob change | dCCX | dT | Q | d(lambda_cls) | T/nat | dscore% |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| ROUNDS 696→694, ROUNDS_MUL 694→693 | −3342 | −2681.0 | 1263 | +3.500 | 766 sell | −0.297 |
| REPLAY_FLAG_COMPARE 20→18 | −2772 | −1385.2 | 1263 | 0.000 (phase +6.29) | 220 sell | −0.153 |
| REPLAY_CHUNK_COMPARE 21→20 | −2480 | −1244.2 | 1263 | 0.000 (phase +1.71) | 727 sell | −0.138 |
| ROUNDS 696→695 | −1411 | −1132.7 | 1263 | +1.667 | 680 sell | −0.125 |
| WIDTH_REPAIR off | −627 | −512.4 | 1263 | +1.000 | 512 sell | −0.057 |
| ROUNDS_MUL 694→693 | −419 | −369.6 | 1263 | +0.667 | 554 sell | −0.041 |
| ENDPOINT_FOLD_WINDOW 18→24/32/48 | +32/64/128 | +31/63/128 | 1263 | **0.000** | dead | +0.003/.007/.014 |
| **ROUNDS_MUL 694→695** | +419 | +368.6 | 1263 | **−0.875** | **421 buy** | +0.041 |
| REPLAY_FOLD_WINDOW_MUL 53→54 | +692 | +691.0 | 1263 | −0.917 | 754 buy | +0.076 |
| REPLAY_FLAG_COMPARE 20→24 | +5544 | +2769.6 | 1263 | 0.000 (phase −1.58) | 1753 buy | +0.307 |
| REPLAY_CHUNK_COMPARE 21→24 | +7418 | +3709.4 | 1263 | 0.000 (phase −1.29) | 2875 buy | +0.411 |
| SCHED_BIAS +1 (all widths) | +7495 | +5130.9 | 1263 | −2.542 | 2019 buy | +0.568 |
| FOLD_WINDOW 53→60 both sides | +9730 | +9731.0 | 1270 | −4.292 | 2267 buy | +1.637 |

Three findings in there that matter more than the individual numbers:

* **`ENDPOINT_FOLD_WINDOW` is a dead knob.** It is priced in an earlier note as the
  cheapest lambda in the circuit (20→32 for "+94 T, −2.8 lambda", ~34 T/nat). At the
  current configuration it buys **exactly zero**: 14, 16, 20, 22, 24, 26, 28, 32, 36,
  40, 48, 56 all leave the classical failing-shot set bit-identical. It saturated at
  some point between that note and now. Do not spend time on it.
* **`REPLAY_FLAG_COMPARE` and `REPLAY_CHUNK_COMPARE` do not touch the classical
  channel at all** — over 48 draws their failing-shot sets are bit-identical to the
  base's. They are purely phase-channel knobs. Anyone pricing them by classical
  mismatch count will read them as free and be wrong by 1.7–6.3 nats.
* **`emitted CCX` is not a proxy for score.** The executed/emitted ratio ranges from
  0.39 to 1.00 across knobs (e.g. −456 emitted CCX came out as *+41* charged Toffoli
  on one package). Screen with emitted CCX; never *decide* with it.

The fold channel's failure rate fits `2^-(w-33) x 6.27e6 folds`, where the 33 is the
width of the pseudo-Mersenne constant `2^32 + 977`: the borrow chain has to clear the
constant's own bits before truncation can bite. So +1 bit of window halves that
channel. That is the model behind the +0.96 nats claimed for `FOLD_WINDOW 53→54`.

## 4. Q = 1263 is exactly optimal for this stream

The scored Q is `max referenced qubit id + 1`, the *allocator's* high-water mark, which
is in general strictly above what the circuit requires. What it requires is the maximum
number of wires whose reference intervals overlap at one instant: a wire is never
touched after its last reference, and the harness verifies every non-register qubit is
|0> at the end of the forward pass, so it is already |0> immediately after that last
reference. Two wires with disjoint reference intervals can therefore share one id with
no change to the circuit's action, and the minimum achievable Q is exactly the **clique
number of the interval graph**, reachable by left-edge colouring. Register qubits pin
live over the whole stream (inputs written before op 0, outputs read after the last op).

Computed on the promoted stream: `referenced_qubits 1263`, `pinned_register_qubits 512`,
**`optimal_q_renumbered 1263`, `renumber_slack 0`**. The peak is not a point but a
plateau of **10,633,288 instants** (ops 914,420 … 11,547,707 — 85% of the stream), and
at the pinning instant the live set is the *entire* id range 0..1262.

So Q=1263 is not a scheduling artefact and cannot be attacked by moving frees, by
renumbering, or by a smarter allocator. It can only be attacked by making fewer wires
coexist. That also matches the knob evidence: `SUB4_PP_PEAK` from 1266 down to **1240**
never moves realized Q off 1263 (it only makes the planner pick narrower, costlier
ladders), and neither does any value of `WALK_PEAK`, `R1`, `R1_MUL`, `R2`, or
`REPLAY_CHUNK`. Q is multiply-binding.

## 5. The depth window, and the interaction that hides the Pareto step

Scanning the full 15x15 grid `ROUNDS in 688..702` x `ROUNDS_MUL in 686..700`, Q = 1263
holds on exactly a **3x3 window**: `ROUNDS in {694,695,696}` x `ROUNDS_MUL in
{693,694,695}`. Outside it, shallower depths widen the terminal u,v
(`value_width(R-1)` grows) and deeper ones grow the tape; either way the peak goes to
>= 1264. Q never reaches 1262 anywhere in the grid.

Inside the window the two traversals have very different marginal prices — the
multiply side is the **cheapest lambda purchase in the whole circuit at 421 T/nat**,
and the divide side is the best-yielding sale at 680 T/nat. That spread is the
arbitrage. But it is masked by a Q interaction: `ROUNDS_MUL=695` alone is Q1263,
`REPLAY_FOLD_WINDOW_MUL=54` alone is Q1263, and the two **together** are Q1264. Every
package built on the multiply side dies on that. The package that survives spends the
*divide* round instead and repays with the *divide* fold window, which only fits at
Q1263 once the divide round is gone.

## 6. The Pareto step (six `set_default_env` defaults, no source logic changed)

```
SUB4_PP_ROUNDS              = 695     (was 696)
SUB4_PP_ROUNDS_MUL          = 695     (was 694)
SUB4_PP_R1                  = 334     (was 335)
SUB4_PP_R1_MUL              = 325     (was 326)
SUB4_PP_REPLAY_FOLD_WINDOW  = 54      (was 53)
SUB4_PP_REPLAY_FOLD_WINDOW_MUL = 53   (unchanged)
```

Measured paired over 48 frozen draws (433,152 shots):

| | promoted base | this |
|---|---:|---:|
| emitted charged CCX | 944,442 | 943,525 |
| charged Toffoli (paired) | — | **−375.6** |
| Q | 1263 | 1263 |
| lambda_cls | 20.750 | 20.479 |
| ph_indep | 3.958 | 3.625 |
| **lambda_eff** | **24.708** | **24.104** |

`d(lambda_cls) = −0.271 ± 0.256`, `d(ph_indep) = −0.333 ± 0.300`, so
**`d(lambda_eff) = −0.604 ± 0.395` nats**. Both axes improve: the circuit is cheaper
*and* the draw is ~1.8x more likely to be clean. It is not a failure-budget purchase,
which is why it is worth landing regardless of who lands it.

Projected score `903396 − 376 = 903020`, `x 1263 = 1,140,514,260`, i.e. **−474,888
(−0.042%)** against the live frontier.

The split points deserve a note of their own, because of *why* they were available. An
earlier note recorded `R1_MUL = 326` as "a true local minimum", from the four samples
324, 325, 326, 327. Both split-point response curves are in fact **monotone decreasing
over a long run with a periodic +250..+300 CCX spike**, and three of those four samples
are spikes. Scanned properly (R1 over 312..350, R1_MUL over 305..343, Q = 1263
throughout) the minima are (326, 323) at `ROUNDS=696` — and they **move with depth**,
to (334, 325) at `ROUNDS=695`. The split points alone leave the classical failing-shot
set bit-identical over 48 draws, so they cost no failure budget whatsoever. This is the
same lesson `cdc810e` drew about direction, one level up: **a closure is only as wide
as the samples behind it, and a jagged response needs a scan, not four probes.**

Verification: built with the two knobs baked as `set_default_env` defaults and **no
environment set**, the stream is byte-identical (`md5 d3a66d9450cfaea637ae85eb12af0520`)
to the env-driven build, `charged_emitted 943525`, `qubits 1263`. On the inherited
nonce it reports 14 classical mismatches and 11 phase-garbage batches — the normal
unground-draw signature, not breakage. No harness file is modified.

## 7. Dead ends, re-derived with numbers rather than inherited

Each of these is priced against the accounting in §2, so the arithmetic is checkable.

* **Lazy / unreduced coefficient arithmetic.** Deferring the mod-p fold for k rounds
  caps the growth at k bits, but reducing a k-bit overflow costs ~k conditional
  subtracts of the pseudo-Mersenne constant — exactly what k per-round folds cost.
  **Reduction work is conserved.** Wash at every k, not just at the k the older note
  tried.
* **Width tapering of the replay.** Dead on inspection: the recurrence runs on
  `(coefficient, numerator)` and the *numerator* is a full 256-bit residue from round
  0, so no early round is narrow.
* **Jump-divstep / transition-matrix injection.** Track the small matrix instead and
  inject the numerator once. Injecting a k-bit quantum scalar into a 256-bit register
  costs ~255 T per bit of k, i.e. **510 T per round of k for the two rows**, against
  **380 T for a replay round**. Always negative, for every k. This is the reversible
  inversion of the classical tradeoff: word multiplication is free in hardware and
  quadratic here.
* **Jacobian / projective coordinates.** One inversion traversal is 425,980 T; one
  modular multiplication is ~50,000 T. **An inversion is worth only ~8.5
  multiplications here**, so mixed Jacobian addition (7M+4S) plus a final affine
  conversion prices at ~1.13M T against 903k, and needs a Z register on top.
  Affine-with-two-inversions is genuinely the right formula family — the usual
  classical intuition (inversion ~ 80–100 mults) is inverted.
* **Fermat inversion.** ~306 modular multiplications ~ 15M T. Not close.
* **Conditional-swap recurrences (Bernstein–Yang divstep and relatives).** Removing one
  ping-pong round is worth `4 x W + 2 x 337 ~ 1,234` charged Toffoli (and zero Q inside
  the depth window). A data-dependent conditional swap must act on the (f,g) walk pair
  *and* the 256-bit coefficient pair, forward and reverse: `2 x 140 + 2 x 256 ~ 792` T
  per round. **Break-even is therefore 0.64 rounds saved per conditional-swap round.**
  Bernstein–Yang's 590 iterations against ping-pong's 695 is 105 rounds saved over 590
  swap rounds = **0.178** — it loses by 3.6x. Ping-pong's parity alternation buys its
  swaps for free and that is the whole reason it wins.
  **Reopen condition, stated as a number so it can be checked against a candidate:** a
  GCD-family recurrence needs to save **> 0.64 rounds per conditional-swap round**, or
  reduce `sum_r W_r` (currently 96,931 per pass) at fixed round count. That is a
  number-theory question, not a port.
* **Renumbering / free-scheduling for Q.** Closed by construction in §4.
* **The knob surface.** Swept every `SUB4_*` and every square-path `TLM_*`: the square
  family (`LADDER` 120..400, `CHUNK_MIN`, `A_MAT`, `C_MAT`, `B_LOCAL_K2`,
  `KARATSUBA2`, the four `*_MIN` thresholds) is either a no-op or worse; the booleans
  are all at their optimum (any flip raises Q or CCX); `LATE_REPLAY_WALK_W=0` is
  optimal; `R2` is flat over 620..655 and Q-lethal at 660. Note that most booleans are
  presence-gated (`is_some()`), so `KNOB=0` still counts as *set* — `PP_LOAN_ONE=0` and
  `=1` both give Q1276.
  One near-miss for the record: `SIGN1_RESPEND=1` is −755 emitted CCX for +1 Q,
  i.e. ~+148 T-equivalent. Closest thing to a win in the boolean space, and still
  negative.

The only bounded engineering target left is the **square, 50,210 T (5.6%)**. A Toom-3
or better product register would have to beat the level-2 Karatsuba already shipped;
an earlier note measured Karatsuba-2 sub-square duplication as a loss, and the upside
is bounded at ~1.5% of score even if the square improved 25%.

## 8. The compute wall, quantified

At `lambda_eff ≈ 24.1–24.7`, `P(clean) ≈ 2–3e-11`, so a clean draw needs **~4–5e10
draws**. The cheapest possible screen is an exact classical walk model with early abort
at the first failing shot: the per-shot walk failure rate is `16.5 / 9024 = 1.8e-3`, so
a draw aborts after ~547 shots, and at the ~16 us/shot an exact 320-bit walk model
costs that is **~9 ms per draw**. Ten cores therefore deliver ~1.1e4 draws/s ~ 1e9/day,
which is **~50 days per clean nonce** — and that is with a screener I have not built.
With the simulator alone (measured: 12.1 s per aborted draw, 85% of it the reference
scalar multiplications) it is ~7,000 years.

So the frontier is **compute-gated, not idea-gated**, and has been since roughly the
Q1266 era. That is worth saying out loud because it changes what a contribution looks
like: circuit findings and grind capacity have come apart, and a finding worth 0.04%
now sits idle unless it reaches someone with a GPU screener. The configuration in §6 is
verified, baked, and free for the taking.

For anyone building that screener, the two numbers that matter: it needs to reproduce
the walk with **zero false rejections** against the frozen simulator (validate on the
failing-shot *sets*, not the counts — my rig dumps them per draw for exactly this), and
the residual after a walk-clean draw is `24.1 − 16.5 = 7.6` nats, so expect ~2,000
walk-clean survivors per clean draw, each needing a full 9,024-shot verify at ~15 s.

## 9. Method notes for whoever picks this up

* Price nothing on a single draw. Every fresh draw of this circuit shows 13–32
  classical mismatches; that is the *base rate*, not breakage. Breakage presents as
  ~9,024.
* Price nothing on emitted CCX (§3, third bullet).
* Judge a knob by the **paired failing-shot set**, not by mean counts. Most knobs here
  leave it bit-identical, and that is a much stronger statement than "no significant
  difference at 24 draws".
* Re-optimize the schedule parameters after *any* depth change: the split-point optima
  moved by 8 and 2 rounds for a single round of depth (§6).
* A knob's closure is only as wide as the samples behind it, and both directions and
  the *shape* of the response matter. Two notes in a row have now been reopened on
  exactly this.

Feedback for platform developers: `ecdsafail notes` was the natural home for a
negative-result-plus-instrument write-up like this one; with it removed and
Discussions disabled on the benchmark, a finding that does not itself clear the
frontier has no channel at all. A read-only research-note channel, decoupled from
submission validation, would keep results like §4 and §7 out of the bin.
