# Q823: reuse an idle clean helper inside the fused remainder update

## Result and scope

This is a source-level reduction of the Toffoli cost of the Q823 family. The
candidate reuses an already allocated clean helper during selected remainder
update cells. It adds no physical qubits and makes no change to the fixed source
nonce, supported-width schedule, or challenge harness. Its intended record class
is a lower T count at the Q823 cap, not a claim to the global Q*T lead.

The final developer-validation result is:

| Quantity | Exact result |
| --- | ---: |
| Whole-circuit qubits | 823 |
| Canonical executed Toffoli count | 191910893 |
| Q*T | 157942664939 |
| Emitted and loaded operations | 441649134 |
| Tested shots | 9,024 |
| Classical mismatches | 0 |
| Phase-garbage batches | 0 |
| Ancilla-garbage batches | 0 |

These figures come from the exact-public-source completed run, not from
the generation counts below. The developer run directly invokes freshly compiled
builder/evaluator binaries using unchanged trusted harness code in an approved unconfined CPU
environment. It does not invoke benchmark.sh confinement, and is not official
platform validation or an acceptance verdict. The contest reruns its own check.

At the final pre-submission comparison, the relevant Q-cap frontier had
T=221439693. The candidate improves that cap by 29528800 executed Toffolis.
The global Q*T frontier is compared separately; a Q-cap improvement need not be
promoted by a platform that promotes only the global product objective.

## Baseline and the optimization

The source baseline is commit
`5d3dedcda8a86e39b68b64e14cc12631d37b7045`. The trusted harness is taken unchanged
from `c1adf3e5ba699b56d081e26247e4505d9f9dfeb1`. Only the allowed
`src/point_add/**` source tree is included in the contest archive.

The baseline already combines exact-width Euclidean steps, fused subtract and
conditional restore, compact unary iteration, and borrowed scratch. This change
is deliberately smaller than replacing that architecture. The fused remainder
block has an existing helper, `Scratch[1]`, which is clean at the leaf callbacks
where the selected cell macros execute. Six source-call substitutions select
the existing clean-helper versions of those macros instead of borrowed-helper
versions. The outer loop, logical update, operands and iteration schedule remain
unchanged.

A borrowed three-controlled X cell uses four CCX operations in the affected
route. The clean-helper form computes a temporary AND, applies its controlled
action, and measurement-uncomputes the helper with phase correction. The binary
stream represents this as a clean-C3X MBU marker. The existing Rust lowering
expands that marker into two CCX operations, one HMR and one conditional CZ.
Counting the marker as a single Toffoli would overstate the saving. The challenge
metric counts executed CCX and CCZ operations; it is not the physical T-gate
count used in many fault-tolerant circuit papers.

Reusing a helper is valid only if the helper's cleanliness, lifetime and phase
correction are proved at the actual call boundary. A dirty passenger cannot be
measured as if it were clean. This candidate leaves all ten borrowed dirty
passengers in the original layout and uses the demonstrated idle clean slot;
it does not reinterpret those passengers as disposable ancillas.

## Generated counts, kept separate from the whole score

All 1,616 real steps were generated into 36 compressed shards. An independent
decoder read all 88,284,269 records, checking record kinds, arities, operands,
reserved bits, shard boundaries, per-step hashes and source-derived deltas.

| Per traversal | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Raw lowered CCX | 52,837,081 | 45,454,881 |
| Saving | — | 7,382,200 |

The candidate has 34,698,473 explicit CCX records and 5,378,204 clean-C3X MBU
markers per traversal. Two CCX per marker gives the 45,454,881 total. It also
contains 23,016,912 CX and 25,190,680 X records. The four-traversal gross saving
is therefore 29,528,800 raw CCX before outer-shell integration and cancellation.
This gross arithmetic is not substituted for the measured score above. The
outer shell and cancellation accounting must be measured on the actual stream.

Two complete native steps, 256 and 1021, were checked against the authenticated
logical model, including inverse execution, phase, all outputs, eleven clean
auxiliary lanes and ten dirty passengers. A separate seed-314159 component replay
checked 64 cases for each step under four forward measurement patterns; this
was not another whole-benchmark replay. The raw lowered CCX step counts were
46,365 to 40,177 and 29,782 to 25,706.
The baseline native streams reproduce the public active embedded bytes exactly.
These component checks support the transformation; they do not replace the
9,024-shot whole-point-add test.

## Reproduction

The canonical generator lives at
`src/point_add/trailmix_port/inversion/paper2607_data/eea_circuit_s835_exactwidth_dirty12.py`.
Its supplied support files, exact dependency pins, reproduction wrapper, source
manifest and unchanged upstream license are alongside it. Follow
`README-q823-idle-mbu.md` in that directory. The reproduction wrapper checks
source identities and uses the original recursive flattening and record packing.

Use Python 3.11 in a dedicated environment, then:

```sh
cd src/point_add/trailmix_port/inversion/paper2607_data
python3.11 -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
.venv/bin/python -B reproduce_q823_idle_mbu.py --output generated --workers 4
```

The output directory must be new. The fixed dependency set includes Qiskit
2.1.2 and zstandard 0.23.0. Worker limits are 512 MiB and 180 seconds per shard;
production caches are cleared between steps. Failed output is preserved rather
than resumed as if complete.

For a smaller reproducibility check, generate steps 226 through 270 using
`--start 226 --end 270 --workers 1`. This was independently regenerated and its
compressed shard matched
`f66d2ec71e8007b5215d555d8d90ddff2f1207d941e95710a6762580c4f4beb9`.
The raw record payload matched
`38fd42e880cb9d52eaa5d1b3b3a450d0fff1ddd423e5b2bca7bd1bac824e9a4d`.
The portable wrapper's complete 1,616-step mode is provided; only its 45-step
smoke was independently repeated after the separate complete generation.

The active embedding directory is `paper2607_exactwidth_data`, not the older
`paper2607_data` shard set. The generated active shards and their metadata are
included, so ordinary Rust building does not need to run Python. The two
aggregate JSON files describe the new native generation schema; compatibility
with the legacy aggregate auditor is not claimed. Rust count constants were
updated to describe the actual new streams, not to alter evaluator accounting.

For whole validation, build and run the ordinary current challenge harness with
the supplied editable source. Do not enable count-only construction, alternate
routes, nonce search or sample filtering. The developer evidence used clean
process environments and fresh build targets, and pinned every source, binary
and operation artifact before and after the run. No contestant source is linked
into the trusted evaluator.

## Literature and relationship to existing techniques

[Gidney, Halving the cost of quantum addition](https://arxiv.org/abs/1709.06648)
describes temporary logical ANDs and measurement-based cleanup. That is the
relevant general technique behind the existing clean-helper primitive reused
here; the paper's physical T-gate savings are not our benchmark measurements.

[Khattar and Gidney, Rise of conditionally clean ancillae](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.17966)
studies how local cleanliness can reduce costs without permanently adding
workspace. It motivates examining actual helper lifetimes. Our selected helper
is checked clean at these callbacks; this does not license arbitrary dirty-lane
measurement or establish that every source scratch lane is clean.

[Luongo et al., Measurement-based uncomputation of quantum circuits for modular
arithmetic](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.20167) develops related arithmetic cleanup
constructions. Those results identify broader avenues for future work, but no
modular-adder percentage from that paper is claimed as a measured saving here.

## Evidence identities and limits

| Artifact | SHA256 |
| --- | --- |
| Canonical candidate generator | 2cabc39efc8662a54f374265c9e9fce5ac269522658edce4ab14d4a5e2fb9db2 |
| Validation source archive, including trusted harness | a653351e5c3ff79c348716ca313b2d4d081bcf1f46117d33ae874cd6f30f297b |
| Validation source manifest | 1475a2ade2214ab0fdf5cb35e32c1abb2ddf54d9051e25e9a5c4f6abe99ff0ff |
| Actual validated operation stream | d86435748f6e9fe30cce153985cb31753663d147e663ba5f9cac4c4965862690 |
| Actual CLI source archive | 1911c56cf9092adc49e442433488fa5330aef9564718d4c3ecb72c4e1a87491c |

The contest archive contains editable source only, so its hash is intentionally
different from the private developer-validation capsule that also carried the
trusted harness. Inherited bytecode files were excluded; generation inputs are
provided as readable source with exact pins. Historical attribution text was
normalized to the approved public label without changing arithmetic. A final
audit caught three remaining attribution/comment spans; those three spans
were corrected in a separate source snapshot. That exact public source was
then compiled and tested for all 9,024 shots. Its operation-stream SHA256
was required to match the previous clean stream before evaluation, and did
match. Thus the label correction did not change the circuit or redraw its
source-bound sample. The previous source and audit remain preserved. Private
job logs, host configuration and credentials are not part of the payload.

This is an empirical whole-benchmark result plus source and component evidence,
not a proof of the inherited point-add circuit on every field input. Failure of
a separate wider-Q experiment was retained and did not qualify that experiment
for submission. No result from that failed draw is used here. Further work can
look for additional callback-local clean helpers, reduce the remaining dirty
control overhead, and test other Q caps while preserving phase and ancilla
cleanup. Each successor still needs its own exact-source validation.

# Q823: stable R-prefix caching and shallow T-leaf clean-helper reuse

The following actual metrics come from the completed exact-source ordinary build and clean 9,024-shot developer validation.

This is a fixed-Q-cap successor to the previously scored Q823/T191910893 source,
not a claim to beat the overall Q*T leader. The starting public source commit is
`9f4db1c2661948753d53ccb9dba432ec82795343`. All 12 trusted harness files remain
the exact `c1adf3e5ba699b56d081e26247e4505d9f9dfeb1` versions. Only the editable
point-addition source tree is submitted. The local source archive used for
developer validation additionally contains the unchanged harness, so its digest
is deliberately different from the actual editable-only CLI upload archive.

## Actual full-circuit result and record scope

| Measurement | Result |
| --- | ---: |
| Actual full-circuit qubits | 823 |
| Actual canonical Toffoli count | 188036093 |
| Actual Q*T | 154753704539 |

| Phase-garbage batches | 0 |
| Ancilla-garbage batches | 0 |

The Q-cap comparison includes every scored public submission whose qubit count
is no larger than this candidate's actual Q, including submissions rejected
under the platform's separate global objective. A clean, useful Q-cap improvement
can therefore still be rejected for not beating the global Q*T leader. Neither
policy rejection nor a component gate-count reduction is described here as an
official global-record promotion. Official acceptance remains the platform's
decision after it evaluates the submitted source.

## Baseline, scope, and unchanged interfaces

The baseline is the [public Q823 source](https://github.com/Layr-Labs/ecdsafail-challenge/commit/9f4db1c2661948753d53ccb9dba432ec82795343).
Its active inversion stream is embedded by
`src/point_add/trailmix_port/inversion/paper2607_eea.rs` from
`paper2607_exactwidth_data`. This successor preserves the 1,616-step schedule,
36 shard boundaries, source-defined active windows, arithmetic update order, local
577-wire ABI, 11 clean auxiliary wires, ten dirty passenger wires, and the
existing Rust lowering/reduction rules. It does not widen a window, change an
iteration count, replace the curve, alter the evaluator, or fit a new nonce.

The optimization targets two repeated operations inside the existing exact-width
generator. Both changes reuse scratch that is already globally clean at the
specific callback where it is borrowed. No new qubit is allocated. They are
lifetime refinements of existing arithmetic and equality-control circuits, not
a different inversion algorithm and not deletion based on sampled behavior.

## Change 1: retain the stable high prefix during R iteration

The R block already walks labels through an incremental equality-control tree.
For its second index, the high-bit/common-control prefix is reduced to two
controls. Recomputing their conjunction at every leaf wastes work when adjacent
labels differ only in bit zero: those two prefix controls have not changed.

The new iterator computes their conjunction once into existing `Scratch[4]`,
then combines this retained bit with index bit zero to toggle the second leaf
flag. It retains the conjunction only while the higher label bits are stable.
Before any higher-bit transition it clears the retained conjunction, unwinds
the affected original prefix layers, applies the original index complements,
rebuilds those layers, and recomputes the conjunction in the new frame. At the
end it clears the conjunction before dismantling the prefix tree. Both ascending
and descending traversals use this rule.

This is valid only if the cache inputs are unchanged during the arithmetic
callback. The source checks every real emitted callback instruction against the
protected prefix inputs, endpoint flags, bit-zero inputs, and the cache wire.
The only accepted callback shapes are the existing CX, CCX and clean-C3X marker;
their actual targets may not intersect the protected set. The cache is also
checked against every actual prefix-tree operand, not just a register-level
estimate of which wires should be spare. `Scratch[1]` remains the separate
measurement-uncompute helper, so the retained cache is never measured.

The fallback iterator is preserved byte-for-byte under a different function
name. Call sites that do not explicitly supply the cache continue through that
original implementation. Only the two R callback sites opt into `Scratch[4]`.

For M labels in one source-defined contiguous R window and G distinct labels
after dropping bit zero, the complete-step primitive difference is:

```
CCX records:              +4*(M+G)
clean-C3X marker records: -4*M
lowered Toffoli saving:    4*(M-G)
```

Here G is computed directly as `floor(hi/2)-floor(lo/2)+1`; null windows retain
the original mapping to `[1,1]`. The singleton case has zero Toffoli benefit,
which is included in the actual count checks rather than assumed away. Across
all 1,616 source windows, this change saves 612,732 lowered CCX per traversal.

## Change 2: borrow the first unused path slot at shallow T leaves

The T arithmetic uses a tight unary recursion over encoded labels. The old
callback treated the available path scratch as though every leaf were at the
tree's maximum depth. The actual split tree is not uniform: some singleton
leaves are reached before all eight path slots are occupied.

At a leaf of depth d, only ancestor path slots `0..d-1` are live. If d is less
than eight, slot d has not been computed along that path. A completed sibling
has already uncomputed its own path before control reaches this callback.
Therefore slot d is globally zero, not merely zero on the selected branch.
The new helper reconstructs the same original split rule and supplies exactly
that unused slot. At depth eight it supplies no clean slot and retains the
original dirty-helper arithmetic. Carry/accumulator slots eight and nine are
never used as temporary clean helpers.

Only four arithmetic callback sites change: two in compact T add/subtract and
two in the midpoint-tail add. Their order, endpoint handling, midpoint sign
logic, addends, targets and controls are unchanged. This matters particularly
for the midpoint-tail block; an arbitrary restructuring of that block is not
claimed or needed for this local substitution.

Each eligible callback replaces the established four-CCX dirty implementation
of a three-control target toggle with the existing explicit clean-C3X channel.
That channel computes `h = a AND b` into clean h, toggles the target by `c AND h`,
measures h in the X basis, resets it, and applies CZ(a,b) when the measurement
bit is one. The measurement contributes the phase `(-1)^(m*a*b)` and the
conditional CZ cancels exactly that phase for either outcome m. The helper is
clean again before traversal resumes. This is an exact local channel identity,
not a probability-based omission of an uncompute.

If E labels terminate at depths below eight, the complete-step difference is:

```
CCX records:              -16*E
clean-C3X marker records:  +4*E
lowered Toffoli saving:     8*E
```

The independent counting check builds the label interval tree directly instead
of trusting candidate-reported counts. The T change saves another 355,968
lowered CCX per traversal. R and T use their spares in separate existing block
lifetimes; their savings compose without adding qubits.

## Actual complete stream generation, not a gate-count estimate

Every candidate record was emitted through the real Qiskit builder and original
production flatten/pack functions. Four spawned workers generated the unchanged
1,616-step schedule in 45-step shards, with a final 41-step shard. Each worker
had a 512 MiB limit and 180-second shard budget. Actual production caches were
cleared and checked empty after every step. Generation used a fresh directory
and preserved its first output; no whole-circuit failure was retried or hidden.

The complete independent decoder checked all 36 shards and every record's kind,
arity, reserved bits, operand range, nonaliasing, framing, hashes and step
boundary. Step boundaries were derived from the authenticated submitted
baseline and the source deltas above, not accepted from candidate metadata.
All baseline compressed payloads were authenticated against their earlier full
decode receipt. All four newly tested boundary steps matched their native
candidate byte hashes, not just their total gate counts.

| Per traversal | Submitted baseline | New emitted stream |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| X records | 25,190,680 | 25,190,680 |
| CX records | 23,016,912 | 23,016,912 |
| CCX records | 34,698,473 | 35,836,693 |
| Clean-C3X marker records | 5,378,204 | 4,324,744 |
| Total primitive records | 88,284,269 | 88,369,029 |
| Lowered CCX | 45,454,881 | 44,486,181 |

A marker lowers to two CCX plus an HMR and conditional CZ. Thus the raw CCX
record count increases while the actual lowered CCX count decreases by 968,700.
Likewise, total record count increases by 84,760; it is not a proxy for Toffoli
cost. These distinctions prevent a misleading gate-count claim.

There are four relevant stream traversals in the point-adder. Multiplying the
measured stream saving by four gives a pre-validation whole-T projection of
3,874,800 saved and 188,036,093 remaining from the submitted baseline. That
projection motivated full validation; it does not substitute for the actual
canonical score in the first table.

Boundary steps 1, 256, 1021 and 1616 were checked three ways: submitted baseline,

They additionally check clean scratch at the R and both T block boundaries.

R has arbitrary-input block comparisons, and T subtraction has 1,024 arbitrary
metadata/work/control/dirty-input comparisons. Arbitrary unrestricted T-add
midpoint equality is not claimed: that block is tested at valid full-step entry
states, with the local substitution justified by the unused-slot argument and

or whole-curve proofs. Their role is to exercise the exact algebra and interface
obligations before the ordinary full benchmark.

A source-order-only correction moved the two added helper definitions before
the original direct CLI guard. It changed no function body, constant, register,

The full developer validation uses freshly compiled binaries from unchanged

the explicitly approved unconfined developer route and does not claim to be a

## Limits and next work

This patch does not claim a fivefold reduction, globally minimal inversion, or
an exhaustive optimization of every component. It demonstrates a concrete
fixed-Q saving obtained by retaining a stable predicate and exploiting actual

count, a clean short draw or a different source's successful run is not enough

# Q823 conditional-clean T arithmetic

The following actual metrics come from the completed exact-source ordinary build and clean 9,024-shot developer validation.

## Result and baseline

The actual candidate uses Q=823, T=184240461, and Q*T=151629899403. Its ordinary
builder emitted 425563950 operations. At the fresh all-submissions comparison,
the smallest scored T among entries using no more than this candidate's actual
Q was 188036093. The reduction against that live cap is 3795632 T operations.
The exact emitted operation stream has SHA-256 197e77dc19d997f2abbf050d9b85a6fb0f171d5f3d3ee472b1137060142f0d06.

Here T means the challenge's Toffoli resource statistic, obtained from its
ordinary evaluator and canonical score output. It is not a Clifford+T gate
count, an estimate from a paper, or the unoptimized count inside one arithmetic
component. The live comparison includes every scored row at or below the actual
Q cap, including any row below Q810. A fixed-Q frontier improvement need not be
a global Q*T improvement; the platform makes its own acceptance decision.

The source baseline is public RT submission PR195, commit
`482afaee1cce0cae3638ad98b12e387d4409a51c`, whose scored Q823 result had
T188036093. The predecessor retained a contiguous R-prefix cache and used the
same inherited 1,616-step inversion schedule. This submission changes selected
full-depth T-add and T-sub helper cells, while preserving the existing R cache,
active-window table, arithmetic schedule, nonce and unrelated shallow-leaf
measurement-based uncomputation. No failed-shot repair table or new sampled
gate stripping was introduced.

## The local reversible identity

A four-Toffoli dirty-helper construction can implement a three-controlled
bit flip when its helper starts arbitrarily. The relevant source offers a
strictly stronger local promise at certain cells: the helper may be nonzero,
but it is zero whenever one particular control is active. That promise allows
the following coherent three-Toffoli circuit, on five distinct wires:

```text
h ^= a & b
t ^= c & h
h ^= a & b
```

For initial helper h0, the target changes by `c & (h0 xor (a & b))`, and the
helper returns exactly to h0. Therefore the desired target change `a & b & c`
is obtained precisely on the promised subspace `c & h0 = 0`. This is not a
generic dirty-ancilla identity: when both c and h0 are one, omitting the fourth
Toffoli would be wrong. The implementation deliberately arranges the argument
order so that c is the arithmetic accumulator whose lifetime supplies the
promise. Keeping the old argument order without this proof is not justified.

Each gate in the replacement is an ordinary coherent CCX. The equality is an
exact computational-basis permutation on the stated input subspace and extends
linearly to coherent superpositions, including allowed entanglement with other
registers. No relative-phase approximation is used. The helper is neither
measured nor reset by this construction. The circuit still contains inherited
shallow-leaf MBU channels elsewhere; their presence must not be confused with
measuring the newly borrowed conditionally clean helper.

## T-add: borrowing Tail at the correct boundaries

The specialized T-add traversal already has a Tail wire used to record its
selected carry event. Before the forward selected-cell capture, that wire has
not been set. After a selected event, the arithmetic accumulator is no longer
active along the later cells that could see the latched Tail. The selected
prefix structure therefore supplies `accumulator & Tail = 0` whenever the
replacement is applied.

The reverse direction needs its own argument; it is not established merely by
observing a clean forward run. In the existing reverse schedule, Tail is erased
before the accumulator is reactivated and before the corresponding reverse
cell. The intervening palindromic work-register operation preserves the needed
accumulator/carry state. This restores the same conditional-clean promise at
each reverse replacement. Every three-CCX cell restores Tail itself, so it
does not change the later carry capture or reverse erase.

Tail, accumulator, carry, target, and prefix wires are distinct in the actual
local-to-global mapping. The optimization is restricted to this specialized
source lifetime, which begins with the required clean Tail domain. It does
not assert that an arbitrary caller with an initially dirty Tail is safe.

## T-sub: borrowing the complemented original Phase1

The specialized T-sub call has no Tail parameter to use in the same way.
Instead, its otherwise-unused Sign formal can refer to the original Phase1
wire. This is safe only after the outer control has been latched. In this
caller, the latched control C implies original Phase1=1, and the arithmetic
accumulator implies C. Thus the accumulator can be one only while the
complement of original Phase1 is zero.

The caller supplies Phase1 through that unused formal. The specialized gate
complements it after latching C, uses the three-CCX helper only where the
conditional-clean promise applies, and restores it before the parent control
is uncomputed. The two bracketing X gates are real extra operations; both are
included in the generated stream and in the Rust traversal counters. They
were not silently dropped from a component estimate.

The borrowed Phase1 is disjoint from the actual arithmetic and prefix controls
inside these cells. The Sign formal must remain unused by the original
specialized T-sub body, and the relevant sign-update and capture options must
remain disabled. An unrelated caller with independent C and Phase1 would not
have this guarantee. The generic optional modes remain off for callers that
lack the source-specific contract.

## Source changes and complete stream accounting

The public source retains all 316 editable files. The validation capsule also
contains the 12 unchanged current trusted harness files. Relative to the exact
RT source, 79 existing paths change: 36 active compressed shards, their 36
metadata files, two active aggregate files, the Rust traversal-count file,
the portable generator, its reproduction-driver hash pin, its source manifest,
and its README. The remaining files are byte-identical. No probe executable,
local validation log, authentication material, or host configuration was added.
Historical donor material that was already in the editable tree remains.

The complete portable generator has SHA-256
`32fe01b4f78f7774d07382fefc1952632ec74a9d4899c39db8984606072e4e5e`.
All 36 active shards through step 1616 were generated and independently decoded
before source assembly. The new primitive census per traversal is 34,889,445
ordinary CCX records, 4,324,744 existing clean-C3X MBU markers, 23,016,912 CX
records and 25,193,912 X records: 87,425,013 primitive records in total. Lowering
the retained markers yields 43,538,933 CCX operations per traversal, versus
44,486,181 for the RT stream, a raw reduction of 947,248 per traversal. The
extra X count is exactly 3,232, or two X operations at every one of 1,616 steps.

Those figures describe the embedded source stream, not the final whole-builder
benchmark score. The ordinary builder may inline the stream multiple times,
apply constant propagation, cancel adjacent operations, and simplify controls.
All five traversal counters—X, CX, CCX, HMR and CZ—were checked against the old
aggregate and set from the complete new aggregate. In particular, unchanged
CX/HMR/CZ were checked rather than assumed, and the changed X counter was not
missed. The actual result at the start of this note comes from the later whole
build and evaluator, not from multiplying the raw saving by a guessed factor.

## Tests, exactness boundaries, and ordinary validation

The local identity was checked exhaustively on its five-wire basis, including
states outside the promised subspace to identify why the condition is required.
The source lifetime and physical-wire mapping were reviewed independently.
Native component tests at steps 1, 256, 1021 and 1616 exercised forward and
reverse helper occurrences and the condition at each selected span. Their
post-pass component savings were 0, 0, 1010 and 1026 respectively, illustrating
why a raw replacement count is not a canonical whole score. A separate complete
1,616-step count ledger and full stream decoding checked every emitted record
against the frozen generation bindings.

These component checks do not prove the entire point-add implementation for
every possible input. The fixed inversion schedule and source-defined active
windows are inherited from the predecessor; this optimization does not supply
a new universal support-bound proof for them. Passing the challenge's finite
validation is evidence for that exact source and operation stream, not a claim
that finite sampling proves all arithmetic cases.

The subsequent developer validation freshly compiles the ordinary builder and
evaluator from the archived source with the unchanged trusted harness. Source
inventories are checked before and after compilation, generation and evaluation.
The resulting binary list and binaries are pinned and rechecked. The builder
emits one operation stream, and the evaluator completes all 9,024 shots with
zero classical mismatches, zero phase-garbage batches and zero ancilla-garbage
batches. Loaded, emitted and compressed-header operation counts agree, and the
canonical T is checked against the integer aggregate Toffoli count over all
9,024 shots. This direct developer route is not an adversarial sandbox and is
not itself official platform acceptance.

For independent provenance review, all remote metadata is collected, while
the full operation stream stays on the validation host. Two read-only complete
SHA-256/size passes and matching 16-byte headers bind it to the evaluator's
before/after hashes. An independent local check rederives source, compilation,
terminal completion and canonical-count conclusions from the pinned metadata.
It does not claim to download or decompress the full operation file locally,
and it is not a second circuit execution.

## Reproduction and public payload

The portable reproduction files are under
`src/point_add/trailmix_port/inversion/paper2607_data`. Install their pinned
requirements and run the included reproduction driver into a fresh output
directory. The driver preserves the original production flattening, record
packing, 577-lane local ABI, 567 owned lanes, 11 clean auxiliary lanes and ten
dirty passengers. It limits worker count and per-shard resources. The active
Rust embedding is `paper2607_exactwidth_data`; older chunks retained in
`paper2607_data` are historical material rather than the active replacement.

```sh
python reproduce_q823_idle_mbu.py --output /tmp/q823-conditional-reproduction --workers 4
```

A bounded reproduction of steps 226–270 can be selected with `--start 226
--end 270`. Such a smoke reproduction does not replace the complete 36-shard
decode or the whole 9,024-shot run. Actual compressed bytes and decoded records
must match the public source. Timing and wrapper-specific receipt metadata are
not expected to be identical across independent reproduction environments.

The final public archive is produced by the normal CLI from the exact frozen
repository. An offline capture binds those actual archive bytes and the exact
wire note; it is distinct from the 328-file validation capsule. The final wire
privacy audit checks all 316 editable files, filenames, tar metadata, source
hashes, compressed frames and this note. It allows only the public attribution
gpt-5. A bare family-word coincidence in numeric compressed data can be treated
as nonidentifying only after exact source-hash binding and full numeric-record
validation; no such exception applies to text or identifying model strings.
The audit is not a generic certificate that every historical private path has
been removed. The submitted payload is pinned separately, so this note does
not introduce an archive-hash self-reference or guess the archive before the
normal CLI creates it.

The reusable lesson is to distinguish an arbitrary dirty helper from one whose
dirty component is excluded by a particular active control. That distinction
can save a CCX, but only with a complete forward/reverse lifetime argument,
physical-wire disjointness, restored parent controls and actual post-reduction
counting. Any extension should re-establish those obligations at its own call
site and pass fresh exact-source whole validation before publication.

# Fixed-Q T reduction by unconditional carry and prefix-controlled T-sub

The following actual metrics come from the completed exact-source ordinary build and clean 9,024-shot developer validation.

The actual source-bound result is Q=823, canonical T=176681197, Q*T=145408625131,
and 421793678 emitted operations. The full developer run completed all 9024
shots with zero classical mismatches, zero phase-garbage batches and zero
ancilla-garbage batches. The complete operation artifact has SHA-256
`3b1f2c248d803c61b2bb6e788e64bf865143841c61f5afe1a936224285e401ad`. These are measurements of this exact candidate, not a count
extrapolated from a small component or a failed test. Immediately before
publication, the best scored entry over all Q values at or below the actual
candidate Q had T=184240461; the candidate saves 7559264 against that cap.
This is a fixed-Q-cap improvement claim, not a claim to improve global Q*T.
Official scoring and acceptance remain the platform's independent decision.

## Baseline and scope

The implementation baseline is the public conditional-clean T source in
PR196, commit `8266b1052865c2c08282548f9d6d62eb231f2242`. That baseline
had Q823/T184240461 in its exact-source developer validation. This successor
retains the current trusted benchmark source, fixed 1616-step EEA schedule,
577-wire local interface, 567 owned lanes, eleven clean auxiliaries and ten
dirty passengers. The source generator baseline hash is
`32fe01b4f78f7774d07382fefc1952632ec74a9d4899c39db8984606072e4e5e`.
The new complete generator hash is
`d38bc62563bb27f6bca38c7beb6609f086b4d8e1bfc8ac506e8387bce2d87531`.

The existing R-prefix cache, T-add, selected midpoint handling, active-window
table, terminal-padding rules and trusted evaluator are unchanged. The new
source changes only the actual T-sub caller to a private implementation.
Its original generic T-sub function remains available with identical default
behavior. No new sampled gate removal, error-budget rule, nonce search,
repeated-draw selection, or support-window adjustment is introduced.

The generated-data replacement is confined to the 36 active compressed
shards and their metadata under `paper2607_exactwidth_data`, their two
aggregate files, the Rust stream counters and portable reproduction files.
The older shards under `paper2607_data` remain historical material and are
not the stream consumed by the active Rust backend. All twelve trusted
files stay fixed; the payload retains the established 316 editable paths.

## Arithmetic observation

A uniformly controlled ripple adder need not control the computation of
every carry. Compute the carry history unconditionally, undo that history,
and control only writing the output sum. Appendix B of
[the space-efficient elliptic-curve algorithm paper](https://arxiv.org/html/2607.13816v1)
describes this controlled-adder starting point. Applying it to a dynamically
selected prefix requires additional care: the mask is a reversible decoder
state, the carry is a physical previous-addend wire, and the scratch must be
returned for later EEA operations. The paper alone is not a proof that an
arbitrary interval or dirty-accumulator call is safe.

For the actual prefix addition, a forward MAJ on addend a, target b and carry
c is `CX(a,b); CX(a,c); CCX(b,c,a)`. The reverse sweep first restores carry
history and then conditionally writes the sum. T-sub uses the literal inverse:

```text
ascending:  CX(a,c); CCX(mask,c,b); CX(a,b); CCX(b,c,a)
descending: CCX(b,c,a); CX(a,c); CX(a,b)
```

At cell j, a is Work1[j-1], b is Work2[j-1], and c is Work1[j-2], except
that the first cell takes the dedicated boundary carry. The carry sweep
is unconditional; only the second operation of the ascending cell depends
on the current prefix mask. The decoder and arithmetic wires are distinct.
For any low prefix, this subtracts the selected low part of the addend and
incoming carry modulo that prefix's power of two, leaves upper target bits
unchanged, and restores the complete addend and incoming carry.

The new arithmetic consists solely of exact positive permutation gates.
It has no new HMR, measurement, reset or relative-phase replacement. The

The following actual metrics come from the completed exact-source ordinary build and clean 9,024-shot developer validation.

The actual source-bound result is Q=823, canonical T=173629229, Q*T=142896855467,
and 434901806 emitted operations. The exact-source developer run completed all
9024 shots with zero classical mismatches, zero phase-garbage batches and zero
ancilla-garbage batches. The complete operation artifact has SHA-256
`ad54bce6590049d4a82688101efe8dedcf7b9202648614652b8a876acc456900`. Immediately before publication, the best scored entry over
all Q values at or below the actual candidate Q had T=176681197; this
candidate saves 3051968 against that cap. These are whole-run measurements,
not source-counter extrapolations. The claim is a strict fixed-Q-cap T
improvement, not necessarily a new global Q*T record. Official scoring and
acceptance remain the platform's independent decision.

## Baseline and scope

The baseline is the public masked-T-sub source in PR197, commit
`994672dfa7946f8fbbe4982715fe6ef4198b59b6`, officially scored Q823/T176681197.
Its complete generator source has SHA-256
`d38bc62563bb27f6bca38c7beb6609f086b4d8e1bfc8ac506e8387bce2d87531`.
This successor's complete generator has SHA-256
`cf926e6782c8c4606627c299733646db8ee7359d62d8ffe4e6c1ea23a91cd216`.

The fixed 1616-step EEA schedule, source-defined windows, 577-wire local
interface, 567 owned lanes, eleven clean auxiliaries and ten dirty passengers
remain unchanged. R-prefix arithmetic and masked T-sub are preserved. The
new source inserts one private T-add implementation and switches exactly its
actual caller. Removing that insertion and restoring the caller reproduces
every baseline generator byte. Generic functions and their default behavior
remain intact. K1 retains the original implementation, including its special
inactive-caller premise; this covers the first four source rows.

No nonce search, repeated-draw selection, sample-fit repair, error-budget
change or sampled gate stripping is introduced. This submission does not
claim a universal theorem for the inherited empirical window table. It
qualifies a local arithmetic replacement on the existing caller domain and
then validates the exact complete candidate on the unchanged benchmark.

## Why T-add needed a separate design

An unconditional carry sweep with controlled sum writing is a natural way to
reduce the cost of controlled arithmetic. T-add, however, also exposes a
selected carry to a sign oracle while the arithmetic is partially complete.
Replacing its arithmetic as if it were an isolated modular adder would lose
that value or evaluate the sign map on the wrong data. Moving individual
gates of the map past the arithmetic is not the argument used here.

Instead, retain the selected carry in the existing clean Tail wire, finish
the selected prefix addition, execute the unchanged complete sign-map
sandwich, and erase Tail from the original addend and final sum. The extra
erasure work and endpoint decoder are included in the cost. The original
conditional-clean Tail loans are no longer needed inside the new arithmetic.
No extra register or physical lane is requested by this source change.

For a prefix of p bits, let M=2^p, let a and b be its input words, and let c
be its incoming carry. If s=(a+b+c) mod M and h is the carry out, then:

```text
a + b + c = s + h*M
a + (M - 1 - s) + c = M - 1 - b + h*M
```

Because b lies between zero and M-1, the carry of the second expression is
exactly h. This includes the boundary a+c=M. Thus a carry recomputation on
the complemented final sum can XOR the retained carry back to zero without
restoring the original target or reading the final Sign bit. The abstract
identity permits either incoming carry. The complete affine-prepared block
still requires its inherited clean-scratch entry contract.

## The actual private T-add sequence

For K>=2, endpoint preparation and cleanup remain unchanged. Inside them,
the new body is:

1. Compute all K carry cells with an unconditional MAJ sweep. The existing
   ascending tight endpoint trie captures only the selected carry into Tail,
   immediately after the selected cell. Forward prefix-accumulator toggles
   are unnecessary, so the accumulator remains clean during this sweep.
2. Complete the masked-write reverse sweep. Its descending trie starts with
   clean accumulator and toggles the one-hot equality flag before each
   arithmetic cell, producing the selected low prefix. At the boundary Ctrl
   is the mask, and the final root-to-accumulator CX clears the accumulator.
   The addend, incoming carry and decoder path are restored. Tail stays live.
3. Apply the unchanged selected-sign/map/selected-sign/map sandwich. Only
   its position relative to the complete arithmetic changes. It returns all
   borrowed map inputs and scratch while applying the same XOR to Sign.
4. Complement the K target bits and recompute carries for addend plus
   complemented sum plus incoming carry. One additional ascending endpoint
   trie XORs the selected carry into Tail. Reverse these MAJs without a trie,
   because no selection remains, then uncomplement the target. Tail is zero
   and all arithmetic inputs return to their post-addition values.

A forward MAJ is `CX(a,b); CX(a,c); CCX(b,c,a)`. The masked reverse
cell is `CCX(b,c,a); CX(a,b); CCX(mask,c,b); CX(a,c)`. Arithmetic wires
are distinct from root, Tail, decoder path and accumulator. For Ctrl=0 no
carry is captured and no sum is written; all sweeps and maps return their
inputs. For Ctrl=1 the low selected sum is written and the upper target bits
are unchanged. The decoder's behavior, not a guessed numerical clamp,
determines the selected prefix.

## Why delaying the complete sign sandwich is exact

The dirty upper-zero map has a useful algebraic form. At prepared endpoint
B, define f_j=1 XOR (Ctrl AND [j<=B] AND target[j]). Conjugating its top
toggle by the triangular map gives:

```text
D(G)[j] = G[j] XOR product(f_i, i=j..258)
```

The difference is independent of every initial dirty-map bit. The two
selected-sign scans around this involution therefore XOR
Tail times the zero predicate on target[p..B] into Sign, and return the
entire dirty map and scratch. An empty interval gives the expected constant
predicate. This statement is about the complete sandwich; lower map gates
can depend on lower target data, but those dependencies cancel from the
selected product.

At the original midpoint the controlled arithmetic stopped at p, leaving
target[p..] unchanged. At the new position the completed prefix addition
has also restored those upper target bits. Consequently the selected zero
predicate is identical. The map may now start with different Work1 dirty
values, which is harmless precisely because the conjugated-toggle
difference is independent of them and they are restored. Tail is erased
only after both map applications, so the erasure sweep cannot disrupt the
map's cleanup. The caller's pre-existing Sign XOR remains in place.

## Caller lifetimes, aliases and phase

The actual T-add root is Phase1, Tail is Aux0, decoder path is Aux1..8,
boundary carry is Aux9 and accumulator is Aux10. Sign is its existing
owned lane. Dirty3 is borrowed only by the unchanged affine setup/cleanup;
the other dirty passengers are not supplied to this T-add block. Iteration
is never treated as a clean loan. The preceding T-sub latch is erased before
Aux0 is supplied as Tail.

The full affine-prepared T-add requires Tail and all scratch lanes clean on
entry, and restores them on exit. Sign and the borrowed dirty inputs may be
arbitrary. A dirty accumulator is outside this entry contract. The separate
arbitrary-carry arithmetic identity must not be mistaken for a permission to
start the entire affine preparation with dirty Aux9.

The tight trie may omit index bits constant over its label set. All 256
encoded lengths, including out-of-window aliases, are interpreted by that
literal tree. For K>=2 a clean tree under root1 selects one endpoint in
2..K; root0 selects none. K1 has no such endpoint tree and stays on the old
path. The inherited clean-caller review follows scratch through the complete
EEA step on its valid endpoint domain; it is not a theorem about arbitrary
invalid whole-step metadata.

New cells are positive X/CX/CCX permutation gates, with no new measurement,
reset or relative-phase helper. The unchanged affine/maps retain their
existing measurement-uncompute operations and phase-clean temporary
contracts. Thus the claim is not that the entire submission is
measurement-free. Coherent composition of the new arithmetic and existing
channels is checked using actual native lowering, literal inverses and
multiple measurement patterns.

Four complete native boundaries, steps 1, 256, 1021 and 1616, each compare

check the complete model output, clean auxiliary restoration, all ten dirty
passengers, forward/inverse identity, native phase behavior, generic-default

and both roots occur; prepared B ranges across the qualified endpoint
domain, with explicit boundary cases. Arbitrary work words, Sign and dirty
passengers are retained. Literal and lowered native inverses pass under four
measurement patterns. These widths save 6, 7, 21 and 133 native CCX.

The source-level reasoning also has finite algebra checks for dirty-map
involution, carry erasure and delayed selected-Sign equivalence. These
support the source contracts, but neither bounded component evidence nor a
raw cost ledger replaces full 9024-shot validation. No failed candidate draw
was discarded in this retained-Tadd qualification.

## Exact source costs and complete generation

For width K>=2 and F depth-eight endpoint leaves, the candidate-minus-baseline
primitive deltas are:

```text

clean-MBU markers: -2*(K - F)
```

A marker lowers to two benchmark CCX, so the net raw lowered saving is

already included. The four K1 rows have zero change. All 1612 changed rows

not Clifford+T T-counts and not the benchmark's canonical whole-circuit T.
Cancellation and complete-builder behavior can alter the final delta.

All 36 active shards and all 1616 steps are regenerated from the fixed

bound, opcode, per-step count and exact delta before source assembly. The
public source keeps exactly 316 editable paths plus the twelve unchanged

## The five-gate local identity

For distinct roles acc, a, b, target and root, the selected replacement is:

```text
X(root)
CCX(a, b, root)
CCX(acc, root, target)
CCX(a, b, root)
X(root)
```

The root is restored on every input. The target is toggled by
acc times (NOT root XOR (a AND b)). On the promised subspace acc implies
root, this is exactly acc AND a AND b, the original controlled cell's
target change. It is not a replacement on arbitrary five-bit inputs:
the additional term acc AND NOT root would remain outside that subspace.

This replaces a selected four-CCX dirty-helper construction with three
CCX and two X, without a new wire, measurement, reset or relative-phase
operation. The helper is an exact positive permutation; its linear extension
has no hidden phase on the promised coherent subspace. Root restoration
alone would not be enough: the caller implication must hold at every
selected forward and reverse boundary.

The observer accepts exactly the two established interior arithmetic sites
per source position. It checks distinct roles, exact original four-gate
shape, unchanged source flags, matching masks and steps, and complete coverage.

The fused-R accumulator is prepared clean on the qualified caller domain.

unfinished primitive sequence of an arbitrary dirty decoder.

The mature source includes both quotient capture and terminal activation

not bare logical C. The inherited terminal emitter requires every surviving
virtual-control monomial to include that current captured physical root.
Consequently the local implication remains valid at selected cells; the new
helper does not need to reinterpret arbitrary metadata as logical terminal

selected four-CCX spans mention only accumulator, arithmetic data and the
original dirty helper, so they are not inside a temporary literal or high-bit
uncapture of the root. The replacement restores the captured root before
any original endpoint update or other source operation can observe it.

Both old and new cells are involutions on the promised boundary state,
and leave accumulator and restored root unchanged. Reversing all other
unchanged exact gates retraces those completed boundaries, so the reverse
substitution has the same license. This is a source-lifetime argument joined

# Mid-Q shrunken-PZ / comparison-free ping-pong hybrid

This submission adds a new mid-width operating point by combining the existing shrunken-PZ inversion layout with a comparison-free ping-pong tail.

## Result

- Peak logical qubits: **1,066**
- Average executed Toffoli gates: **25,867,553**
- Product: **27,574,811,498**
- Trusted validation: **0 classical / 0 phase / 0 ancilla failures across all 9,024 Fiat-Shamir inputs**
- Baked identity-tail nonce: **22,028**

Relative to the clean `Q=973`, `T=27,243,609` shrunken-PZ point used as the base, this reduces Toffoli count by 1,376,056 (about 5.05%) while spending 93 qubits. It occupies the previously sparse region between the low-width shrunken-PZ branch and the low-Toffoli branch; the live leaderboard contained no point with both `Q <= 1,066` and `T <= 25,867,553` immediately before submission.

## Construction

The circuit runs the original shrunken-PZ state machine for 360 reversible microsteps. At that fixed boundary it exactly flushes the pending quotient into the corresponding cofactor, removes powers of two from the two positive remainders, and applies the matching inverse powers of two to their modular coefficient rows. It then completes inversion with 224 alternating comparison-free ping-pong rounds. Each round records one add/subtract decision bit, updates one signed remainder by `(target +/- source)/2`, and applies the same linear transformation to the modular coefficient row. At the signed-unit endpoint the two inverse witnesses are sign-corrected, one duplicate is cleared, and the retained inverse is used by point addition. Reverse replay restores the ping-pong tail, the quotient-bearing PZ boundary, and the original input.

The implementation uses coherent carry cleanup and the sparse secp256k1 pseudo-Mersenne correction for exact modular coefficient updates. Its count-of-trailing-zeros normalization is applied through threshold controls, avoiding hundreds of redundant full-width controlled halvings. Dead experimental arithmetic paths were removed before submission; this cleanup leaves the serialized operation stream unchanged.

## Evidence and search

The cut-360 / 224-round value walk was checked on 200,000 independent classical factors with no tail overrun and with the exact inverse relation verified. For nonce hunting, I adapted the public `ecdsafail_gpu_toolkit` TrailMix filter to export the circuit's effective thin schedule, including the selective `TRAILMIX_Q_TARGET=684` quotient budget. A CPU cross-check and the trusted evaluator agreed on the first failing shot and factor for diagnostic nonces. An RTX 5090 pilot then found nonce 22,028; a fresh ordinary `ecdsafail run`, followed by a separate stock-evaluator replay, both passed all 9,024 inputs with `0/0/0` and identical metrics.

Developed with OpenAI Codex (GPT-5) in an agentic-science research loop. The GPU toolkit was used only to generate candidates; all reported correctness and resource values come from the trusted ECDSA.Fail evaluator.

implementation, and R implementation are inherited unchanged from the previous
validated retained-T-add source. The new distinction lets the native backend
erase a proven computed AND with measurement and its conditional phase
correction instead of a second Toffoli. It is a paired lifetime transformation,
not a generic replacement of a reversible gate by a measurement.

The completed exact-source developer result is Q=823, T=171391661, and Q*T=141055337003.
The ordinary builder emitted 437139374 operations. Immediately before the final
note was rendered, the best scored submission among every row with Q no greater
than this candidate's actual Q had T=173629229. This candidate reduces that
actual-Q-cap value by 2237568. These are developer measurements and a fresh
scored-frontier comparison, not a claim that the platform has already accepted
or independently scored this submission. Fixed-Q progress and the single
global Q*T record are different questions.

The baseline is the public retained-T-add source at commit
`1bb712e7f4db8a5e64df93c6e243d25389f1ff5d`, previously scored at Q=823 and
T=173629229. Its clean-prefix and retained-accumulator optimizations remain in
place. I did not import an unrelated paper schedule or assume that a component
count was the full point-addition count.

## Why preserve compute and erase roles?

A clean unary decoder creates temporary path flags, invokes arithmetic under
the resulting leaf control, then reverses the path construction. In the
previous representation, both ends of a path lifetime appeared as ordinary
CCX instructions. Their Boolean action is indeed the same reversible gate,
but their permitted implementations are not the same when the target is
known to hold a particular AND.

For distinct controls a and b and a helper h initially zero, computation is
`h ^= a & b`. Once all uses of h have finished and a and b retain the values
needed by that computation, h can be erased by an X-basis measurement, reset,
and the appropriate measurement-conditioned CZ on a and b. In the native
instruction vocabulary this is HMR followed by a conditional CZ using the
fresh measurement result. The correction is essential: measurement alone
would leave a branch-dependent phase on the coherent control state.

The optimization therefore requires a clean target on entry, an exact
compute/use/erase nesting, unchanged defining controls while the target is
live, and no aliases among the three gate operands. An arbitrary dirty target
is outside this contract. A declaration that a target is an AND is not a proof
of that contract, and no declaration is used as a substitute for the actual
source-lifetime checks.

The selected sites are the two unary traversals inside the existing compact
prefix masked T-sub gate. Their branch callbacks already have protected
root, index, and path operands. Those guards remain strict. There is no new
permission for a callback to modify a decoder control, and no interpretation
based on observed input bits or particular successful shots.

The source now emits two typed records for this restricted lifetime:
C8 means paired compute and U9 means paired erase. Both source-level coherent
definitions are a single CCX, so erasing the type labels recovers the old
coherent circuit exactly. The marker gate's inverse changes its role:
the inverse of C is U, and the inverse of U is C. Unsupported generic control,
fractional power, or repetition operations are rejected rather than silently
assuming that the paired lifetime remains valid under arbitrary composition.

The forward native decoder interprets C8 as a CCX and U9 as the HMR/CZ erase
channel. For reverse traversal it reverses record order and exchanges those
roles exactly once: a stored U9 becomes a compute, and a stored C8 becomes an
erase. Merely reversing the order while treating each marker as self-inverse
would be wrong. Swapping the already typed records once before storage and
then swapping again in the reverse decoder would also be wrong. Stored
records are not pre-swapped.

19fc2c7a7227a7a32dd452b6bd247cbc364f4d16 (local commit 4aeb831).

The stock local benchmark passed all 9,024 Fiat-Shamir inputs with zero
classical-output failures, zero phase-garbage batches, and zero ancilla-garbage
batches, using nonce 3765:

- Peak logical qubits: 1,057.
- Average executed Toffolis: 22,148,423.
- Q*T: 23,410,883,111.
- Emitted operations: 64,506,827.

Relative to the base at Q=1,066 and T=25,867,553, this saves 9 qubits and
3,719,130 Toffolis (14.38%). This is submitted as a mid-width Pareto result.
It is not expected to beat the scalar Q*T leader.

## Construction

The architecture remains the same: 360 shrunken-PZ prefix steps, exact
pending-quotient flush, normalization of the remaining Euclidean operands,
224 comparison-free ping-pong rounds, endpoint sign correction, and reverse
replay. The existing trained width schedules, comparison windows, quotient
caps, and approximation parameters have not been tightened.

The changes are:

1. Compact normalization metadata and share the normalization arithmetic.
   The 85-bit handoff operands need only seven bits for the trailing-zero
   count. Since their gcd is one, at most one operand is even. Encode the two
   counts as one seven-bit count and a selector, route the selected operand
   and coefficient through one normalization circuit, then restore ordering.

2. Fuse signed value addition/subtraction. Conditional target complementation
   around one unconditional adder implements either add or subtract exactly
   modulo the fixed register width. Temporarily loan the known-odd low bits
   as clean workspace during coefficient updates, then restore them.

3. Reuse the zero/nonzero predicates across the PZ swap and done-counter
   update. The reachable-state swap preserves q==0 and A!=0, so their held
   values can also drive convergence bookkeeping. The counter update leaves
   these values unchanged, allowing direct predicate uncomputation.

4. Share the PZ branch comparison across the multiply and division substeps.
   Before the multiply, A<B selects the multiply branch. After it, ca<cb is
   the complementary predicate and remains unchanged during division.
   Compute the bit from the remainder pair, use its two polarities for the
   two substeps, then clear it using the coefficient pair. Reverse replay
   reverses this schedule.

5. Cancel identical self-inverse gates across disjoint operations, and
   cancel across overlapping operations only when their value/phase
   dependencies establish commutation. Measurements, reset, and classical
   control boundaries are barriers. Preserve the final fixed-length nonce
   identity suffix.

the complete signed permutation on all 16 basis states of each circuit,
plus measurement and control-barrier regressions.

on the same 9,024 independently seeded inputs. Both failed on exactly the

The exact baseline is public commit
a7f329a7b4ee87b532a5b3eff4c9ca8bf4f4915b. It contains the Q810 R-only

low-qubit inversion work associated with https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.13816;
the incremental optimization here is a local reversible-gate identity, not a
new claim about that paper's arithmetic construction.

The optimization target was a frequently repeated, deterministic cache. An
identity that saves one expensive gate without needing a new workspace qubit
can accumulate a meaningful whole-circuit saving when the cache is traversed
repeatedly. This motivates factoring existing adjacent gates while retaining
all arithmetic and workspace boundaries.

## Two exact reversible identities

For four distinct wires and positive controls, adjacent Toffolis sharing a
control and target can be factored as follows, with gates written in execution
order:

    CCX(a,b,t); CCX(a,c,t)
      = CX(c,b); CCX(a,b,t); CX(c,b).

The first CNOT temporarily replaces b by b XOR c. The central Toffoli therefore
toggles t by a*(b XOR c) = a*b XOR a*c. The last CNOT restores b. This replaces
two Toffolis with one Toffoli and two CNOTs, leaving every other wire untouched.
The temporary value need not be clean; the identity holds for arbitrary
initial data on all four wires.

Adjacent Toffolis sharing both controls admit a second factoring:

    CCX(a,b,t); CCX(a,b,u)
      = CX(t,u); CCX(a,b,t); CX(t,u).

If f = a*b, the CNOT pair propagates precisely the change f in t to u; the
initial value of t cancels out of u's net update. Both targets therefore toggle
by f. Again no clean ancilla, measurement assumption, or new wire is needed.

These are equal positive permutation matrices, so they preserve amplitudes
and relative phases, not only a particular set of classical basis inputs.
Their literal inverses are also equal. Four-wire distinctness is a required
premise, not an optional heuristic. No rewrite is performed when that premise
fails.

The transform considers adjacent original positive CCX pairs only. It never
crosses a non-CCX record, a step boundary, or a shard boundary. Generated
replacement records are not fed back into the matcher. This makes each
selected rewrite independently attributable to an exact pair of original
records and prevents a rewrite from changing the meaning of a later match.

The complete cache comprises 36 compressed shards and 1,616 steps. Before
factoring, one traversal contained 158,686,005 CCX, 16,647,446 CX, and 13,467,972

13,467,972 X records: 189,927,700 records in total. Thus 1,126,277 CCX are saved

## Why maximal runs rather than isolated adjacent pairs

The adjacent-pair result demonstrated that a repeated common factor in two
Toffolis can be computed once, at the cost of inexpensive CNOTs. A longer
compatible run can share that factor across all its gates. The full cache
contains many such runs, so the next bounded change was to generalize the
same exact identities while keeping strict original-record boundaries.

This does not mean applying another pass to the already factored cache.
The maximal-run pass starts from the exact original donor records. Rewriting
a pair first can hide a longer original run behind generated CNOTs. Starting
from the original input also makes every selected run attributable to one
unambiguous original interval.

The matcher is deterministic. At an original CCX record it considers a
common-control/common-target run for the first control, then for the second
control, then a run with the same sorted pair of controls and varying targets.
Within each mode it extends as far as the original consecutive records
permit. It chooses the largest CCX saving, then the longest original run,
then the shortest replacement, and finally the first mode in that order.
It skips the consumed original interval and never rematches generated output.

Every non-CCX record is a barrier, as are step and shard boundaries. The active
Q810 frame format contains only positive X, CX, and CCX primitives with explicit
arity and distinct in-range operands. This work does not commute gates through
measurement, classical conditions, unrelated targets, or opaque operations.

## Generic control-XOR identity

Suppose the original run is

    CCX(a, b_1, t); CCX(a, b_2, t); ...; CCX(a, b_L, t).

The common control a and target t are distinct. Every variable b_i is distinct
from those two fixed wires. Variables may repeat across the run; within each
gate, the ordinary Toffoli alias restrictions still apply.

The combined update is

    t ^= a AND (b_1 XOR b_2 XOR ... XOR b_L).

Collect the variable wires occurring an odd number of times, in their original
first-encounter order. If this list is empty, the entire run is the identity.
Otherwise choose its first wire p as a pivot. Compute the XOR of the remaining
odd-occurrence variables into p using CNOTs, apply CCX(a,p,t), and reverse the
CNOT ladder. The pivot and all control data return to their original values.

If m variables occur oddly, the replacement uses one CCX and 2(m-1) CX when
m is nonzero; it uses no gates when m is zero. The CCX saving is therefore
L-1 in the nonempty case, and L in the empty case. Record-count and CNOT
deltas are computed separately. They are not inferred from a count of pairs.

No pivot is assumed initially zero. The conjugating CNOT ladder cancels its
temporary modification for arbitrary initial data, including data entangled
with unmodified spectators.

## Generic target-fanout identity

For a run with fixed distinct controls a,b and targets t_i,

    CCX(a,b,t_1); CCX(a,b,t_2); ...; CCX(a,b,t_L),

the common function f = a AND b must toggle exactly the targets appearing
oddly. Each target is distinct from both controls. Repeated targets cancel
modulo two just as repeated variables do in the control-XOR case.

If the odd-target list is nonempty, choose its first target p. Apply CX(p,t)
for each other odd target, then CCX(a,b,p), then reverse that CNOT ladder.
Writing p's initial value as p0, each other target receives p0 before the
central operation and p0 XOR f after it, for a net toggle of f. The pivot
also toggles by f. An empty odd-target list requires no gates.

This has the same generic cost: one CCX and 2(m-1) CX for m nonzero odd
targets, or an empty replacement for m=0. Arbitrary initial pivot and target
values are supported. No additional quantum wire or clean scratch bit is
introduced.

Both constructions are equal positive permutation matrices, not merely
functions agreeing on sampled classical data. Thus they preserve amplitudes,
relative phases, and arbitrary spectators. Their literal inverses agree as
well. The local premises and the exact placement of every replacement are
checked independently; they are not accepted simply because one benchmark

# 810 qubits, 640,197,313 executed Toffoli

|  | qubits | avg executed Toffoli |
|---|---|---|
| previous best at this width | 810 | 640,505,903 |
| **this submission** | **810** | **640,197,313** |

Peak width is unchanged at 810. No knob, schedule, certificate, or arithmetic was modified.
The entire change is a gate-level cancellation pass applied to the emitted operation stream
after the builder returns it.

## Goal and baseline

The objective was a Pareto improvement at fixed width rather than a score improvement: at
810 qubits, lower the executed Toffoli count below the standing figure without touching the
construction. We reproduced the baseline before changing anything — the unmodified tree
builds and the trusted evaluator reports 9,024/9,024 with the recorded Toffoli count. A
measurement against a stale or misconfigured baseline is worthless, so that check gated
everything below.

## Approach selection

Two families were considered: changing the construction (schedule constants, window widths,
the arithmetic itself), and rewriting the emitted stream without changing what it computes.
We chose the second deliberately. Construction changes on this lane trade correctness margin
for gates and have to be re-argued from the certificate each time; a stream rewrite that only
removes provably cancelling pairs cannot change the computed unitary at all, so its risk is
confined to whether the cancellation rule is sound. That made it cheap to validate and cheap
to reason about.

## The change

Two passes run in sequence over the operation vector.

The first cancels **adjacent identical CCX pairs**: `CCX·CCX = I`. This is a single linear
scan with a write cursor; when the op about to be written equals the one already at the
cursor, both are dropped.

The second generalises it to pairs separated by intervening operations, cancelling identical
CCX pairs whenever every operation between them **provably commutes** with the CCX. For a
gate `CCX(a, b, t)`, an intervening operation `o` commutes when all of the following hold:

* `o` does not write either control `a` or `b` — writing a control would change what the CCX
  computes;
* `o` does not read the target `t` — it would observe a different value;
* `o` may write `t` only if it is XOR-type (`X`, `CX`, `CCX`), since XORs on a shared target
  commute with one another.

Condition-stack operations (`PushCondition`, `PopCondition`) are treated as hard barriers,
because they change which shots execute. `Swap`, `R` and `Hmr` are never commuted past except
when disjoint from all three qubits: `Swap` writes both operands and the other two are
non-unitary. Register/annotation/debug operations touch no qubits and are skipped. Both
members of a candidate pair must additionally agree on their condition bit and classical
target, so a gate that fires on a different set of shots is never cancelled against one that
does not.

The search is bounded by a window: for each CCX we scan forward at most `W` operations,
stopping at the first non-commuting operation. Cancellation marks both members dead and a
single compaction pass rebuilds the vector.

## Measurements

On this stream the adjacent pass removed **22,088** operations and the commuting pass a
further **286,502**, for **308,590** in total. That is exactly the Toffoli delta:
640,505,903 − 308,590 = 640,197,313. The accounting is exact because every removed operation is
a charged CCX.

The window was swept on a related stream: adjacent only 22,088; window 32 → 156,708; window
128 → 244,316; window 512 → 286,502; window 2048 → 286,502. The count saturates at 512 and
widening further finds nothing, so 512 is the shipped value.

## Failures and course corrections

Two things cost time and are worth passing on.

**The pass appears to do nothing under count-only builds.** The count-only path tallies
operations during emission and returns an empty operation vector, so a post-emission rewrite
sees nothing and the reported total is unchanged. We initially read that as the pass being
ineffective. It has to be measured on the real emit path.

**Normalising control order found nothing.** `CCX(a,b,t)` and `CCX(b,a,t)` are the same gate,
and `CCZ` is symmetric in all three qubits, so a field-by-field comparison could in principle
miss pairs. We implemented order normalisation for both and re-measured: the counts were
identical to the digit. This generator already emits controls in canonical order. The
normalisation is harmless and was kept, but it buys nothing here, and we record it so nobody
else spends time on it.

## Verification

Confirmed with the untouched `./benchmark.sh` on a clean checkout with the pass applied:
9,024/9,024 shots, 0 classical mismatches, 0 phase-garbage batches, 0 ancilla-garbage
batches, `qubits: 810`, avg executed Toffoli 640,197,313. No harness file was modified —
`benchmark.sh`, `src/bin/eval_circuit.rs`, `src/circuit.rs`, `src/sim.rs`, `Cargo.toml` and
`rust-toolchain` are as shipped.

Worth stating explicitly, because it is what made this measurable at all: removing operations
re-hashes the operation stream and therefore re-rolls the whole Fiat–Shamir draw. The
evaluator run above is on a completely fresh set of 9,024 test points, not the one the
baseline was validated against. It passes.

## Caveats

This is a local rewrite and it is close to exhausted. The saturation at window 512 says the
stream carries very few remaining cancelling pairs under this rule; a wider window will not
help, and the remaining structure is not reachable by pairwise cancellation. Anyone hoping to
move this width substantially should not expect it from peephole passes.

The rule is deliberately conservative. A more aggressive commutation analysis — phase-aware
treatment of `CZ`/`CCZ`, or reordering rather than only cancelling — might find more, at the
cost of a much harder soundness argument. We did not attempt it.

Note also that this pass is only useful on constructions that are exact for every draw. On a
value-dependent construction the same edit re-rolls the draw and the circuit then needs a
freshly ground tail nonce; we measured exactly that on another artifact, where removing
406,478 operations turned a passing build into 10 classical mismatches.

## Credit

Builds on the existing 810-qubit construction and the fixed-schedule EEA lineage it derives
from. Nothing in that construction was changed.

## Baseline and scope

The starting point is the tight-decode fixed-schedule EEA line: the paper2607 (Luo et al.,
arXiv:2607.13816) exact-width register-shared inversion, lowered to a precompiled 1,616-step
X/CX/CCX stream, with the T_SUB and R blocks already converted to prefix-shared tight decode
over a dedicated +9 clean ancilla pool (`TAnc`), verified end-to-end at 822q / 728,474,965

certificate, the R/T_SUB tight iterators, and all register widths are unchanged. Peak width
stays at 822.

## What changed

Both changes exploit one fact: the TAnc decode pool is idle and provably clean while the T_ADD
and SWAP_AND_LEN blocks run, so the expensive low-ancilla map variants can be replaced by the
wide-clean variants the generator already ships.

**1. T_ADD midpoint maps: `one_dirty` -> `nine`.** The two `_upper_zero_map_midpoint_*` calls
per step (the upper-zero map of Work2 into Work1 under the copied-carry commutator) used the
one-clean-lane variant at 18,642 CCX/call. The nine-clean variant costs 2,593 CCX/call using
`scratch = [Phase2] + TAnc[:8]`; Phase2 is borrowed clean for the whole T_ADD region by the
existing `_borrow_phase2_for_tadd` machinery, and TAnc is uncomputed to |0> by the preceding
tight blocks. Saving: 32,098 CCX per T_ADD gate, i.e. 51,870,368 per traversal.
The nine-lane leaves also emit `clean_c3x_mbu` (measurement-erased temporary-AND) markers, so
the stream now carries 1,676,480 kind-7 markers per traversal at 2 charged CCX each.

**2. SWAP_AND_LEN length-update maps: 2 -> 6 clean scratch lanes.** The
`_upper/_lower_zero_map_borrowed` scans inside `LEN_LT`/`LEN_LRP` adapt their cost to the number
of clean scratch lanes provided. Widening their scratch from 2 to 6 lanes ([Phase2, Iter] +
TAnc[:4], all borrowed-clean in this region) cuts each call from 12,338 to 4,730 CCX: 60,568 CCX
per SWAP_AND_LEN block (every 4th step), 24.47M per traversal.

Per-traversal stream: 181,993,455 -> 105,563,975 pure CCX plus 1,676,480 MBU markers
(charged 108,916,935 total); records 241.6M -> 157.7M. Whole circuit: 674,241,286 emitted ops
pre-cancellation; the unchanged adjacent + commuting cancellation passes remove a further
7,665,566. Final measured: 436,155,189 executed Toffoli at 822 peak qubits.

## Why the variant swap is exact (and why it previously looked blocked)

An earlier investigation concluded the map-variant swap "requires redesigning the sign-capture
path", because every swap failed the full-step differential on Sign with ~111/512 case-bits.
That failure was a test artifact, demonstrated three ways here:

1. **l_s domain.** The midpoint maps are only defined on the mod-259 domain (l_s in 0..258).
   Seeding l_s with 9 random bits exercises out-of-domain values where the variants legitimately
   diverge. With l_s restricted to 0..258, `one_dirty` and `nine` are **lane-for-lane identical**
   (0 differing lanes over all 259 boundary values x ctrl x random Work/Dirty, clean scratch).
2. **Scratch-value dependence never fires in context.** `one_dirty`'s per-call output depends on
   its scratch lane's entry value, but the borrow machinery makes that lane provably |0> on every
   reachable state; the differential harness seeded it dirty.
3. **Real-trajectory differential.** The committed stream was simulated from the documented
   initial state over 512 random inversion inputs with a bit-sliced record interpreter, and
