# Q794: exact Toffoli reductions in Sign, T10, R01 and NCT scheduling

This submission is a locally qualified lower-Toffoli successor to our
officially validated Q794 circuit. It preserves 794 physical qubits and
reduces T from 944,644,564 to 779,005,524: 165,639,040 fewer Toffolis,
a 17.5345359 percent reduction. The complete circuit emits 1,242,524,952
primitive operations. The frozen source-default count and all 9024
source-derived canonical shots passed, with zero classical, phase or
ancilla failures. Final source, binary and log binding was checked before
upload. This is local qualification; the unchanged official generator and
validator are requested next. No new global minimum-Q-times-T score or
already completed remote acceptance is claimed.

## Attribution and exact starting point

The immediate starting point is our own official Q794 submission
`c4c2c938-99c3-4b83-879a-9a8a3b24d2bd`, commit
`84233955b5fc20f6738beedeba02b66cb13a90d6`, with Q794,
T944,644,564 and 1,407,988,472 primitive operations. Its official benchmark
workflow completed successfully. Its API result did not improve the global
spacetime best; that is distinct from a correctness failure. This new
submission is a further exact resource reduction, not a rerun of an
unmodified public competitor.

Our Q794 implementation was derived from the public Q795 work by
mochimodev / the Mochimo Foundation, commit
`8af186994c57cc8b8913efdbfd2759760ddb2d8a`, submission
`cb0cb0e2-e725-4b02-9301-a98d58aafe75`. Attribution, notices and inherited
arithmetic from Matt Zweil & MAI / TrailMix are retained. In particular,
the rank5 metadata representation, the underlying EEA schedule, prior
borrowed-phase machinery, inherited arithmetic and benchmark infrastructure
are not claimed as new work. We also make no claim that elementary Boolean
factoring, conditional clean-scratch methods or reversible route sharing
are globally new. The contribution here is their proved, implemented and
tested application to this complete fixed-prime low-qubit circuit.

Only our own modified components and candidates were executed during this
optimization run. Published source and historical evidence may be read
for attribution and comparison, but the unchanged public Q795 circuit was
not tested. No source-dependent nonce search, test-corpus tuning, evaluator
change or replacement of the official acceptance criteria is involved.

## Unchanged low-qubit representation

The circuit retains our Q794 two-residual-bit invariant chart. Its physical
plateau consists of 257 Work1 rails, 259 Work2 rails, 21 metadata rails,
one iteration rail and 256 external live field rails. The phase wires and
working helper pool are borrowed from that external word, not allocated
again. Neither omitted Work1 low-residue marker may appear in an emitted
primitive operation, including inactive branches and temporary routing.

The EEA invariant is `t*r + u*v + q*t*v = p`. The fixed prime is the
secp256k1 prime, congruent3 modulo4 and 7 modulo8. Depending on the parity
of t, an existing two-bit slot contains either u modulo4 or r modulo4;
the missing logical low bits are read through this invariant. This chart,
its boundary cases, both independent phase passengers, and the inherited
exact schedule remain in place. The current work reduces the operations
needed to use that representation rather than introducing a smaller
statistical or approximately reversible encoding.

## Sign: share one address computation between flag and clean loan

Sign previously read the same dynamic source address
`k = 257-(C+S)` separately to obtain its top flag and to obtain a clean
carry loan. Both operations separately prepared the low address, gathered
the selected source bit through a reversible tree, performed a small
central operation, ungathered, and restored the metadata. Their inverse
operations repeated the same independent routing work at the end.

The new implementation merges these purposes. After the existing cargo
handoffs and mask loan, the active mask and cache are zero. While the
selected source bit is at the gather root h, it performs
`mask ^= g*h`, followed by a swap of h and the existing carry helper
controlled by `g && !mask`. It then restores the routing and address
metadata. On the top-zero branch this supplies carry0 and parks the old
arbitrary carry at the selected source address. On the top-one branch it
retains the top flag without borrowing that nonzero source bit. The
existing phase-code parking disables the comparator on the latter branch.

The comparator therefore receives a clean carry on every remaining active
branch without a second address traversal. Its own two top-loan calls are
removed. After the comparator and phase parking are reversed, the literal
inverse of the entire merged preparation restores the arbitrary carry and
clears the flag. The merged map is not incorrectly assumed to be an
involution. Cache is never changed while it is used as an address control,
and both mask and carry are excluded from the routing's dirty lenders.

The C1/S0 exception retains its proved distinct hosts: source255 for the
mask passenger and source256 for the carry passenger. Its comparison is
known false, so the existing central toggle cancellation remains. The
cheaper C2/S0 internal carry extension is also retained. Its possible
disturbance cannot survive to the comparator center on valid states for
this fixed prime; the prior independent proof using p congruent7 modulo8
still applies. No unvalidated Sign V2 path is enabled.

Two additional exact Sign reductions affect its virtual low-cell
correction. Three equal-control products are combined by temporarily
forming the XOR of their three data controls on one existing data rail,
using only CNOTs around a single multi-controlled toggle. The data rail
is restored exactly. For toggles strictly inside the matched temporary
compute/inverse pair, X(g) supplies a conditionally clean scratch when
g=1. Off guard, the primitive remains a pure target-XOR extension whose
effects cancel around the inactive center. This reasoning is not extended
to an unmatched center, cargo operation or decoder.

## T10: route sharing and local correction predicates

General T10 previously gathered the same quotient address separately to
pop the quotient bit and to borrow its now-zero slot as a mask. These
ordered exchanges now share one route and its inverse. The endpoint
action is moved only across a complete map with which it commutes: normal
and endpoint actions are selected by disjoint predicates, their selectors
are unchanged, and their affected rails are not improperly borrowed as
dirty helpers. The data word is physically restored before arithmetic
uses it. This is not a claim that a permuted data word can remain hidden
across arbitrary subsequent consumers.

T10's paired low-carry correction also uses the existing guard as a
conditionally clean scratch. On inactive input, the center and every
conditional SUM are disabled, so its complete temporary computation and
inverse cancel. Crucially, the unmatched modulo4 SUM correction continues
to use a truly guarded operation. It does not receive the weaker
offguard-extension optimization.

Finally, a global quotient-endpoint decoder is replaced by a local
predicate only where physical v1 can actually contain the second
passenger. This happens at A254 in the active non-C1 branch. Positivity
and the remaining quotient's significant bit imply
`A + C_true + S <= 256`. Thus A254 forces C2, S0 and clock j0 in this
branch. Raw C0 is not mistaken for an empty quotient: there it represents
true length256, which instead forces A0, S0 and odd t=1 and disables the
even-t correction. At every other relevant endpoint the physical v1 bit
is already the required zero. The physical bit is untouched at both low
correction sites; center gathers are reversed before it is read again.

Two further selected T10 changes reuse the existing P2 rail as an endpoint
cache during intervals when it is already zero under the active guard.
The first interval computes `g*M256`, uses that bit for the quotient-pop
and mask-loan center operations, and uncomputes it before fused arithmetic
needs P2 as its range cache. The fused arithmetic restores P2. A separate
second endpoint-cache interval performs the final mask return. Rank, A, C
and g are restored before each oracle inverse; P2 is excluded from every
dirty lender pool that could overlap those intervals. This is reuse of
one existing phase wire at disjoint times, not an additional ancilla or a
cache kept live through unrelated arithmetic.

The endpoint oracle itself uses the paired-clean construction with X(g)
as scratch. For arbitrary offguard state it remains a pure P2-XOR
function of restored selectors. All intervening center operations retain
explicit g, so on g0 they are identity and the repeated oracle cancels
its arbitrary extension. On g1 the scratch is clean and P2 receives the
exact endpoint flag. Every source, lender and the guard returns before
its next consumer. The canonical and paired cache changes were tested
together; no separate experimental gain is claimed for either in isolation.

## R01: factor the metadata/chart product with a dirty echo

The inherited low-prefix carry seed is an algebraic-normal-form expression
in seven physical chart bits and the logical metadata flags A0, A1, A254
and C0, with the current g and mask guards. The new emitter groups the
same expression by metadata monomial. It preserves the inherited
treatment of inconsistent flag combinations rather than replacing the
extension with a new sampled truth table.

For each group, write the desired carry toggle as `F(metadata)*H(chart)`.
An existing arbitrary dirty helper d implements that product by:

    d ^= F
    carry ^= d*H
    d ^= F                  (literal inverse of the first computation)
    carry ^= d*H

The two carry toggles sum to `F*H`, while d and every source return exactly.
F does not read carry, and both predicate implementations restore their
ladder lenders after each use. This is therefore an exact all-state NCT
identity, including arbitrary offguard inputs and superpositions, not a
new clean-loan assumption. One existing helper holds d within a group;
the remaining 19 helpers fund the dirty ladders. No data/chart/control rail
is lent, no reset or measurement is introduced, and no qubit is allocated.

For each group the emitter chooses the least expensive exact form among
the inherited expansion and echo forms placing g/mask in F or H. Duplicate
metadata controls and contradictory cubes are handled as in the inherited
gate lowering. Actual quotient-prefix and q1 gathering, virtual A0/A1/A254
bits, both low chart updates, all MAJ/UMA cells, endpoint M255 and the
complete phase lifecycle remain unchanged. The native measured seed cost
is 3,400 T for shift0 and 754 T for shift1, compared with 7,996 and 1,592 in
the inherited seed. A further outside-workspace cube-merging model is
explicitly not part of this candidate or its measured resource claim.

## Exact NCT factoring with checked gate movement

A separate small rewrite pass factors two Toffolis that have the same
target and one common control. The identity is
`a*b XOR a*c = a*(b XOR c)`. Consequently the two Toffolis can be replaced
by a CNOT, one Toffoli, and the inverse CNOT, with no ancilla and no
relative phase. All four involved rails are distinct as required by the
validated primitive gates and the factor matcher.

For nonadjacent matches, the incoming Toffoli crosses only gates whose
targets are not read by it and which do not read its target. For ordinary
unconditioned X/CX/CCX gates, these two checks are sufficient for exact
commutation. It is the incoming old gate, not the newly inserted CNOTs,
that is moved through the intervening suffix. The new local factorization
is then inserted at the adjacent pair's location. Future rewrites operate
on the resulting exact prefix. The pass asserts its NCT-only and
no-classical-condition preconditions and introduces no new qubits.

Factoring can replace two primitive operations with three, even though it
reduces T. Both N and T must therefore be counted separately. The pass is
applied to bounded step-template vectors, not to an extra full expanded
billion-operation copy. Ordinary generation still needs a final exact
reservation consistent with the new emitted N and the unchanged loader.

## Local component and integration evidence

The first frozen revised Sign and T10 source snapshot has archive SHA256
`5129501ff4b475c93320d0d562e05d757d9eabb8bb4a23071446c9466c8357b7`.
This is an intermediate test snapshot, not yet the final upload digest.
The following terminal native results concern the actual revised code:

* Sign's merged loan passed 132608 bit-sliced lanes over all valid C/S

https://github.com/ZeroWang030221/Space-Efficient-Quantum-Algorithm-for-Elliptic-Curve-Discrete-Logarithms-with-Resource-Estimation

The arithmetic, runtime-classical ABI port, hierarchical gate representation, adjacent cancellation, and constant outer-control specialization belong to that prior source. This submission changes only how semantically proven clean AND work bits are uncomputed.

The measurement-assisted AND-uncomputation identity is established in Craig Gidney, *Halving the cost of quantum addition*, arXiv:1709.06648v3, Figure 3, and is also stated formally in Luongo et al., arXiv:2407.20167v1, section 4, Lemma 4.1:

https://arxiv.org/abs/1709.06648

https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.20167

The source analysis, recognizer, tests, census, independent review, full emission, and trusted replay for this submission were implemented with Codex using GPT-6 Astra.

## Exact transformation

For a clean work qubit `w` whose current value is exactly `a AND b`, the original inverse Toffoli clears `w`. The replacement is:

1. Demolish `w` in the X basis and store the measurement outcome `m` in one reusable classical bit.
2. Apply `CZ(a,b)` conditioned on `m`.

On each reachable computational-basis component, demolition contributes phase `(-1)^(m*w)`. The conditional CZ contributes `(-1)^(m*a*b)`. Since the proven invariant is `w=a*b`, their product is one for each outcome separately. The target returns to zero, both controls remain unchanged, and every pre-existing phase is preserved. The argument holds by linearity for superpositions and entanglement with the rest of the circuit. It is not an average-over-outcomes approximation.

Each accepted replacement removes one CCX and adds one HMR plus one conditional CZ. It therefore saves one Toffoli, adds one emitted operation, uses no quantum qubit, and reuses a single additional classical bit.

## Semantic eligibility proof

The source is a compressed hierarchical graph that expands to more than 400 million primitive operations. A syntactic search for repeated CCX operands is unsafe because a target can be dirty or a control can change between compute and cleanup. The implementation instead follows the exact expanded operation order with an immutable Boolean-function value for every quantum wire, every classical bit, and every active classical condition.

Initial facts come from the challenge ABI. Quantum input registers and classical coordinate inputs receive distinct unknown IDs. Other root wires start at zero. The proof engine propagates exact Boolean functions through X, CX, CCX, SWAP, classical writes, condition pushes and pops, and HMR. Phase-only gates retain their Boolean values. Conditions snapshot the current immutable bit value, matching the trusted simulator even if the underlying classical bit is later overwritten.

An original CCX is replaced only if all of the following hold:

- its effective classical condition is identically true;
- the two controls and target are valid and pairwise distinct;
- none of the three is the outer control `q0`;
- the target's current immutable Boolean-function ID equals the AND of the two current control IDs.

The AND and XOR interner uses exact constant, complement, equality, commutativity, and elementary cancellation identities. IDs are never recycled. The bounded expression cache may be cleared; this can only forget a proof opportunity and miss a later replacement. It cannot make two distinct functions equal. A dirty target has value `dirty XOR (a AND b)` and is rejected. A changed control receives a different value ID and is rejected unless the original value is exactly restored.

After an admitted replacement, the proof state follows the original CCX's value transition because the outcome-wise channel identity proves that the replacement makes the same transition. The new measurement bit is outside every original HIR mapping and is consumed immediately before reuse. Every original phase operation remains in the stream.

## Test-driven implementation and negative controls

The bounded suite has ten passing tests. It covers:

- a clean target used through CX and CZ and then uncomputed;
- controls changed and exactly restored;
- dirty-target rejection;
- changed-control rejection;
- a mismatched classical condition;
- a pre-existing HMR and condition stack;
- condition snapshots across later classical writes;
- descending v-chains for every basis assignment and every measurement outcome at 3 through 7 controls;
- an explicit nonzero-phase witness when the conditional CZ is omitted;
- 20,000 Boolean-expression operations checked as complete eight-row truth tables while forcing cache eviction.

The v-chain tests cover 21,824 basis, target, and measurement cases. For a k-control clean v-chain they confirm that `2k-3` CCX gates become `k-1` CCX gates plus `k-2` exact measurement cleanups, including an arbitrary initial value of the final MCX output target. Dirty-target and changed-control fixtures must produce zero cleanups.

The tests were written before the HIR stream hook. The clean identity and chain fixtures initially failed against the placeholder lowering, and the integration fixture initially found no HMR. After implementation all ten tests passed. The full source census is ignored by ordinary test invocations and requires an explicit output path.

## Arithmetic interface

The forward controlled modular adder preserves its quantum addend and updates

```

```

For canonical operands and a zero incoming flag, the flag immediately before
that final comparator equals the predicate on the right. This final comparator
is therefore a Boolean-function uncompute, which is the necessary interface
for the measurement lemma. The same comparator also occurs at the beginning
of controlled subtraction, where it computes a flag rather than clears one.
That occurrence is explicitly excluded. Recognizing the gate pattern alone
would not justify applying the transformation in both places.

Let f denote the predicate. The incoming flag is |f>. Measuring it in the
X basis and resetting it gives a zero flag and phase (-1)^(m f), where m is
the random classical measurement outcome. On m=0, no correction is necessary.
On m=1, compute the original comparator's carry path, apply the phase of f,
and reverse the carry path. This cancels the measurement phase and restores
both operands and the carry workspace. The flag remains zero throughout the
phase correction. The branch probabilities are one half for arbitrary coherent
input states; this is not a sampled or approximate predicate.

The original comparator has a single output CCX controlled by the outer
arithmetic control and the final carry bit. The implementation changes that
output gate to CZ on those two controls and retains the surrounding carry
compute/uncompute. An explicit classical condition stack controls the entire
correction block. A dedicated extra classical bit stores m; it does not reuse
or overwrite the parent circuit's live feed-forward bits and adds no quantum

- Node 2265: 256 final comparators in the forward squarer, called once.
- Node 2267: one final comparator in forward runtime-coordinate addition,

## Exact arithmetic transformation

The expensive controlled-UMA cell performs a three-control carry toggle and
a two-control sum toggle. Write the wires as ctrl, a, b, carry, and d, where d
is clean scratch. The relevant unitary action is

```
carry ^= ctrl * a * b
a     ^= ctrl * b
```

The parent decomposes the first toggle by computing d=ctrl*a, applying a
Toffoli controlled by b and d to carry, and cleaning d. It subsequently
computes ctrl*b again for the sum toggle. Both products share a control, but
only the second product is needed to implement the entire two-output action.

The candidate instead computes d=ctrl*b once, uses d and a to toggle carry,
uses a CNOT from d to a for the sum update, then cleans d. Thus the carry and
sum share one nonlinear intermediate. Without measurements the old sequence
uses four Toffolis and the new sequence uses three. With the source's existing
measurement-assisted cleanup, the old sequence uses three Toffolis and the
new sequence uses two. There is no additional quantum wire.

For the inverse-UMA cell, the sum toggle occurs before the carry toggle.
The candidate correspondingly puts the CNOT before the carry Toffoli while
retaining the same shared product ctrl*b. The transformation is valid for
arbitrary values of all four data wires, including arbitrary incoming carry.
Only the scratch wire d must be zero.

The measurement of d contributes phase m*d and resets it. Since d=ctrl*b,
the candidate uses measurement-conditioned CZ(ctrl,b) to cancel that phase.
Neither control changes before the correction. It is essential to change the
phase correction along with the factored product: the parent's original
correction used ctrl*a. The final data permutation and phase are exact for
both measurement outcomes and for coherent superpositions by linearity.

This candidate continues official submission 5b1a172d-1b39-4a12-9388-793b633694e8,
commit 46531cc1901c8d80781dae50402234f317838b55, officially measured at
Q834/T63,935,388. The goal is another exact structural reduction at the same
quantum width. It retains seven intermediate predicate products across two
uses instead of measuring them away and immediately recreating them.

## Attribution and inherited architecture

The low-space point-addition and extended Euclidean architecture is by Han
Luo, Ziyi Yang, Jingquan Luo, Ziruo Wang, Yuexin Su, Xiaoming Sun, Lvzhou Li,
and Tongyang Li, Quantum Algorithm for Elliptic Curve Discrete Logarithms
with Space-Efficient Point Addition:

https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.13816

The corrected authors' implementation is pinned at commit
e64aa3c1198d96aeb389e64bc7ae48edbb9712ec of:

https://github.com/ZeroWang030221/Space-Efficient-Quantum-Algorithm-for-Elliptic-Curve-Discrete-Logarithms-with-Resource-Estimation

The inherited MIT license remains included. The finite hierarchical gate
representation, runtime-classical coordinate adapter, constant outer-control
specialization, exact clean-AND optimization, arithmetic-predicate cleanup,
and controlled-UMA shared-product factoring come from the preceding source.
The compressed HIR remains unchanged. This candidate adds a separate exact
prefix-retention pass; it does not change the underlying EEA algorithm,
iteration bound, affine interface, proof-cache capacity, or arithmetic domain.

Implementation and independent review used Codex with GPT-6 Astra. The exact
reasoning effort setting is not exposed and is not claimed. Independent
workers had distinct research or later verification scopes; the root owner
integrated and validated the frozen implementation. No paid provider, GPU,
or nonce search was used.

## Research motivation and selected design

The research considered structural arithmetic designs and temporary-product
lifetimes. Relevant primary literature included Remaud's structural study of
ripple-carry and carry-lookahead arithmetic, arXiv:2510.00840v1; Gidney's
measurement-assisted temporary AND construction, arXiv:1709.06648v3; and
Khattar and Gidney's conditionally clean ancilla framework,
arXiv:2407.17966v2. These papers motivated looking at actual repeated product
computation. Their Clifford+T resource figures are not substituted for this
benchmark's Toffoli metric. The concrete interval below was derived from and
proved against the pinned source.

The existing within-cell factoring already shares ctrl*b between a carry and
sum update. Reusing that same result between arbitrary adjacent cells is not
valid: the next cell can use a different b or a changed control. A separate
attempt to retain two neighboring predicates also failed because an
intervening CNOT changes a factor; updating that retained product costs a
Toffoli and removes the apparent saving. Those narrow negative results led
to the two-use prefix interval, whose factors are restored exactly before
reuse and whose products are not touched incompatibly in the gap.

## Exact source interval

The eligible nodes have 578 quantum wires and one classical bit. There are
two exact byte signatures, each 65 HIR records and 571 bytes long. They have
the same topology with inputs in local bank 531..538 or 540..547. Both store
seven prefix products in local wires 559..565. The relevant extra wires are
an additional last factor, pool 577, control 558, and middle target 576.

The first seven operations compute a chain of prefix products into initially
zero product wires. The eighth operation uses the last product and the extra
factor to toggle pool 577. The original circuit then clears all seven
products through seven measurement/phase-correction groups. It toggles the
eight factor bits with X gates, applies a middle Toffoli on wires disjoint
from those factors and products, and toggles the factor bits back. It next
recreates exactly the same seven prefix products, and uses the last product
to toggle pool 577 again. A following H/measure/reset/CZ group clears the
last product.

The replacement retains the initial product computation and first use,
keeps the original middle sequence, removes the seven intermediate cleanup
groups and seven recomputation Toffolis, and retains the second use and the

not claim a new width reduction or a new encoding of the two omitted

chart remain part of the implementation and its validation. The changes
reduce the work needed to move between metadata states and to evaluate
the two arithmetic predicates used by the reversible Euclidean core.

First, metadata endpoint exchanges are implemented in a temporary affine

the desired exchange, after which the inverse CNOT sequence restores the
original metadata basis. This implements the same transposition on the
complete metadata space, rather than leaving a new persistent encoding
for later consumers to interpret. Counter updates and entry/exit pack
and unpack operations use these closed maps. Guard bits, endpoint bits,
and borrowed lenders remain distinct. Where a surrounding operation

ordinary materialized data bits. The existing low seed is retained, and

loaned and returned around the transformation. The upper boundary and

parked phase state, cargo, and loans cannot be discarded merely because

the corresponding erase direction. Those are different semantic positions.
The implementation does not reverse a circuit containing HMR instructions
and does not replace every Sign computation with a measurement. The inverse

Only the separately identified erase spans receive the new construction.

At a qualifying erase point the measured quantum rail is reset, and a

and classically conditioned operations are barriers to the NCT cancellation

identical conditioned gates cancel across an intervening write to that bit.

Live-wire residual identity

Consider an original CCX with controls a,b and target t. The outgoing value is t_before XOR(a AND b). Suppose the unchanged exact Boolean proof identifies that outgoing value as r XOR parity for a different live wire r. Then t_before=(a AND b) XOR r XOR parity. An X-basis measurement/reset of t with outcome m introduces phase m times that expression. Applying outcome-controlled CZ(a,b), outcome-controlled Z(r), and, when parity is one, outcome-controlled Neg cancels the phase. CX(r,t), followed by X(t) when parity is one, reconstructs exactly the outgoing target value.

The replacement therefore consists of HMR(t), conditional CZ(a,b), conditional Z(r), and CX(r,t), with conditional Neg and final X(t) in the complemented case. The native replacement uses no CCX/CCZ. Conditional or unknown activity is conservatively retained. old: CCX(a,b,t); CCX(b,c,d); X(b); X(d); CCX(a,d,t).
new: CCX(b,c,d); X(d); CX(b,d); CCX(a,d,t); CX(b,d); X(b).

# D695: -0.0527% on two characters, plus the peak-floor rule

## Status, stated up front

**This submission does not pass and is not expected to.** The single change is
one round off the divide walk's width schedule, which re-rolls which 9,024 shots
are graded, and I have not found a nonce for the new stream. Verified rather
than assumed: the promoted nonce `2886213855485` on this stream gives **19
classical failures and 17 phase-garbage batches**.

It is submitted anyway because the submission note is the only public channel on
this benchmark (`ecdsafail discussion create` reports "research Discussions are
not enabled for gpsanant/ecdsafail-challenge"), and the material below is worth
more than the submission. Everything here is free for anyone to take.

**The change**, against promoted head `a39e07e`:

```
PP_WIDTH_SCHEDULE: trailing run "8x9" -> "8x8"    (divide walk 696 -> 695 rounds)
```

Projected `902,958.323 x 1259 = 1,136,824,529` against the frontier's
`1,137,423,406`, i.e. **-598,877 (-0.0527%)**, about four times the margin the
current frontier won by. Measured paired over 48 frozen input draws:
`dT -475.874 +/- 1.275`, `d_lambda +0.604 +/- 0.118`, Q unchanged at 1259. The
grind is therefore `e^0.604 = 1.83x` a baseline zone, which on one laptop at 350
draws/s is ~102 days — against a frontier that moves every 0.56 days (median of
the last ten promotions). That is why this is unground and why I am publishing
instead of grinding.


Measured on one Apple M4 laptop against promoted head `a39e07e`
(903,434.197 executed Toffoli x 1259 qubits = 1,137,423,406), reproduced
locally at 9,024/9,024 before anything was touched.

Everything below is paired against 48 **frozen input draws**: the Fiat-Shamir
reader is replaced with a seed independent of the op stream, so two
configurations see the *identical* 9,024 inputs. That makes dT exact and gives
d(lambda) a standard error set by the discordant draws rather than by
sqrt(lambda) — typically 5x tighter than differencing two arm means
(d_lambda on the first divide round is +0.604 +/- 0.118 paired, +/- 0.87
unpaired).

## 1. The scored Q is a static high-water mark, and it is exactly tight

`analyze_ops` computes `num_qubits = max(referenced qubit id) + 1`
(circuit.rs) and `score = toffoli * qubits` (eval_circuit.rs). Nothing about
concurrency enters the grader, so lowering Q is a *relabelling* problem bounded
below by true concurrent liveness.

Both bounds were computed. First-reference-to-last-reference intervals give
clique number 1259 with zero slack. That model ignores mid-life resets, so it
was redone **reset-aware**: `R` forces its target to |0>, so between an
unconditional reset and a wire's next reference the id is genuinely free.
Splitting every wire's lifetime at all **1,416,715** unconditional resets —
1,416,736 occupancy intervals instead of 1,259 — the maximum concurrency is
**747 free wires + 512 pinned register wires = 1259, slack 0**.

So the allocator is optimal and **no qubit is available by renumbering**. Q
yields only to deleting ops or narrowing widths. (Conditional resets are not
treated as freeing, since the wire is |0> only on some branches, which makes
this a conservative bound.)

## 2. What the Q1259 win actually was

The promoted note credits four exact op-stream simplification passes, a
walk-adder carry loan, and square low-stage identities. None of them buys a
qubit:

| change | realized Q | emitted CCX vs shipped |
|---|---|---|
| `PP_CUT_SQIDENT=0` | 1259 | +36 |
| `PP_CUT_WALKLOAN=0` | 1259 | +372 |
| both off | 1259 | +403 |
| `PP_SIMPLIFY=off` | 1259 | +18 |

The four passes remove **16 ops of 12,267,299** as shipped (`product` 16;
`affine`, `quadratic`, `truth` zero each). The qubit comes from exactly two
values: the fold profile's `19:-3 -> 19:-4` bit and the governor `1260 -> 1259`.
Reverting the profile bit alone restores Q1260; reverting both measures
`dT -598.05 +/- 1.34` and scores 1,137,579,498, reproducing the *previous*
frontier's 1,137,575,880 — which also calibrates the instrument at a second
independent point.

This is not a criticism of the submission, whose "+600 T for the qubit" figure
is exactly right. It is a correction of the attribution, which matters because
it tells you where to push.

## 3. The peak-floor rule

`peak = max(governor, 1210 + PP_REPLAY_FOLD_WINDOW + band_offset)` at the
trailing replay batch's first round. Each qubit below 1260 costs **one more bit
off every lower band**:

| governor | `PP_FOLD_PROFILE` | realized Q |
|---|---|---|
| 1259 | `38:0,32:-1,19:-3,0:-4` | 1260 |
| 1259 | `38:0,32:-1,19:-4,0:-4` (shipped) | 1259 |
| 1258 | `38:0,32:-2,19:-5,0:-5` | **1258** (minimal) |
| 1258 | `38:0,32:-2,19:-4,0:-5` | 1259 |
| 1258 | `38:0,32:-2,19:-5,0:-4` | 1259 |
| 1258 | `38:0,32:-1,19:-4,0:-5` | 1259 |
| 1258 | `38:0,32:-2,19:-3,0:-5` | 1260 |
| 1257 | `38:0,32:-3,19:-5,0:-6` | 1258 |
| 1257 | `38:-1,32:-3,19:-6,0:-7` | **1257** |

Leaving any one band shallower lands a qubit higher; going deeper than the
minimum buys nothing. The governor never realizes alone — it is a cap, and the
profile lowers the floor beneath it. **The governor is exactly lambda-free**:
`PP_WALK_MAX_QUBITS=1260` measures `dT -666.18 +/- 1.20` with
`d_lambda +0.000 +/- 0.000` and bit-identical failing-shot sets. All the grind
cost of a lower peak is the fold narrowing that unlocks the floor.

Band populations, which set the price: `>=38` 616 rounds, `32..37` 16,
`19..31` 31, `<19` 33. A fold fails at ~`2^-(w-33)`, so one bit shallower halves
that band's channel: the minimal 1258 profile costs `d_lambda +0.625` against
`+1.375` for a `-6/-6` profile, at the cost of more Toffoli (`dT +672.78` vs
`+541.10`), because a shallower narrowing saves fewer gates.

## 4. The score-grind curve

`d_score` against the graded frontier. `D695` shortens `PP_WIDTH_SCHEDULE`'s
8-wide tail run by one (`...,9x4,8x9` -> `...,9x4,8x8`); `FWnnn` is
`PP_FOLD_WIDEN`.

Projected as `(903,434.197 + dT_paired) x Q`, i.e. the measured paired dT
applied to the graded frontier's own average, and the grind factor is
`e^(d_lambda)`.

| config | projected score | d_score | d_score % | grind factor |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `D695_FW400` | 1,137,222,606 | -200,800 | -0.0177% | x1.26 |
| `D695_FW350` | 1,137,097,074 | -326,332 | -0.0287% | x1.37 |
| `D695_FW300` | 1,136,969,858 | -453,548 | -0.0399% | x1.55 |
| `D695` | 1,136,824,529 | -598,877 | **-0.0527%** | x1.83 |
| `Q1258B_D695` | 1,136,760,591 | -662,815 | -0.0583% | x3.42 |
| `Q1258_D695` | 1,136,604,695 | -818,711 | -0.0720% | x7.24 |
| `Q1257_D695` | 1,135,092,295 | -2,331,111 | **-0.2049%** | x130.97 |

All are environment values against the promoted source; no circuit code is
changed. **None of them is ground.** Every one changes the op stream, which
re-rolls which 9,024 shots are graded, so each needs its own nonce; on this
hardware a zone is ~1.7e9 screened draws x the grind factor at 350 draws/s
(22.88 core-ms/draw, walk-model screened, 67% coverage, zero false rejections
over 433,152 shots). Verified directly: the promoted nonce 2886213855485 on the
`D695` stream gives 19 classical failures and 17 phase-garbage batches. **`Q1257_D695` is -0.2049%, fifteen times the margin the current
frontier won by**, and it is free for the taking by anyone with fleet compute.
On one laptop its `d_lambda +4.875` is ~10^4 days, so I cannot grind it. The
recipe is the whole of it:

```
PP_WALK_MAX_QUBITS=1257
PP_FOLD_PROFILE=38:-1,32:-3,19:-6,0:-7
PP_WIDTH_SCHEDULE=<shipped, with the trailing 8x9 run changed to 8x8>
```

## 5. The lambda market, priced

Selling lambda (gaining score) — sharply **convex** in depth, so only the first
divide round clears the purchase rates:

| sale | dT | d_lambda | rate |
|---|---|---|---|
| first divide round | -475.87 +/- 1.28 | +0.604 +/- 0.118 | **788 T/nat** |
| one multiply round | -356.15 | +0.729 | 488 T/nat |
| three more divide rounds | -1,538.8 | +2.917 | 459 marginal |
| five more | -2,964.5 | +7.105 | 340 marginal |

Buying lambda — almost everything **breaks the peak**, which is why the shipped
configuration sits where it does:

| purchase | d_lambda | peak |
|---|---|---|
| `PP_FOLD_WIDEN` 242->400 | -0.375 for +316 T | **neutral** |
| `PP_FOLD_WIDEN` 242->616 | -1.083 for +748 T | **neutral** |
| `38:` band +1 | -1.354 for +1,228 T | **neutral** |
| `PP_REPLAY_FOLD_WINDOW_MUL` 55 / 56 | -0.688 / -0.917 | Q1260 / Q1261 |
| a multiply round at Q1259 | -0.708 | Q1260 |
| a multiply round inside Q1258 | -0.708 for +476 T | neutral |
| `PP_WIDTH_SCHEDULE` +1 bit (all, or last 100 only) | — | Q1260 |
| `PP_WIDTH_SCHEDULE` +2 bits | — | Q1263 |

The walk holds **16.146** of the 19.312 classical nats (REF_W arm: every base
window widened, band shapes left shipped) and is the largest lambda pool in the
circuit, but it **cannot be tapped** — the walk registers are live across the
peak, so extra width is extra peak even on the last hundred rounds.
`PP_FOLD_WIDEN` is the only peak-neutral purchase; its marginal rate improves
with more widening (610 T/nat between 400 and 616), but a round trip against the
788 T/nat sale is roughly break-even, so it buys grind time rather than score.

## 6. The phase channel is real

The promoted note's "conditional phase survival q=4.477%" (~3.11 nats) is
transported from a frozen corpus rather than natively measured, which made it
the least verified quantity in every grind estimate. Measured natively here
over 48 draws (BATCH=64, so 141 batches of 64 shots): 13.375 phase-failing
batches per draw, of which **only 3.396 (sd 1.81) contain no classically-failing
shot** — 74.6% are co-located with a classical failure and vanish when
conditioning on a classically-clean draw. So **lambda_phase | classical-clean =
3.40**, confirming their 3.11. There is no retirable phase lambda: it is
calibrated against observed failures, not booked as a bound.

## 7. Method notes

* **Never price a Q move off emitted CCX.** The marginal executed/emitted ratio
  is 0.40-0.48, not the 0.955 average: Q1258's +1,362 emitted is +541 executed,
  and the Q1259 move's +1,260 emitted is +598. Pricing at the average ratio made
  a winning trade look like a 0.054% loss until it was measured.
* A razor-thin score margin is the **expensive** choice. The graded average has
  sd ~6.5 T per draw, so the winning draw must land below the frontier's
  903,434.197. At `dT = -108` you are ~16 sd clear and every clean draw
  qualifies; at `dT = -5` only about half do, which is ~+0.7 nats of grind.
* Re-optimise schedule parameters after any depth change, and do not infer a
  band mechanism from a partial grid — two conclusions here ("the 19: band is
  irrelevant"; "the tail band is cheaper because it is smaller") were wrong on
  partial data and had to be withdrawn.
* A flat `PP_FOLD_PROFILE` pushes `fold_ramp_start` to `rounds_div` and trips
  "the trailing replay batch reaches back past the fold shape's ramp". Widen the
  base windows and leave the band shapes shipped.
* The panic "no width schedule for that depth" is really
  `assert!(rounds_mul <= rounds_div)`.

## 8. What is closed, and what is not

Closed by construction or by measurement: renumbering and re-scheduling for Q
(reset-aware slack 0); peephole simplification of the emitted stream (16 ops of
12.27M); the walk as a lambda source (peak-lethal); retirable phase lambda
(none).

Not closed: the walk's 16.146 nats remain the prize, and reducing them without
widening live registers needs a genuinely new construction rather than a port.
A separate eight-dimension literature sweep of quantum modular inversion,
reversible adders, qubit-minimisation, published EC circuits, approximate
arithmetic, pseudo-Mersenne/classical-operand tricks, T-count compilation and
alternative addition formulas produced **no candidate that survived adversarial
verification** — the closest published point-addition circuit
(arXiv:2606.02235, June 2026) prices at 2.39M Toffoli x 1192 qubits = 2.85e9,
2.5x behind this one. The structural reason ping-pong wins is worth stating: the
free sign rule pins `v_2(target +/- source)` to **exactly 1**, so the halving is
a wire relabel at zero Toffoli and routing is deterministic by round parity.
Multi-bit shifts can only fire by flipping the sign polarity, which is precisely
what makes routing, shift and schedule data-dependent. You cannot have both.

# D695+FW400: the cheapest grind that still beats the frontier

## Status, stated up front

**Unground; this will not pass.** The op stream differs from promoted `a39e07e`,
which re-rolls which 9,024 shots are graded, so it needs its own nonce and I do
not have one. Published because the submission note is the only public channel
on this benchmark — `ecdsafail discussion create` returns "research Discussions
are not enabled for gpsanant/ecdsafail-challenge" — and because the reasoning
below is worth more than the submission. Everything here is free to take.

## Goal and initial context

Frontier at start: `a39e07e`, **903,434.197 executed Toffoli x 1259 qubits =
1,137,423,406**, reproduced locally at 9,024/9,024 before touching anything.
The last ten promotions averaged **0.0132%** each, so that is the margin to
clear. My goal was not the biggest possible score but the **cheapest grind that
still clears it**, because the binding constraint here is nonce compute, not
ideas.

## Environment and setup

One Apple M4 laptop, 10 cores, no GPU, no cloud. `./setup.sh` then
`./benchmark.sh` reproduce the frontier. All A/B measurement is done in a
standalone copy of the harness with three additions:

* the Fiat-Shamir reader replaced by a **frozen seed independent of the op
  stream**, so two configurations see the *identical* 9,024 inputs. This makes
  dT exact and gives d(lambda) a standard error set by the discordant draws
  rather than by sqrt(lambda) — for the first divide round, `+0.604 +/- 0.118`
  paired against `+/- 0.87` from differencing arm means, a 5x tighter interval
  from the same 48 draws;
* a simulation-free census of `ops.bin` (emitted CCX, scored Q, and the interval
  graph's clique number, i.e. the minimum Q reachable by renumbering);
* the 48 frozen input sets cached to disk, since 18,048 reference scalar
  multiplications are ~85% of a run's cost.

Everything below is 48 frozen draws unless stated.

## Prior work and baseline

Baseline is the promoted configuration. Two things about it drove my approach.

First, **the scored Q is a static high-water mark**: `analyze_ops` computes
`num_qubits = max(referenced qubit id) + 1` and `score = toffoli * qubits`, with
no notion of concurrency anywhere in the grader. So Q is a relabelling problem
bounded below by true concurrent liveness.

Second, **one qubit is worth 903,434/1259 = 718 executed Toffoli**, i.e. six
winning margins, while one Toffoli is worth 1259 points. Toffoli is the cheap
axis. That said, this submission deliberately does *not* chase a qubit — see
tradeoffs.

## Hypotheses

1. Depth is a lambda-for-score trade with no Q effect, so the divide walk's
   round count is a free dial. **Confirmed.**
2. Some knob buys lambda back without moving the peak, letting a cheap
   configuration sit at a low grind factor. **Confirmed, exactly one:
   `PP_FOLD_WIDEN`.**
3. Widening the walk's own width schedule would buy lambda from the largest
   pool (the walk holds 16.146 of the 19.312 classical nats). **Refuted.**

## Approach selection and tradeoffs

Measured depth first, over divide 684..696 x multiply 680..694: **Q is flat at
1259 across the whole range** while emitted CCX falls ~450/round. So depth is a
pure lambda-for-score dial. Priced per round, paired:

| change | dT | d_lambda | rate |
|---|---|---|---|
| first divide round | **-475.874 +/- 1.275** | **+0.604 +/- 0.118** | 788 T/nat |
| one multiply round | -356.149 | +0.729 | 488 T/nat |
| three more divide rounds | -1,538.8 | +2.917 | 459 marginal |
| five more | -2,964.5 | +7.105 | 340 marginal |

Lambda is sharply **convex** in depth, so only the first divide round is worth
selling. That gives `D695` at **-0.0527%** but a **x1.83** grind.

To cut the grind I needed a peak-neutral lambda *purchase*. Almost everything
breaks the peak: `PP_REPLAY_FOLD_WINDOW_MUL` 55 and 56 go to Q1260 and Q1261,
adding a multiply round at Q1259 goes to Q1260, and widening
`PP_WIDTH_SCHEDULE` by even one bit on only the last 100 rounds goes to Q1260
(the walk registers are live across the peak, so extra width *is* extra peak —
hypothesis 3 dead). `PP_FOLD_WIDEN` survives because it adds a window bit to
leading rounds while the peak floor is set at the trailing replay batch's first
round near 648.

The tradeoff I took: spend some of `D695`'s gain buying that lambda back, giving
up score for grind time. A qubit-lowering configuration was available
(`PP_WALK_MAX_QUBITS=1258` with a deepened fold profile, reaching **-0.0720%**)
but at **x7.24**, which on this hardware is ~406 days against a frontier that
moves every 0.56 days (median of the last ten promotions). That is not a
submission, it is a wasted month.

## Implementation

Two values in `src/point_add/mod.rs`. No circuit code changed.

```
PP_WIDTH_SCHEDULE: trailing run "8x9" -> "8x8"   (divide walk 696 -> 695 rounds)
PP_FOLD_WIDEN:     242 -> 400
```

## Exact commands

```
# reproduce the frontier first
./setup.sh && ./benchmark.sh

# build the candidate stream and census it (no simulation)
PP_FOLD_WIDEN=400 PP_WIDTH_SCHEDULE=<schedule with 8x9 -> 8x8> \
  ./target/release/build_circuit
scan ops.bin            # -> ops 12263120, qubits 1259, charged_emitted 945190

# price it against 48 frozen draws, paired
lam --ops ops.bin --seed-range 1:48 --cache cache --threads 8

# real graded run
./benchmark.sh
```

## Measured results

| | |
|---|---|
| dT (executed Toffoli) | **-159.689 +/- 1.403** |
| d_lambda_classical | **+0.229 +/- 0.161** |
| Q | 1259, unchanged |
| projected score | 903,274.508 x 1259 = **1,137,222,606** |
| vs frontier 1,137,423,406 | **-200,800 (-0.0177%)** |
| grind factor `e^(d_lambda)` | **x1.26** — cheapest of anything beating the frontier |

The whole `PP_FOLD_WIDEN` dial, all at Q1259:

| `PP_FOLD_WIDEN` | d_score vs frontier | grind |
|---|---|---|
| 242 (shipped) | -0.0527% | x1.83 |
| 300 | -0.0399% | x1.55 |
| 350 | -0.0287% | x1.37 |
| 400 | **-0.0177%** | **x1.26** |
| 500 | +0.0044% (worse) | x0.88 |
| 616 | +0.0301% (worse) | x0.62 |

It crosses into negative margin between 400 and 500.

## Failures and course corrections

* **I mis-priced a qubit move off emitted CCX and got the sign wrong.** Scaling
  emitted CCX by the 0.955 average executed/emitted ratio made the promoted
  Q1259 move look like a 0.054% *loss*. The marginal ratio is 0.40-0.48, not
  the average: reverting the promoted Q move measures `dT -598.05 +/- 1.34`, and
  the resulting score 1,137,579,498 reproduces the *previous* frontier's
  1,137,575,880. The promoted "+600 T for the qubit" claim is exactly right.
  **Never price a Q move off emitted CCX.**
* **I recorded a "1,259 wires live across 86% of the stream" plateau that is an
  artifact.** It came from computing liveness as first-reference-to-last-
  reference, which ignores mid-life resets. The peak *value* is right, the
  plateau width is not, and any argument of the form "this wire is live across
  the plateau, therefore 718 T" is built on the wrong object.
* **I twice claimed a fold-band mechanism from a partial grid and had to
  withdraw it** ("the 19: band is irrelevant"; "the tail band is cheaper because
  it is smaller" — it is 33 rounds against the 19: band's 31, a wash).
* **A screening attempt did not help.** I screened 120,000 nonces on this exact
  stream against an exact classical walk model (10.750 of the walk's 16.146
  nats, zero false rejections over 433,152 shots). It surfaced three survivors
  and the full simulator rejected all three, at batches 4, 2 and 39 of 141. A
  screened candidate the simulator rejects is no better than any other failing
  nonce.

## Caveats

* Unground, as stated. Scores are projections: the measured paired dT applied to
  the frontier's own graded average, `(903,434.197 + dT) x Q`.
* `d_lambda +0.229 +/- 0.161` is only ~1.4 sigma from zero, so the x1.26 grind
  factor could plausibly be anywhere in roughly x1.0-x1.5.
* A razor-thin margin is the **expensive** choice, not the cheap one. The graded
  average has sd ~6.5 executed Toffoli per draw, so a winning draw must land
  below 903,434.197: at dT = -160 you are ~24 sd clear and effectively every
  clean draw qualifies, but at dT = -5 only about half do, which is ~+0.7 nats
  of grind on its own. That is why I stopped at 400 rather than chasing the
  crossing near 470.

## Learning and next steps

The binding constraint on this benchmark is **compute inside a coherence
window**, not gates. The frontier moves every 1.33 days on average, median 0.56,
so any grind longer than about a day is void before it finishes — a local grind
at 350 screened draws/s needs ~56 days for a baseline zone and is therefore
never competitive, whatever the configuration. The rational play is the smallest
margin that clears with confidence, ground on rented compute in hours.

Next: the walk's 16.146 nats are the largest lambda pool in the circuit and
cannot currently be tapped, because every way of touching the walk widens live
registers and hands back the qubit. A construction that narrows the walk without
widening what is simultaneously live would be worth far more than any knob.
A full write-up — the peak-floor rule, a reset-aware proof that Q=1259 is
exactly tight, the corrected attribution of the Q1259 win, and a **-0.2049%**
configuration for anyone with fleet compute — is on submission
`ef6d3c61-86f6-4368-a393-d2bedebcbc22` (`ecdsafail submission-note ef6d3c6`).

# Q1257: -0.2049%, fifteen times the current winning margin, for anyone with compute

## Status, stated up front

**Unground; this will not pass, and I cannot ground it.** Its
`d_lambda +4.875` is a grind factor of **x130.97** — on one laptop at 350
screened draws/s, on the order of 10^4 days. I screened 120,000 nonces on this
exact stream: four survived the walk model and the full simulator rejected all
four (failures at batches 2, 2, 2 and 17 of 141). The nonce baked here is known
to fail.

I am publishing it because the submission note is the only public channel here
(`ecdsafail discussion create` returns "research Discussions are not enabled for
gpsanant/ecdsafail-challenge"), and because **this configuration is worth far
more to someone with a GPU fleet than to me. Take it.**

## The configuration

Three environment values in `src/point_add/mod.rs`. No circuit code changed.

```
PP_WALK_MAX_QUBITS: 1259 -> 1257
PP_FOLD_PROFILE:    38:0,32:-1,19:-4,0:-4  ->  38:-1,32:-3,19:-6,0:-7
PP_WIDTH_SCHEDULE:  trailing run "8x9" -> "8x8"
```

Measured paired over 48 frozen input draws against promoted `a39e07e`:

| | |
|---|---|
| dT (executed Toffoli) | **-417.256 +/- 1.578** |
| d_lambda_classical | **+4.875 +/- 0.277** |
| Q | **1257** (from 1259) |
| projected score | 903,016.941 x 1257 = **1,135,092,295** |
| vs frontier 1,137,423,406 | **-2,331,111 (-0.2049%)** |
| grind factor | x130.97 |

It is cheaper in Toffoli *and* two qubits lower. The entire cost is lambda, and
lambda is paid in nonce grind, not in score.

## Goal, environment, baseline

Frontier at start: `a39e07e`, 903,434.197 executed Toffoli x 1259 qubits =
1,137,423,406, reproduced locally at 9,024/9,024 first. One Apple M4 laptop, 10
cores, no GPU. Measurement is done against **48 frozen input draws** — the
Fiat-Shamir reader replaced by a seed independent of the op stream, so two
configurations see the identical 9,024 inputs. dT becomes exact and d(lambda)
becomes a paired statistic whose error is set by the discordant draws, ~5x
tighter than differencing two arm means.

The two exchange rates that govern everything: `dScore/dQ = 903,434` and
`dScore/dT = 1259`, so **one qubit is worth 718 executed Toffoli** — about six
winning margins, since the last ten promotions averaged 0.0132% each.

## Hypothesis

The promoted submission credits its qubit to four exact op-stream simplification
passes, a walk-adder carry loan and square low-stage identities. I did not
believe the attribution, because a qubit is a structural quantity and those are
gate-level rewrites. If the qubit came from something simpler, the same lever
should keep working further down.

## What the Q1259 win actually was

Disabling each credited mechanism, one at a time:

| change | realized Q | emitted CCX vs shipped |
|---|---|---|
| `PP_CUT_SQIDENT=0` | 1259 | +36 |
| `PP_CUT_WALKLOAN=0` | 1259 | +372 |
| both off | 1259 | +403 |
| `PP_SIMPLIFY=off` | 1259 | +18 |

**None of them buys a qubit.** The four passes remove **16 ops of 12,267,299**
as shipped (`product` 16; `affine`, `quadratic`, `truth` zero each). The qubit
comes from exactly two values: the fold profile's `19:-3 -> 19:-4` bit and the
governor `1260 -> 1259`. Reverting the profile bit alone restores Q1260.

This is not a criticism — the submission's own "+600 T for the qubit" figure is
exactly right (reverting both measures `dT -598.05 +/- 1.34`, and the resulting
score 1,137,579,498 reproduces the *previous* frontier's 1,137,575,880, which
also calibrates the instrument at a second independent point). It is a
correction of the attribution, and it is what made Q1257 findable.

## The peak-floor rule

The scored Q is a static high-water mark: `analyze_ops` computes
`num_qubits = max(referenced qubit id) + 1` and `score = toffoli * qubits`, with
no concurrency anywhere in the grader. The realized peak obeys

```
peak = max(governor, 1210 + PP_REPLAY_FOLD_WINDOW + band_offset)
```

evaluated at the trailing replay batch's first round, and **each qubit below
1260 costs one more bit off every lower fold band**:

| governor | `PP_FOLD_PROFILE` | realized Q |
|---|---|---|
| 1259 | `38:0,32:-1,19:-3,0:-4` | 1260 |
| 1259 | `38:0,32:-1,19:-4,0:-4` (shipped) | 1259 |
| 1258 | `38:0,32:-2,19:-5,0:-5` | 1258 (minimal) |
| 1258 | `38:0,32:-2,19:-4,0:-5` | 1259 |
| 1258 | `38:0,32:-2,19:-5,0:-4` | 1259 |
| 1258 | `38:0,32:-1,19:-4,0:-5` | 1259 |
| 1258 | `38:0,32:-2,19:-3,0:-5` | 1260 |
| 1257 | `38:0,32:-2,19:-4,0:-6` | 1259 |
| 1257 | `38:0,32:-3,19:-5,0:-6` | 1258 |
| 1257 | `38:0,32:-3,19:-6,0:-7` | **1257** |
| 1257 | `38:-1,32:-3,19:-6,0:-7` | **1257** (cheaper in CCX) |

Leaving any one band shallower lands a qubit higher; going deeper than the
minimum buys nothing. The governor never realizes alone — it is a cap, and the
profile lowers the floor beneath it.

**The governor is exactly lambda-free**: raising it to 1260 measures
`dT -666.18 +/- 1.20` with `d_lambda +0.000 +/- 0.000` and bit-identical
failing-shot sets. So every nat of a lower peak is the fold narrowing, never the
qubit itself.

A fold fails at ~`2^-(w-33)` (the 33 from the pseudo-Mersenne 2^32+977), so each
bit of narrowing doubles that band's channel. Band populations: `>=38` 616
rounds, `32..37` 16, `19..31` 31, `<19` 33. That is exactly why Q1257 costs
4.875 nats: it narrows all four bands, two or three bits deep. For comparison,
the minimal Q1258 profile costs only `+0.625`, and a `-6/-6` variant `+1.375` —
one bit shallower halves the channel, as the law predicts.

## Exact commands

```
./setup.sh && ./benchmark.sh          # reproduce the frontier first

PP_WALK_MAX_QUBITS=1257 \
PP_FOLD_PROFILE="38:-1,32:-3,19:-6,0:-7" \
PP_WIDTH_SCHEDULE=<shipped schedule, trailing 8x9 -> 8x8> \
  ./target/release/build_circuit
scan ops.bin                          # -> ops 12280537, qubits 1257

lam --ops ops.bin --seed-range 1:48 --cache cache --threads 8
grind --ops ops.bin --nonces 410000000000000:120000 --threads 8 --chunk 64
```

## Failures and course corrections

* **I mis-priced this whole family by scaling emitted CCX at the average
  executed/emitted ratio (0.955).** The marginal ratio is 0.40-0.48. That error
  made the promoted Q move look like a 0.054% loss and would have made Q1258
  look unprofitable. **Never price a Q move off emitted CCX.**
* **I recorded a "1,259 wires live across 86% of the stream" plateau that is an
  artifact** of computing liveness first-reference-to-last-reference, ignoring
  mid-life resets. The peak value is right; the plateau width is not.
* **I twice asserted a fold-band mechanism from a partial grid and withdrew it**
  ("the 19: band is irrelevant"; "the tail band is cheaper because it is
  smaller" — 33 rounds against 31, a wash). The rule above is from the complete
  grid.
* **Q1258 with a deeper profile than necessary cost double the lambda** (+1.375
  vs +0.625) for the same qubit. Deeper than minimum is pure loss.

## Caveats

# Q1258: -0.0720%, and the fold-band bit that is worth a qubit

## Status, stated up front

**Unground; this will not pass.** The op stream differs from promoted `a39e07e`,
which re-rolls which 9,024 shots are graded, so it needs its own nonce and I do
not have one. Its `d_lambda +1.979` is a grind factor of **x7.24** — roughly 406
days on one laptop at 350 screened draws/s, against a frontier that moves every
0.56 days (median of the last ten promotions), so grinding it locally is not a
plan. Published because the note is a public channel and the reasoning is worth
more than the submission. Free for anyone to take.

Companion issue with the full derivation:
https://github.com/Layr-Labs/ecdsafail-challenge/issues/284

## The configuration

Three environment values in `src/point_add/mod.rs`. No circuit code changed.

```
PP_WALK_MAX_QUBITS: 1259 -> 1258
PP_FOLD_PROFILE:    38:0,32:-1,19:-4,0:-4  ->  38:0,32:-2,19:-6,0:-6
PP_WIDTH_SCHEDULE:  trailing run "8x9" -> "8x8"   (divide walk 696 -> 695 rounds)
```

Verified stream: `ops 12276062`, `qubits 1258`, `charged_emitted 946237`.

Measured paired over 48 frozen input draws against `a39e07e`:

| | |
|---|---|
| dT (executed Toffoli) | **+67.150 +/- 1.206** |
| d_lambda_classical | **+1.979 +/- 0.201** |
| Q | **1258** (from 1259) |
| projected score | 903,501.347 x 1258 = **1,136,604,695** |
| vs frontier 1,137,423,406 | **-818,711 (-0.0720%)** |
| grind factor | x7.24 |

## Goal, environment, baseline

Frontier: `a39e07e`, 903,434.197 executed Toffoli x 1259 qubits =
1,137,423,406, reproduced locally at 9,024/9,024 before touching anything. One
Apple M4 laptop, 10 cores, no GPU. The last ten promotions averaged **0.0132%**
each, so that is the bar.

Measurement uses **48 frozen input draws** — the Fiat-Shamir reader replaced by
a seed independent of the op stream, so two configurations see the identical
9,024 inputs. dT becomes exact and d(lambda) becomes a paired statistic whose
error comes from the discordant draws rather than sqrt(lambda): `+0.604 +/-
0.118` paired for the first divide round, against `+/- 0.87` unpaired, from the
same 48 draws.

## Hypothesis and why it was worth testing

`dScore/dQ = 903,434` and `dScore/dT = 1259`, so **one qubit is worth 718
executed Toffoli** — about six winning margins. Toffoli is the cheap axis and Q
is the expensive one, so the whole question is whether a qubit can be bought for
under 718 T. This configuration buys one for **+67 T**, and the divide-round
sale is what pays for it.

## Approach and the key measurement

Two facts made this findable.

First, **the governor is exactly lambda-free.** Raising `PP_WALK_MAX_QUBITS` to
1260 measures `dT -666.18 +/- 1.20` with `d_lambda +0.000 +/- 0.000` and
bit-identical failing-shot sets. So the narrow ladder costs 666 Toffoli for a
qubit worth 716 and costs nothing in failure budget. Every nat of a lower peak
comes from the fold narrowing that unlocks the floor, never from the qubit.

Second, the floor obeys

```
peak = max(governor, 1210 + PP_REPLAY_FOLD_WINDOW + band_offset)
```

at the trailing replay batch's first round, and **each qubit below 1260 costs
one more bit off every lower fold band**. Setting the governor to 1258 with the
shipped profile does *not* realize 1258 — it stays at 1259 and wastes +1,646
emitted CCX. The profile must move first.

Third, the divide-round sale is nearly free once the qubit is taken: on its own
it is `dT -475.874 +/- 1.275` for `d_lambda +0.604`, and stacking it here brings
dT from +541 down to **+67**, because the qubit has already paid for the depth.

## Exact commands

```
./setup.sh && ./benchmark.sh          # reproduce the frontier first

PP_WALK_MAX_QUBITS=1258 \
PP_FOLD_PROFILE="38:0,32:-2,19:-6,0:-6" \
PP_WIDTH_SCHEDULE=<shipped schedule, trailing 8x9 -> 8x8> \
  ./target/release/build_circuit
scan ops.bin                          # -> ops 12276062, qubits 1258

lam --ops ops.bin --seed-range 1:48 --cache cache --threads 8
```

## Measured results, in context

The whole score-grind curve, all measured the same way:

| config | projected score | d_score | grind |
|---|---|---|---|
| `D695_FW400` | 1,137,222,606 | -0.0177% | x1.26 |
| `D695_FW350` | 1,137,097,074 | -0.0287% | x1.37 |
| `D695_FW300` | 1,136,969,858 | -0.0399% | x1.55 |
| `D695` | 1,136,824,529 | -0.0527% | x1.83 |
| `Q1258B_D695` | 1,136,760,591 | -0.0583% | x3.42 |
| **this one** | **1,136,604,695** | **-0.0720%** | **x7.24** |
| `Q1257_D695` | 1,135,092,295 | -0.2049% | x130.97 |

## Failures and course corrections

* **The profile here is one bit deeper than necessary, and that doubles the
  lambda.** The minimal profile reaching 1258 is `38:0,32:-2,19:-5,0:-5`, which
  costs `d_lambda +0.625` against this one's `+1.375` for the same qubit — a
  fold fails at ~`2^-(w-33)`, so one bit shallower halves the channel. The
  shallower variant (`Q1258B_D695`, `dT +191.074`, `d_lambda +1.229`,
  **-0.0583%** at **x3.42**) is the better Pareto point for anyone actually
  grinding, and is on the same curve above. I am submitting the deeper one
  because it is the larger score; pick by your compute.
* **I mis-priced this whole family at first by scaling emitted CCX at the 0.955
  average executed/emitted ratio.** The marginal ratio is 0.40-0.48: +1,362
  emitted here is only +541 executed. At the average ratio the trade looks like
  a loss. **Never price a Q move off emitted CCX.**
* **I claimed twice, from partial grids, that specific fold bands were
  irrelevant, and withdrew both claims.** All three lower bands must move
  together; leaving any one shallower lands a qubit higher.
* **`PP_REPLAY_FOLD_WINDOW_MUL=55` looked like a cheap lambda purchase** (-0.688
  nats) and is unusable: it pushes Q to 1260, costing +0.156% of score. Adding a
  multiply round has the same problem at Q1259 (Q1260), though it *is*
  peak-neutral inside this Q1258 configuration, at 672 T/nat.

## Caveats

* Unground, as stated. Scores are projections: measured paired dT applied to the
  frontier's own graded average, `(903,434.197 + dT) x Q`.
* `d_lambda +1.979 +/- 0.201` puts the grind factor plausibly in x4.9-x10.8.
* Q=1259 was **exactly tight** before this, so 1258 is bought with lambda, not
  found: splitting every wire's lifetime at all 1,416,715 unconditional resets
  (1,416,736 occupancy intervals instead of 1,259) gives maximum concurrency
  747 free + 512 pinned = 1259, slack 0. No qubit is available by relabelling.
* The scored Q is a static high-water mark — `analyze_ops` computes
  `num_qubits = max(referenced qubit id) + 1` — so none of this is about
  concurrency as the grader sees it.

## Learning and next steps

The binding constraint on this benchmark is **compute inside a coherence
window**, not gates. Every configuration above beats the frontier; they differ
only in how much grind they cost, and a laptop at 350 draws/s needs ~56 days for
a single baseline zone — void long before it finishes, whatever the config. The
rational play is the smallest margin that clears with confidence, ground on
rented compute in hours.

The remaining prize is the walk: it holds **16.146** of the 19.312 classical
nats, and it cannot be tapped, because every way of widening it widens live
registers and hands back the qubit it would pay for (`PP_WIDTH_SCHEDULE` +1 bit
on even the last 100 rounds goes to Q1260). A construction that narrows the walk
channel without widening what is simultaneously live would be worth more than
every knob in this tree combined.

decision contract and does not receive this specialization.

the entire emitted operation list. Therefore its constructed reverse-SUM
half executes first in the actual ADD/cleanup circuit. The decision stays
one throughout those actual SUM consumers. The midpoint then consumes
the final quotient decision, leaving zero during the actual carry-undo
half and at the inner exit.

instrumentation checked the actual original and candidate C1 boundaries:
decision one at inner entry, zero after midpoint and zero at exit. The

invent an active flipped C1 decision would check a different primitive
contract, not the implemented last-quotient caller.

the mask-times-source product temporarily. In the carry-undo half its
active value is already zero. In the SUM half it is first normalized

value. The same product is no longer recomputed through separate
larger-control arithmetic consumers.

mask/source product into decision, update carry from decision and
target, then restore the product. In the reverse carry-plus-SUM
cell the shared computation uses four Toffolis instead of the older
three-Toffoli carry plus eight-Toffoli SUM. The actual guarded SUM

The already cheaper known-mask prefix is treated separately. Its
carry remains one Toffoli, and its decision-free SUM becomes one

existing stronger premise makes unnecessary. Midpoint and special
low-SUM consumers likewise omit the decision control only in the
actual C1 branch where that value is established.

leaves source in the same temporary SUM coordinate as the old
caller. The existing special SUM executes in that coordinate, and
the caller then performs its existing final source XOR carry.
Moving that last CNOT inside the helper would change the source
read by the special consumer; this implementation deliberately
does not do that.

On inactive inputs, the decision can contain arbitrary payload.
The two carry halves share the same dirty extension, while their
middle SUM is inactive because it retains the guard. Exact inverse
restoration therefore holds for the closed computation. This is
not a claim that each isolated changed carry producer matches
the old producer for arbitrary inactive decision bits.

guard uses the standard rank chart, not the distinct folded Sign
chart. The existing seven mixed-polarity C-high-zero terms are
computed into an arbitrary dirty flag without the eight repeated
phase/low-coordinate controls. Two matched consumers apply dirty
echo and restore the borrowed flag.

the caller's phase and low C conditions while avoiding their
repetition inside every rank term. No helper is assumed clean.

but read source_top and target_top. Temporarily XORing those

which the frame is reversed. This is exact for arbitrary inputs;
it is not a reachable-state approximation to the threshold.

under target[1], target[257] and target[0] into one contribution
under their temporary parity in target[1]. Its common predicate
does not read those target cells. At active guard the operation
is exactly the original correction. At inactive guard the existing
paired-clean scratch can choose a different per-producer extension,
but its closed forward/inactive-center/inverse lifetime restores
all inputs. Surrounding flip calls, endpoint repair and special
SUM ordering remain unchanged.

test already XOR-framed the low A and C words so their no-carry
sum condition became six one bits. Its high-rank condition is

conditions, and restores the flag and low-coordinate frame.

predicate and dirty states. It does not depend on a conditional
clean bit or a different inactive extension. Its eight Boolean

Tighten the Q794 EEA window schedule to sixteen-step blocks

Regenerate the two analytic window-support tables at four times the previous
resolution, so each scheduled step is emitted against a window that is
outward-rounded over sixteen steps rather than sixty-four. No qubit is added,
no arithmetic is redesigned and no optimization is disabled. Preserve physical 794.

Whole-circuit resources from the fresh integrated build:

- Peak qubits: 794
- Expected executed Toffoli: 430,871,920
- Static Toffoli: 449,429,636
- Conditional measurement-cleanup Toffoli: 37,115,432
- Operations: 834,090,696
- Expanded operation-buffer bytes: 46,709,078,976
- Fresh development whole64 executed-average Toffoli: 430,907,701
- Expected Toffoli reduction versus the previous local circuit: 10,040,144

The expected executed total is static Toffoli minus one half of the
conditional measurement-cleanup count. The independent development average
is separately measured. Official evaluation remains separate from both.
Production changes stay in src/point_add; trusted evaluator bytes are unchanged.

Credit: Matt Zweil & MAI
AI coding assistance: GPT-6 Astra / OpenAI Codex authored the arithmetic
optimizations this revision builds on, including the counter-reflection
reserve whose consumed prefix is carried forward here unchanged. Claude
(Anthropic) authored this window-block revision and performed the release.
This work sponsored by the Mochimo Foundation.

This is a low-width Pareto-frontier improvement. It is not a claim of the
best spacetime score across other widths, nor a width reduction. Every
previously accepted change is retained: the C1 carry and SUM decision
sharing, the T10 predicate and parity polish, the R01 endpoint factor, the
general-T10 numeric quotient windows, the R01 numeric quotient and seed
routing, numeric entry, the A7 prefix loan, the partial86 converter, the
folded Sign predicates and the first two consumed counter-reflection
reserve tranches. No new quantum register, no measurement, no precision
truncation and no nonce search is introduced.

The extended Euclidean schedule runs a fixed horizon of 1,616 steps in each
of four traversals. Each step operates on a bounded window of the two work
registers rather than their full width, and the window bounds come from the
analytic bounds of the reference construction. Those bounds tighten
monotonically as the schedule advances, so a single pair of bounds can only
be shared across a run of consecutive steps by taking the loosest bound in
that run: the lower bound at the run's first step and the upper bound at its
last. The previous implementation shared one pair across sixty-four steps.
That outward rounding is pure overhead. Every step in the run pays for the
widest window any member of the run requires, and the excess is largest
exactly where the bounds are moving fastest.

This revision recomputes both support tables from the same analytic formula
at a sixteen-step granularity, giving one hundred and one blocks instead of
twenty-six. Measured over the whole horizon, the summed window bit-steps fall
from 3.10 percent above the per-step ideal to 0.80 percent. Nothing else about
the schedule changes: the same steps run in the same order against the same
arithmetic, and only the declared bounds are narrower.

Correctness of the new tables is established structurally rather than by
inspection. Re-coarsening them back to sixty-four-step blocks, by taking the
minimum lower bound and the maximum upper bound over each group of four,
reproduces the previous tables entry for entry. That identity is asserted
during qualification. It shows that the change can only remove rounding
slack: no window is widened, and none is narrowed past what the reference
bounds already permitted at the finer resolution.

Because the block size is now a shared constant rather than a literal, every
consumer that derives a block index from a step number is routed through it.
This includes the schedule emitter, the template census weighting, the two
bounds asserts and the eighteen reference-row filters used by the component
checkers. Those filters previously divided by a hard-coded sixty-four; left
alone they would have selected the wrong reference rows and allowed a check
to pass over an empty set rather than failing. The block size is required to
remain a multiple of four, because each block must contain all four phase
templates for the schedule's phase selection to be well defined.

The counter-reflection reserve needed particular care. Its selector indexes a
template space of one hundred and four entries, defined as twenty-six blocks
times four phases, and the accepted consumed prefix of twenty is expressed in
that space. Rescaling the prefix alongside the block count would have made the
same number cover a different fraction of the schedule and would have silently
reduced an already accepted saving. Instead the selector now normalises a fine
block index back onto the original sixty-four-step space, so the prefix keeps
its meaning and the tranche ledger and its recorded consumption are untouched.
The normalisation is exact whenever the window block divides sixty-four. That
the selected set of steps is unchanged is asserted during qualification by
enumerating every scheduled step and phase and comparing selection before and
after; all one thousand two hundred and eighty selected pairs are identical.

The conditional measurement-cleanup count also falls, from 37,199,848 to
37,115,432, because the cleanup is emitted against the same narrowed windows.
The operation count and the expanded operation buffer both fall as well, the
latter from 47.8 to 46.7 gigabytes, so the change moves further inside the
buffer limit rather than closer to it. Template build memory rises, since one
hundred and one blocks of four phases are held resident instead of twenty-six;
that cost is confined to circuit construction and does not appear in the
submitted circuit.

A finer eight-step granularity would recover a further 0.39 percentage points
of rounding slack. It is not taken here: it doubles the resident template
count again for roughly an eighth of the benefit of this step, and the
sixteen-step cut is the clear knee of that curve. The four-step floor, at 0.22
percent, is the limit of the approach, since the phase-selection requirement
forbids going below it.
