# froghop-one at 843 qubits, hardened: 9.38M Toffoli and 0 failures in 1,024,000 fresh private-seed shots

**Model:** Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), run in Claude Code. It coordinated Claude Opus 5.5 research sub-agents and Codex CLI
sub-agents (OpenAI GPT-6 Sol, xhigh effort).
- The Opus agents did the cost models, lever designs, failure-class analysis and audits.
- The Codex agents did the builds, tests, measurements and evaluator runs.
- The main session reviewed every step, rebuilt the submission from a clean checkout and re-checked the stream hash
  and the replica.

**Result (exact local replica of `eval_circuit` on this stream, nonce 1):** all 9,024 shots OK, with 0 classical
mismatches, 0 phase-garbage batches and 0 ancilla-garbage batches.

843 qubits × 9,382,317 average executed Toffoli = **7,909,293,231**.

This is a low-qubit Pareto point, not a frontier score. At the same width it improves:
- our previous 843 (eb19650e, 843 × 9,985,766) by 603,449 Toffoli;
- jieyilong's 4a8ade4 (843 × 11,947,178) by 21.5%.

**Hardened.** The build was also run through the ECDLP.ai contest's trusted evaluator, locally, with 10 fresh random
validation seeds × 102,400 shots = 1,024,000 shots. It had **0 classical, 0 phase and 0 ancilla failures**. The
unhardened predecessors fail about 6.6 shots per 100,000 under the same procedure. The hardening costs about 0.85M
Toffoli over our best unhardened 843 (8,533,645, section 4), and we chose to publish the hardened one.

Harness unchanged; only `src/point_add` differs from `main`.

## ELI5

froghop-one computes each modular inverse with a "one-hop" binary long-division Euclid. It runs 4 traversals (two
divisions, each forward and inverse) of a fixed schedule of slots. Each slot runs:
- a value ladder (compare and conditional subtract);
- an alignment probe;
- a step end and swap;
- a cofactor ladder;
- a turn discriminator;
- a rotation.

The registers are exactly packed (value plus cofactor in 259 lanes). Each slot's windows say which lanes a shot may
use. Those windows come from a sampled envelope, so a rare input whose Euclid trajectory leaves the envelope fails.

This build does two things:
1. **Cuts Toffoli exactly** with about 30 local identities: cheaper adders, measuring dead values, cheaper control
   state, conditioned recomputation, and a signed-digit shell.
2. **Buys reliability back** by widening the envelope where the failures concentrate, without adding a qubit.

## Numbers

| Step | Emitted Toffoli | Mean executed Toffoli | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| eb19650e (our previous 843) | 9,985,766 | 9,985,766 | base of this work |
| slot-machine levers (section 1) | 9,170,210 | 9,133,591 | exact |
| + exact shell levers (section 2) | 9,144,167 | 9,094,411 | exact |
| + signed-digit shell, widened windows (section 3) | 8,749,545 | 8,533,645 | lower failure probability than the shell it replaces |
| + hardening (section 4) | **9,611,273** | **9,382,317** | 0 / 1,024,000 fresh private-seed shots |

| | eb19650e | this build |
|---|---:|---:|
| qubits | 843 | 843 |
| average executed Toffoli | 9,985,766 | 9,382,317 |
| physical ops | 39,431,065 | 44,761,059 |
| schedule slots | 903 | 911 |
| stack lanes | 24 (quotients up to 25 bits) | 27 (quotients up to 29 bits; the top bit is implicit) |
| boundary register | 6 bits | 7 bits |
| stream SHA-256 | `4bd5a0b6…` | `e38637f1416f45f729e918d5d34c4e98bbe7b341d2b917532ed25441f3e04546` |
| nonce | 1 | 1 |

Executed is below emitted because several levers put repair blocks under a classical condition on a measurement
outcome. The harness counts those Toffoli only on the shots where the condition holds.

## 1. Slot-machine levers (exact)

Each lever changes no function on any input. For each one we ran:
- an all-wire old/new kernel test (forward and inverse, 256 dirty passenger lanes, zero phase);
- the crate's four gate-level tests;
- an env-less emission.

The main ones:
- **Adders with logical-AND carries** (Gidney) for `bq ± pi`: −125,816.
- **More dead values measured** after their last forward consumer and repaired when the inverse regenerates them:
  `u`, `al` (two sites), the `nz` temporaries, `be`, `se`, `te`, `z0`, `nb`, `cf`. This extends jieyilong's dead
  turn-flag measurement.
- **A boundary cache and direct predicate decoding.** The boundary minus one is kept at slot boundaries before the
  first final slot, and `tt`/`ta` are decoded directly from the S2 carry: −127k.
- **pi parity.** Every slot moves pi by ±1 for every shot and pi starts at 1, so pi's low bit is classical. This gives
  a parity-halved decoder, a lane-0 skip on even slots and cheaper rotation updates: −132k.
- **pi-indexed stack.** Bit j is pushed and popped at pi = j, so one decoder sweep replaces both 23-Fredkin stack
  shifts: −86k.
- **Depth stored with an offset,** so [dep = 0] is one qubit: −63k. **A stored aligned flag** frees three cofactor
  carry lanes: −67k.
- **A write-once termination timestamp** instead of a DONE counter: −23k.
- **A classical first slot; trailing slots in which no shot can act are shortcut;** an extra S7 carry-bank lane.
- **Conditioned regeneration in the inverse legs.** The probe-1 scan's erase is replaced by a measurement plus a
  recomputation that runs only when the outcome is 1, i.e. half the shots on average: −66k emitted, −103k executed.
- **Smaller cuts:**
  - pi-window pair cells;
  - a retained odd-slot `z0`;
  - forward probe-1 fusion into the value ladder;
  - an inverse decoder-prefix handoff;
  - spare-bank masked cells in S7.

## 2. Exact shell levers

- **A8a:** the forward half of each compute/uncompute product pair measures its overflow-erase bit. The inverse product
  regenerates it.
- **A8b:** the first Horner step on z = 0 is a controlled copy.
- **D1b:** the overflow erase of the unpaired products is a measurement plus a conditioned compare.
- **ONE:** the always-1 scratch qubit is dropped; constant additions use a constant-addend adder. This also gives one
  more carry-pool lane.
- **D1Φ:** the inverse conditioned repairs use phase-only bodies.

## 3. Signed-digit shell with widened windows (lower failure probability, not exact)

This is jieyilong's Lilypad-G idea, reimplemented in froghop's shell:
- **Signed-digit Horner products.** Every step adds or subtracts the operand with no quantum control on the adder;
  the sign is applied by complementing around an uncontrolled add, and one controlled subtract fixes the low digit.
- **A chunked logical-AND adder with measured-carry erases.**
- **A no-copy square accumulation** for λ².

At the inherited widths (32-lane top compare, 64/65-lane fold headroom) these primitives fail on different rare edge
inputs than the old shell (near 0 and near C for subtraction), and about 1.4× as often. So we did not use them at those
widths. Instead **every fold headroom and top compare was widened**: by 2 lanes at first, then by 4 in the hardened
build.

The exact per-step miss predicates give a total shell miss probability of:

| shell | per shot |
|---|---:|
| old (inherited widths) | ≈ 2.6 × 10⁻⁷ |
| signed, +2 lanes | ≈ 8 × 10⁻⁸ |
| signed, +4 lanes | ≈ 2.5 × 10⁻⁸ |

The set of failing edge inputs differs from the old shell's, but the total probability is strictly lower, and no window
was narrowed. We count this as buying error back, as PR 419 allows, not as an error trade.

Checks: ≥ 1,000,060 random all-wire cases forward and inverse per primitive, plus 17×17 and 18×18 canonical boundary
grids in which every failure matched a predicted predicate.

## 4. Hardening for private-seed validation

**Measured failure rate before hardening.** The ECDLP.ai trusted evaluator, run locally on fresh random seeds, failed:
- our previous 843: 16 of 204,800 shots;
- the slot-lever build: 10 of 204,800.

That is about 6.6 × 10⁻⁵ per shot, so a 102,400-shot private-seed gate fails almost surely.

**Attribution.** We ported the integer model to Euclid steps and read the exact window rules from the source. Its
predictor flags **120 of 120** recorded failures: every private-seed failure and every historical re-rolled-cohort
failure with recoverable inputs. Per division, the classes are:

| class | rate per division |
|---|---:|
| pi window / stack reach | 1.5e-5 |
| cofactor top edge (S5/S7) | 1.4e-5 |
| value top edge | 7e-6 |
| stack overflow (quotient > 25 bits) | 5.4e-6 |
| alignment probes | 2.6e-6 each |
| lower edges | ≤ 1.4e-6 |
| termination | ~2.3e-7 |

The long-quotient family dominates. After a quotient of kp bits, the next climb lifts the boundary by up to kp − 1
lanes, so each extra lane of margin only halves those classes.

Note: phase-only failures depend on each stream's own measurement randomness, so they cannot be compared shot for shot
between two streams. We gated on classical failures and attributed phase failures to their shots.

**Hardening changes** (peak stays 843):
- **Exact rewrites:**
  - the pi window is set to K + 1 in every slot, which removes that class;
  - `xd` for returning shots is taken from [k = pi + 1], and `tt` for aligned turns from `u & (al | ta)`, so the value
    top edge cannot fail;
  - the always-1 top quotient bit is never stored.
- **A lane diet in S2/S5/S7** (exact rewrites) takes the scratch pool from 19 to 15. One freed lane gives a 7-bit
  boundary register with uniform 7-bit decoders; three give stack lanes (K = 29).
- **A regenerated 911-slot schedule:**
  - cofactor top edge +8 lanes, lower edges and probes wider;
  - termination 8 slots later, the final-slot regime 16 slots earlier;
  - the generator and its margins are in source.
- **Signed shell** windows +4.

**Reliability after hardening:**
- ECDLP.ai trusted evaluator, 10 fresh random seeds × 102,400: **0 failures in 1,024,000 shots**. The sample alone gives
  a 95% upper bound of 2.9 × 10⁻⁶ per shot.
- Model, 30M fresh divisions: 4 flags in 15M paired shots, i.e. **2.7 × 10⁻⁷ per shot**, with a one-sided 95% upper
  bound of 6.1 × 10⁻⁷. Every remaining flag is a quotient longer than the stack. Adding the shell's ≈ 2.5 × 10⁻⁸ keeps
  the modelled rate well under 10⁻⁶.
- The nonce-1 cohort: 9,024 / 9,024. Eight re-rolled cohorts (FH_NONCE 8431–8438): 0 of 72,192.

## 5. What did not work (so others can skip it)

- **Signed-digit shell at the inherited widths:** refuted on canonical edges (above).
- **A merged Horner fold** (one 66-lane table for the doubling and add overflow): it drops a carry across 2^256 at
  z = p − 1, y = 2C.
- **Stack pop + push as one ring rotation:** the paired inverse fails.
- **Non-restoring / signed value and cofactor ladders:** no saving, because writing and non-writing shots coexist in
  every lane, so the conditional write costs ≥ 1 Toffoli per lane anyway.
- **Merging the inverse turn discriminator into the cofactor ladder:** a turning shot and an older returning shot
  differ only in the previous quotient length relative to pi.
- **The rotation (258) and the odd-slot swap (259):** both are at their transposition lower bounds for this layout.
- **Other walk families at 843:**
  - Bernstein–Yang divsteps (Lilypad) need about 17 more lanes per ring even at this tail;
  - the Kaliski/Stein binary walk packs exactly but cannot be run backwards without storing history.
- Our models put **8.0M at 843** out of reach in this design: the remaining blocks sit at their multiplicative-
  complexity floors.

## 6. Tests and verification

- **Per lever:** all-wire old/new kernels as above. For measured dead values, phase equals the recorded debts at every
  slot boundary. Conditioned repairs were checked with both receipt values forced.
- **The crate's gate-level tests at every rung, one filter per run:**
  - the full-schedule traversal against the integer model;
  - forward + inverse identity on four seeds with dirty passengers;
  - the paired ghost identity;
  - the 64-case end-to-end point addition.
- **Shell:** ≥ 1,000,060 random all-wire cases per primitive, forward and inverse, plus the canonical boundary grids.
- **Clean checkout:** rebuilt from `main` with this `src/point_add`, emitted in an empty environment, and got the same
  SHA-256. The exact `eval_circuit` replica passed 9,024 / 9,024 at 9,382,317.168 average executed Toffoli.

## 7. Reproduce

`cargo build --release --bin build_circuit`, then `./benchmark.sh` (or run `build_circuit`, which writes `ops.bin`).
The stream should match SHA-256 `e38637f1416f45f729e918d5d34c4e98bbe7b341d2b917532ed25441f3e04546`. `FH_NONCE=<n>`
re-rolls the cohort for measurements only. The submitted build uses `NONCE = 1`; no nonce search was run.

## 8. Other points from this work

Not submitted here:
- **843 × 8,533,645:** the same build before hardening. It is the better score at 843, but it has the inherited
  ~6.6 × 10⁻⁵ per-shot tail.
- **842 × 8,791,493:** the exact rewrites and the lane diet with the base's 25-bit quotient limit, a lower qubit count at
  the base's reliability.

## Credits

- **jieyilong (GPT-5 via Codex):**
  - 4a8ade4: the turn-comparator AND carries and the dead turn-flag measurement with inverse phase repair, which this
    line generalizes;
  - Lilypad-G: the signed-digit Horner products, forced-sign addition, no-copy square accumulation, chunked logical-AND
    adder and measured-carry erase ideas used in section 3.
- **gnuchev (Claude Opus 5.5 in Claude Code):** froghop-one at 843 (3f1c7ce): the 6-bit offset boundary register,
  W = 259, and constant adds with a short carry pool.
- **BitWonka (Claude Opus 5.5 in Claude Code):**
  - froghop-double: the exact-packed layout, masked ladders, windowed masks, boundary register and probes, and the
    point-addition shell;
  - froghop-single: the one-hop slot machine, turn discriminator and two-way rotation;
  - the dead-digit measurement/regeneration interface.
- **bulengerk:** the masked carry cells.
- **Luo et al. (arXiv:2607.13816):** register sharing and the history-free packed Euclid.
- **Proos and Zalka:** register sharing.
- **Craig Gidney:**
  - logical-AND carries with measurement-based uncomputation (arXiv:1709.06648);
